title_review: Not Adequately Seasoned - Seasoning layer gone after one batch of cornbread
text: This pan is a good piece of iron that is well balanced. However, the pre-seasoning is a joke. It is no where near adequate. I've attached a photo to show that what seems to have been a single layer of seasoning is gone after just one use. I baked one batch of cornbread in the pan with plenty of oil & butter. The cornbread stuck to the pan. I washed the pan with hot water (no soap) and used an OXO cast iron pan brush to remove the stuck on crumbs. I did not soak the pan. The seasoning is now gone. The pan will require a great deal of seasoning work before I can use it again. Don't expect to use it without going through the seasoning process. I have other well-seasoned pieces of cast iron cookware, so I'm not new to caring for this type of item.

title_review: Big, too big?  Hard to heat evenly
text:
5 stars for cast iron, and 5 stars for Lodge. Nevertheless, I found this "15 inch" skillet very difficult to cook with because it heats so unevenly.

This skillet is massive so it is a very large heat sink. I heat it on a 12.5" electric cooktop element. I have not seen too many elements (gas or electric) larger than this.

On high heat, the center of the pan expands substantially and the outside so much less that the pan deforms and the bottom cones. This exacerbates the uneven heating because as the pan deforms the edges lift off the cooktop and the pan teeters on the bulge in the center of the bottom, further heating the center and cooling the perimeter. Gas burners do not need flat bottoms so much but they are usually smaller in diameter than my 12.5" electric element and may also have trouble heating the perimeter.

Pancakes didn't work. Even though I cooked 9-10" diameter cakes, the perimeter of the pan works like a heat sink to draw heat away, leaving the center much hotter than even the circumferance of the pan bottom that is directly over the heating element.

French toast didn't work. The difference between the center and the edges was enough to burn the toast in the center and leave the pieces around the edges undercooked. Further cooking the edge pieces resulted in visible differences between the outside and inside edge of the piece (light to dark).

I thought I could overcome the size and mass of this thing by preheating it and working with awareness of the thermodynamic problems it presents, but I have not had practical success so far.

My reference pan is a well seasoned All Clad Cop-R-Chef 12" fry pan. The All Clad with its aluminum core heats very evenly. Cast iron is much better than stainless for fried eggs, and this spacious 15" pan would provide considerably more room for frying and could saute more without getting so crowded that the food gets steamed.

I want it to work out, but I might have to downsize to the 13 inch skillet because I don't see a practical way to heat a pan this large evenly.

title_review: Worst Cast Iron Skillet I ever Used!
text:
First of all, I am a Chef...I've worked in fine Restaurants all over the country...Started out in High School as the youngest Prep Chef/Sous Chef in Henris' History while a Senior in school and working part time in Chicago. I have owned (and still own) Henkel Knives, Custom jute and wax handle wrapped pans and even spatulas. I have owned many Cast Iron Pans and consider them to be the one of the most valued tool for any chef due to their sheer versatility and ease of use.

That said....I just lost my trusted old friend of 25 years....yeah my Cast Iron Skillet. I went to Amazon to find a WORTHY replacement. I found the Lodge Products and saw by the reviews, that this company was going to fit my needs perfectly.

How wrong I was!

I purchased the 10.5 inch cast iron skillet from Lodge. First notice after getting the skillet was the ROUGH, STIPPLED texture of the skillet. My other cast iron "champs" were SMOOTH like a teflon pan, and were easily SEASONED! This chunk of iron was rough and "pimpled" ...like I was as a teenager when I first worked as a line chef for Henrisis.!

Ok so I figured, "OK well, I'll just season the thing and all will be well in the Kitchen! NOT SO!

I started with my "tried-and-true" canola and sunflower oil @ 450f for an hour. OK. pan is still not seasoned. OK, do it again 4x and lets use GHEE (mp480f) this time. Still the surface looks my face when I was 13 years old....Yeah....full of bumps and no SMOOTH surface like with my last beloved cast iron wonder.

Conclusion, Yeah, these Lodge Folks do not know how to cast real fine cook ware. They need to figure out a way to create SMOOTH CASTED IRON COOKWARE. or just go away.

I will never buy another product from these PATZERS!

This skillet is the perfect size: big enough to cook two "kissing" over-medium eggs at the same time (or a generous omelette), yet small enough to fit on one of the small back burners I seldom use except to boil water. I can leave this skillet sitting on my stove, opposite my Lodge double grill/griddle, and cook up a bodacious amount of food without having to shuffle things around so much.

text: Diatomaceous earth consists of fossilized remains of diatoms, a type of hard-shelled algae. It is used as a mild abrasive in some polishing products including metal polishes and toothpaste, as a mechanical insecticide, which I plan to do, cat litter, an absorbent for liquids, an activator in blood clotting studies, a reinforcing filler in plastics and rubber, a stabilizing component of dynamite,  a thermal insulator and a filtration aid.  No, I'm not a chemist, but for the purpose I intend to use this Diatomaceous Earth, as a food grade product for my health and also to kill insects. It is good for both.  It  is a naturally occurring, soft, siliceous sedimentary rock that is easily crumbled into a fine white to off-white powder with an odd combination of uses, for us.  I'll dust areas inside my walls after drilling a hole and around the patio to negate the crawling insects that fly and swarm around. Termites and ants especially. The dusting will be done while wearing a mask for a filter, as breathing the dust is not good for you. It has a particle size ranging from less than 3 micrometers to more than 1 millimeter, but typically 10 to 200 micrometers, so getting it into your lungs it may do you some harm. After my inside wall dusting, I'll cover the hole with a little plastic cap for some neatness. I'll use a little in my food, and it will supply me with an additive for gastro health.  Although it was discovered in 1866, the fact that the extremely volatile explosive nitroglycerin, could be made much more stable if absorbed in diatomite by Alfred Nobel, thus Dynamite. It's uses are varied and it is still in use almost everywhere it is available.

title_review: Kept the hummingbird feeder from freezing
text: Well, I can't speak to this as a coffee mug warmer, but it worked great last winter suspended an inch or two below the hummingbird feeder.  It kept the nectar from freezing so that the birds could get calories on board as soon as it started getting light and they woke up from their nighttime torpor.  (Here in the Pacific Northwest, we have Anna's hummingbirds who stay all winter.)  (If you're going to try the same thing, just be sure it's a bit below the bottom of the feeder -- I'm sure it would melt the plastic, or at least heat it enough to release toxins into the nectar.  But being as heat rises, even an inch or two below was adequate in our climate where a really cold winter night is in the teens.)

title_review: MWBLK Mug Warmer from Mr. Coffee
text: Here is a product that I plan to use in combination with a motion sensor, Sensor Plug - Motion Activated Electrical Outlet, which I purchased on Amazon, earlier for about 12$.  So my coffee warmer plate will not be turned on and off manually, very much, except when I move to and from my computer desk.  The switch, on the mug warmer, is a slide on an off.  If anything I would expect a good lighted toggle switch. Other wise, it works, gets hot and the switch is why I don't give it a better star rating out of the gates.  I do recommend them updating this old style coffee warmer to a more modern concept of powering it up.  It is dated, but I will say, when you pick up your cup, the coffee is hot, but not scalding.  With my Temp. gage, it shows 140 degrees F.  The surface is 175.  I keep an air conditioner on, so it is about 78 at desk level and it draws 18 watts off the killa-watt meter when plugged in and on.  I like it well enough for four stars.

title_review: Looks to be slightly superior to its predecessor
text:
This is my 3rd OXO Good Grips Salad Spinner. It looks like they discontinued their large salad spinner with the rounded bottom. It is just as well as both of them developed cracks on the bottom of the outside bowl and we use the spinner to soak whatever green leaves we are prepping, putting them through several soaks and rinses, and then we spin out all remaining water. Sometimes we are so surprised at how much dirt we cleaned off the leaves, this includes every once in a while those 3-in-a-package Romain lettuce hearts. We even do this with fresh herbs, but not all herbs do well soaked. They are rinsed and done. We never put the previous OXO spinners through the dishwasher and there is a scald protection on our kitchen faucet, so we never ran it through water that was too hot when we washed it by hand. So as you can imagine, we weren't happy campers when the second one broke, too.

I wanted to find a different vendor, but the capacity had to be the same if not better and I had other specific requirements about functionality. Turns out that this OXO one fit the bill even though I was nervous about the new model still failing like its predecessor has. We needed it to be just as big. It's capacity seems to be just a tad more probably due to the removal of the curved bottom. We are quite happy about that. I have only used this new model twice. The lettuce leaves came out fresh and dry and when I did it for curly parsley, it performed just as well. If the veggies stay wet, they will spoil fast. If they stay dry, they can last a week in the fridge. In general, I'm happy to have a spinner back and I am happy this one has a little more capacity without taking up any additional space. We're just crossing our fingers that the bottom of the bowl won't crack like the preceding model did.

Lastly, I'm loving the see through top and this perk I did not expect since all previous salad spinners we owned had an opaque top. You can spin to your heart's content, hit the break, and sort of eyeball how things are going with removing the water. I found with the curly parsley, after the first spin, I could still see water (this is normal, but I'd lift the lid on the older model to see the water). With the older model, I would move the greens around because centripetal force pegs them against the walls and put the cover on and spin again. Repeat as necessary. The clear top saves time. I actually spun it, saw the water through the lists sifted it back and forth a little to get the greens to fall into the center (don't turn upside down because the water will go back onto the greens) and then I spun it again. I like the fact that I didn't have to touch the greens again and saved time by not having to remove and reset the lid.

title_review: LARGE LETTUCE LEAVES DID NOT DRY SUFFICIENTLY
text:
The spinner arrived overnight as a result of my Prime Membership. I used it for the first time tonight. It is a sturdy and beautiful piece of equipment and works as described. It held tightly to my counter. I was concerned that it might take up too much space, but the shape and option to flatten the lid assure that it does not. Moreover, it will probably remain mostly in my refrigerator to encourage me to eat more salads.
I did reduce my rating by one star, however, as it did not quite measure up to my high expectations given the "rave" reviews. It was definitely sturdier and easier to use than my Zyliss salad spinner. Yet, it did not spin nearly as fast as the corded Zyliss. My first use was with large, slightly cupped red/green lettuce leaves. While I spun them a half dozen times, they were never really dry! I did try putting a small amount of leaves in the spinner with little improvement. I finished drying them with a clean tea towel.
Perhaps this trial was misleading. It may well be that these leaves were too large to shed the water sufficiently. Were I making a salad immediately, it would perhaps be better to cut the leaves so that the water drained more completely.
Be assured that I do not regret making this purchase. I am reasonably certain that it will not only be easier to use but will also function better long-term. I replaced my Zyliss because I the basket got easily "warped" and the cord had to be frequently re-wound.

ADDENDUM
After many more tries, this spinner work did not do the job as well as my tea towel wrapping. In fact, I still had to dry the lettuce on towels after using the spinner! Perhaps it was a defect as my opinion is countered by hundreds of rave reviews and the consensus that it is the # 1 spinner. I emailed the manufacturer and had no problem returning it via Amazon, I will now plan to order from Amazon what some analysts conclude to be the # 2 spinner.

text: If you have hard wood and tile floors, if you have pets and issues with hair, food crumbs, and tracked litter, if you need something for frequent and easy clean up, this vacuum is just about perfect.  But it won't do everything.  So if you're looking for one machine to do everything, this is not the one.  It will not deep clean carpeting, but does pick up surface lint and crumbs from carpet and throw rugs.  Pros:  Very light weight.  Strong suction.  Good design of floor brush allows it to fit in tight places and up against base boards.  Inexpensive.  Cons:  Can't be used on carpet.  Short Cord (I added an extension cord which stays on permanently) and the handle is a bit short.  I am 5'7" and it works for me but a taller person may find it too short.  The best thing about this is the price.  Under $20.  When it wears out, I can replace it and I'd buy the same thing.  Prior to this purchase I bought a cordless stick vacuum which fell apart in 6 months and cost over $100.  The suction on the Dirt Devil is stronger so I am well satisfied with my purchase.

title_review: Shark is the only vacuum I will buy
text:
I have owned a lot of different brand vacuum cleaners, Shark is definitely one of my top favorites. The suctioning power lasts with this brand. The key is to clean your filters regularly. Especially if you live where you get a lot of dust in your home or if you have pets. We have two German Shepherds . My boys shed like a winter snowstorm all year round. We are very pleased with how well this picks up the hair.
I wasn’t expecting this vacuum to be smaller than the standard vacuum cleaner, and was considering returning it for the standard size. However it works so well that it didn’t make a difference. Actually I’m glad it’s smaller now since it makes cleaning the stairs easier. It seems to have a little bit better suction than the larger vacuum. I would have rated this a five except there is one thing that I don’t care for. When you use the hose attachment the vacuum cleaner tends to fall over very easily when using the tools. So I end up having to hold the vacuum steady with one hand while using the wand with the other. My other shark did the same thing. That’s my only complaint. Otherwise I a loyal customer to this brand. I also own the shark floor vacuum for downstairs and couldn’t be happier with it as well.
On a side note: My last Shark vacuum I had almost 5 years. The suctioning power was still very good till the end. The only reason we had to purchase another vacuum is because the canister lid broke by our own doing and could not be replaced due to the company no longer carrying it.

text:
I've had this vacuum for 3 months, and got it off of QVC with more attachments than on here, but I never use the microfiber mop anyway. I'll put brackets around reviews for the attachments that don't apply to this amazon package but for someone who was wondering about the extra pieces (which you can see here on the QVC website [...]

This vacuum sucks a lot of stuff out of our carpet. With a dog and two cats we have a lot of pet hair around, and every time I'm done vacuuming the canister is full of dirt and hair.

The cord isn't a long or short length. I use a vacuum extension cord anyway, but if I don't then I need to change the outlet once or twice while vacuuming my main floor.

[I use the bare floor attachment for my kitchen. It works okay, but when you run it parallel to the wall, it won't get any dirt or crumbs against the baseboard. Instead, you have run it at a perpendicular angle, so that's a little annoying since I have to often run over the same floor twice in two different directions just to make sure I get all the dirt/crumbs around the edges, and it forces you to slowly make your way down the wall a foot at a time, only as wide as the nozzle. It's irksome to say the least. I think I'll just start sweeping before I vacuum, which is pretty annoying.]

[I haven't used the dry dust mop attachment (microfiber pad) because I haven't had any real use for it when I have the bare floor attachment. The kitchen is high-traffic area and for the amount of crumbs from food and dog food that land on the floor, I'd rather use the bare floor piece rather than the dust mop. If I had a wood floor without as much traffic I might use it, but the rest of my house is carpeted!]

The regular "motorized floor brush nozzle" works well. I have to cut out the hair from the spinning brushes every few uses--it's amazing how much of my own long hair ends up on the carpet (gross, I know). I don't think it gets the edges of my carpet very well either, but I didn't seriously expect it to.

I wish the turbo brush could have somehow been motorized, but it wasn't with my last vacuum either so I didn't really expect it to be. I use it on my carpeted stairs, and it works ok but could definitely work better and more efficiently if it was motorized.

The vacuum is very tippy, [especially with the bare floor attachment. It almost can't stand up on its own with that attachment], so I always lean it up against a wall anytime I need to stop vacuuming (that goes for both floor attachments I use, [but the bare floor one hardly stands up at all without tipping over).]

My biggest issue with this vacuum is the "stretch hose." On the vacuum itself, it is 22" long. When fully extended, it's as long as 65". They want you to detach the floor attachment and use just the handle with stretch hose (with other attachments), OR you can detach the extension wand and use it with a floor attachment (like the dust mop piece in the pictures on QVC, turning the vacuum into a canister vacuum rather than upright).

However, the resistance of the hose is so strong that you can't extend the hose without holding on to the vacuum itself or else the vacuum gets dragged along with you (or tips over at the very least). If I wanted to use the vacuum as a canister vacuum rather than an upright, it'd be nearly impossible to do so since you can't tow the canister along with you. I have the biggest problem while using it on the stairs. I wish I could leave it at the top or the bottom of the stairs and use the handle with the turbo brush, but I can't go more than one step without the vacuum falling over because the resistance is so strong on the hose once you stretch it in the slightest. Instead, I detach the canister from the floor piece and extension wand, and just try to hold it in one hand while using the nozzle handle in my other hand. It's a big pain that I wasn't prepared for with this vacuum.

Overall, I don't think I'd recommend this vacuum just because of the inconveniences I have with it. I'm not very excited that I know I'll be stuck with this vacuum for a least a few years before I can try something else. All of the attachments make you excited about it, but I don't think they make up for the cons. The high ratings really made me think it'd be fantastic, but unfortunately I just don't think it's all that it's worked up to be.

11/7/2012 Edited to Add: I forgot to mention that this thing is a pain to empty. The bin holds very little until it is at is "max full." But if you have any sort of pet hair then it gets all clumped up in the top of the bin instead of the bottom. The bin is shaped so that all the hair/dust/dirt gets caught way up inside it and you have to reach your fingers up to pull it all out. I can't imagine this being possible for anyone with bigger fingers than I have, and my hands are fairly small. Another reason I'm very disappointed with this vacuum. Cannister vacuums are supposed to be easy to empty--just tip the bin upside-down and everything pours out. This vacuum is the opposite of that scenario.

text:
I love this vacuum. It isn't nearly as loud as most others, has excellent suction, is easy to empty and to clean, has great attachments and features, and has a HEPA filter, which is a must for allergy sufferers like me. I was surprised how much it picked up on a first pass on my "clean" rugs and carpet. This brand also seems to have better quality control on their products than some of the other leading brands, which is one reason why I chose it.

PROS:
- HEPA filtered
- Not super loud
- Excellent suction. It practically pulls itself across my berber carpet and I have to hold my settee in place while using the upholstery attachment on the hose, or else the vacuum's suction will pull it across the floor.
- Push-button dust cup dump
- Easy to clean filters (pretty cheap and easy to replace as well!)
- Suction adjustment near the handle (for small or lightweight rugs that like to move)
- Everything (hose, dust cup, vacuum head, etc.) snaps back into place and has a release clip. No wedging parts together and hoping for the best
- Enough cord length for small/medium sized rooms
- Gets under furniture more easily than bulky models and is easy to maneuver
- Vacuum head detaches so it's easy to use the hose on stairs, curtains, etc. I've even used it while standing on a step stool, sanding wall putty
- You can see the brush through a window in the vacuum head, so it's easy to monitor if it gets hair around it. There is also a safety feature that the brush will turn off if it is meeting too much resistance, which saves the belt from burning out. You can hear when this happens, but there is also a light on the vacuum head that turns from green to red. I've only had this happen on my hard-to-vacuum super thick pile rug, but I'd much rather adjust the way I'm vacuuming than have to replace the belt
- Brush in vacuum head is operated on the on/off button. You can run the vacuum without running the brush. As a safety feature, the brush will not turn on unless the vacuum is tilted
- Works great on my hard wood and tile floors and picks up just about everything it comes across

CONS:
- Unit is a little top-heavy. It stands up fine on hard flooring and low-pile carpet, but may try to tip over on thick rugs/carpeting. (This is the only con I'd say is actually significant)
- Cord may not be long enough for large rooms
- Kind of tall and not as lightweight as I might prefer, but still easy to carry upstairs
- Hose could be a foot longer
- Since the cord winds onto the hose, you'll need the cord completely unraveled to use the hose

title_review: 11 furry pets and this vacuum gets ALL the hair easily!
text:
Amazing product, used but worked perfectly out of the box. Didn't come with assembly instructions but it was extremely easy to see which hose clicked in where and I had it together in two minutes. Started using it right away since our last vacuum has been broken and our floor was, well, gross! I've been looking for a great vacuum that can get up pet hair. I don't mean like 1 or 2 dogs or 3 cats type of pet hair, I mean 4 dogs, two chinchillas (yea they shed), two lionhead bunnies, two guinea pigs, and a cat. Plus stray hay pieces that get tracked through the house from the rodent cages. I bought a brand new vacuum that said it was specifically designed for pet hair but under a minute of vacuuming it just completely broke. I've been using a bagless that I'd have to stop every minute (almost literally) and dump it or it would be clogged and would take 10+ minutes to clean. It was getting tiresome. I saw this vacuum on a site reviewing the best vacuums for pet hair and this was #2 (under a $400 Dyson vacuum!). So this won because of the amazing price here on amazon (under $200 which included shipping right to my door!) and the amazing reviews.

Granted, when I pulled it out of the box and assembled it I was having worries it was too small to be powerful enough to handle my home, but I was super wrong! As soon as I turned it on I could feel it grab onto the carpet and start sucking everything up! Now, I DID have to stop every 3-5 minutes to dump it but that is because my house has so many furry animals and hadn't been vacuumed in longer than I will mention here. O_o Overall with going back to my daily vacuuming routine I am certain I can get the whole house with only 1 dump of the cannister. Man, this vacuum seriously vacuumed everything: tile, chinchilla and guinea pig poop, hay, animal hair and the normal dust and dirt a home collects. It is amazing, light, maneuverable and if you have a difficult amount of pet hair in your home it is perfect! I recommend this whole heartedly!

title_review: Some Good Elements, a Few Negatives
text:
I've use the Shark Navigator Pro for about 10 days now. I was expecting to be really impressed based on the infomercial and the reviews. Instead, I find it adequate, but not impressive in any way. I bought it mainly for two features: it's bagless, and for the lift-away canister because I'm moving to a house with 2 sets of carpeted stairs. I do appreciate the bagless feature, but the stairs have been more frustrating than not. Here are the pros and cons:

Pros:
- It navigates well around furniture due to the swivel head
- The canister removes from the base for reaching things higher up or doing stairs (not always well, see below)
- Suction is good. Compared to my Hoover Widepath, which has excellent suction, it's about as good. I'm hopeful it will keep good suction over time.
- It's lower profile in front than my Hoover, so it goes further underneath furniture.
- The cord is nice and long so I can do even my larger rooms without unplugging and replugging.
- It's pretty quiet. The brush-on (for carpet) switch makes it do a whining sound, but I think it's still quieter than my other vacuum. And the bare-floor setting is rather quiet for a vacuum.
- Switching from carpet to bare floors is so easy! I love going from my living room carpet right onto my wood floor entry with just the flip of a switch. It vacuums very well on wood floors.
- The dust cup capacity is good. I've vacuumed 5 rooms and stairs and only emptied it once.

Cons:
- The number of latches and releases is too many and they all look alike. It's confusing figuring out which one you need for which thing.
- The latch to release the extension wand won't work if the cord is wrapped around the cord holders or in the cord clip. You might spend 5 minutes the first time trying to release it before you realize this is the issue.
- It's heavy!!! The canister is located up higher near the handle (so it can be released from the base) so when you vacuum, more of the weight is carried by your shoulder and elbow instead of it sitting on the base. After only a few passes with this thing, my elbow becomes sore and I have to keep switching hands. (I'm young and in great shape, so I can't imagine an older person trying to use this vacuum.)
- There is no good stair tool!! The main reason I bought this was for doing the stairs more easily than a regular vacuum (which I have to hold between my legs so it doesn't tumble down while I vacuum). The Shark comes with a crevice tool (not good for stairs), a brush tool which is not good because the air all leaks out between the bristles, reducing suction dramatically, and the pet hair tool, which has velvety strips to grab pet hair off couches and such, but doesn't work well on med-long carpet piles. What it needs is a wide, brush-less tool, but it doesn't come with one. I may try to scour a vacuum supply store for an accessory like that that will fit. It's nearly useless without such a tool.
- If the lack of a good stair tool wasn't bad enough, the canister's super short hose and top-heavy design causes the canister to topple over all the time while doing stairs. I've tried using the extension wand, but it creates an awkward angle whereby you can't do more than one stair at a time without moving the canister and it still tips pretty often. I bashed myself in the head a couple of times. :( The stair element of this vacuum definitely needs rethinking. A longer hose and a good stair tool would help a ton.
- It has a shorter width than my Hoover Widepath (and most other vacuums, judging from the reviews) so it means more vacuuming. It's not a huge deal for me, but my husband hates that about it.

Overall, I'm on the fence about keeping it. It's not a bad vacuum. And if you currently have a vacuum with bad suction or if you don't intend to use it for stairs much, it's a good vacuum to purchase. But if you bought it for the canister-to-stair feature, you're going to be very disappointed. It may not be worth the money. Personally, I'm just so sick of buying vacuum bags all the time I'll probably keep it.

text: I never thought I would 'love' a vacuum, it is just one of those tools you need to have but seldom give it much thought.  I purchased a wide range of different vacuum brands from high dollar Hoovers to low end Bissels, and each of them fell far short of the job they were supposed to do, and most of them simply fell apart after a very short period of time.  In total desperation I purchased a Shark Navigator, it was about the only brand left untried.  I did not have much hope, it was so very light weight, but at least it appeared that the wheels might stay on and that would be an improvement over the others!  When I got it home and gave it a try I was totally amazed that such a light weight vacuum could do the job that this vacuum did.  It has a wonderful pivot point at the head which allows you to turn the body of the machine away from counters and furniture while still setting the head close to the cleaning edge.  The head itself is very flat which allows you to get under odd pieces of furniture that previously were out of range for other vacuums, and because the body is capable of going almost flat to the ground you can easily get under coffee tables and chairs without hitting the furniture.  This vacuum seems to hit all the critical needs, and is well thought out in design. The accessories included the basic brush and also the pointed/angled nozzel attachment for corner cleaning.  If I were to mark it down, it would be for only one thing - when you disconnet the upper portion to use the hose/brush, it tends to take the machine a bit off balance and it will tip if you are not careful.  Otherwise, I think this vacuum is one of the best I have used, it is easy to clean and for the price, well worth it..so worth it that I purchased a second one for upstairs!

title_review: Not ideal if you have pets and not a good fit for our household
text: I really wanted to like this product. We have pets and I needed a vacuum that can handle the volume of cat hair on the carpet and is easy to use. It is light and self propels on carpet which makes it wonderful to use. it also picks up the cat hair on the carpet easily due to its powerful engine and suction. Best part is you can keep it clean very easily but just rinsing the actual canister. The turbo brush was great on furniture and the cat tree for 3 uses and than died on me. I cleaned it out and put it back together multiple times and it will not work again :( Shame. Another downside: it tips way too easily. It is great that is light especially since we have 2 flight of stairs in our house but the hose is not very flexible and pulling on it tends to tip the whole unit. Not pleasant if it falls on you and annoying since it does it every time. Also the extension rode is not very long. I am the kind of person that likes to clean under furniture. This is not the unit to do it with. The hose on my old Kenmore fit wonderfully under furniture. This one only allows for a certain angle and than the floor unit lifts off :(. I was hoping reading all the pros and cons. Alot of the cons mentioned in feedbacks are on the nose so please weigh them carefully before you purchase the unit. It is a great vacuum if you DO NOT have pets and easy cleanable environment such as an apartment.

text:
Our FOURTH Lasko Wind Curve fan arrived today. I ordered three of them a few summers ago. My son managed to render his non-functional after a year or so. My daughter's died a quiet death (no fan) this past week.

Looking online, I don't see how to repair these fans. I gather they're supposed to be "disposable" -- kind of expensive to throw one away after several years of use. Maybe my expectations are askew.

Anyway, it's the best household type fan I've found. Takes up very little space, it's very quiet and it's fairly strong. Just don't expect them to last forever. Especially if they're in your kid's rooms... beats anything you can find at the local hardware store. Highly recommended!!!

text:
I bought the Lasko Portable Electric 42" Oscillating Tower Fan with Fresh Air Ionizer in the in the Blackwood T42950, for my 21yr old son's room.
The reason I chose to look for a tower fan was it doesn’t take up much floor space, it is taller and off the floor and circulates the cool air better.
The number one reason I bought this model was for its IONIZER! It neutralizes ODORS!!!
I did say I bought this for my 21yr old sons room right! Lol… seriously that is the only reason I bought it!
A Con for me-
I DO NOT care for the colors at all. It is 42” tower of a whole lot of BLACK with a faux wood front which would be beautiful in the right home that has a decor that can compliment its heavy modern look. I prefer a lighter colors that disappear 🫥 or isn’t the first thing you notice when you walk in the room.

AFTER Some mental internal debate with myself this is why I bought it-
It is for my sons room so it will go well with his particular interior design style of Post Apocalyptic. It will look great with his unfolded tossed about laundry and whatever else! Most importantly hopefully it will SMELL BETTER.
Oh I almost forgot It has a Timer and Remote Control which is a plus as well.

PRO- it is so bloody quite even on high!! I had to check if it was on at the low setting ! Love that! Now he can’t say he couldn’t hear me because the fan is too loud!! Extra Pro he can’t use that as his defense… lol 😂

I have a light silver tower Lasko tower fan that I bought for my garage. I love that one but it’s loud. I love the light silver color because it’s not over bearing in color.
I hope they come out with a light color one I would buy it for my bedroom to help with menopause hot flashes and the Ionizer will help with my husbands night long expelling of the gas from his bowels… ugh 😩

Seriously great fan super quite and builds well!
I gave 4 stars ⭐️ because of the color options if they has another one in a light color it would have given it 6 stars ⭐️!

title_review: Too heavy/fragile, no handle, why the lid?
text: I do like this cup because it made a beautiful Mother's Day gift. However, I also bought one for myself, and as a product that I would use, I'm not as much of a fan. First off, there's no handle, so you have to wait until your beverage has cooled off significantly before you even think of transferring the cup. Second, it is *heavy* porcelain, so you must make sure there is no wetness on your hands or the cup, or it's going to slip right out of your hands and break. It also comes with a lid that is just as heavy and fragile, and I'm not quite sure what the lid is for. Is it to keep steam from escaping? I just don't use it. What I do love about this cup is the generous tea strainer. It's huge! I will definitely be using that for my other mugs. As for this mug, I'm not a huge fan. Also, I was a little annoyed with the seller because I had ordered the mug and the tea as a gift for the aforementioned Mother's Day, and they both came on separate days, despite my selecting the free Two-Day shipping. I reported it to Amazon, and they were apologetic (which I appreciate), but I was still annoyed that a gift arrived to the recipient in two parts!

title_review: Great Waffle Maker for the Price
text: This waffle maker is a great value for the money.  The instruction booklet contains a few recipes and I used their recipe for a batch of basic waffles.  They turned out great in this maker.  I set it right in the middle between light and dark and let each waffle cook for 6 minutes.  They were crispy dark on the outside and completely cooked and light and fluffy on the inside.  That recipe freezes well too.  I've already pulled one that I froze out of the freezer and nuked it for a few seconds and while not as crispy (should probably warm them in the toaster or oven) it was still very good as a snack.  I did clean it by following the directions and also applied a layer of cooking oil before using it the first time as the directions said to and wiped it down when I was finished.  No problems with sticking at all.  I'm very pleased with this waffle maker.

text: For years I have been looking for a cordless vacuum that actually worked, had a powerful suction and the charge didn't die after a couple of minutes. After trying (and wasting money on) a number of different vacuums by other brands, I have finally found the best ever! This Shark Navigator is the best of the best when it comes to a cordless vac. It sucks up just about anything, even small rocks! I can do over 650 square feet one one charge without ever a drop in power/suction. It moves easily from hard wood floor to carpet. The swivel head gets around corners, in tight spots and snug around furniture legs. The body can drop nearly flat to get under beds, sofas and other low furniture. And the best part?....no stupid cord to wrap up, or to pull out of the power socket by accident while vacuuming, or to get tangled up on stuff or knock stuff over while vacuuming through the house! Best purchase I ever made!

title_review: No stick to get carpeted corners clean, especially dog hair
text: This is an good vacuum cleaner. Pet hair has no place to hide...EXCEPT IN CARPETED CORNERS.. This is where the problem starts. I bought this for our 5th wheel camper, the house for our us humans and our 2 yr old Chocolate Lab who leaks hair, We do not have the option to bring it home, vacuum / clean it, then take it back.  So three stars because it does not have an onboard “stick” to clean corners. I need to wet a cloth, swipe all corners, pick up the hair, dust, etc, then vacuum. I held on to this for 6 weeks, but it’s going back...as soon as I figure out who to call. Too many requests for info, and after completing all these form fields, guess what? The customer service wants to know the same info. On this particular order, I cannot find the button that says “ return item” nor does it state how long you have until you return your purchase. What’s up with that??? Oh my oh my Amazon...

title_review: For the price, they are perfect for food storage
text:
I read the other reviews and I'm a little concerned that mine are different than the ones other customers received. I just microwaved homemade soup in one of the larger containers and got no warping at all. So as am experiment, I put hot water into two of the smaller ones, stuck them in the microwave and again no warping. Keep in mind that I don't have a huge, high power microwave, just a counter top unit. That may make a difference in whether the heat builds up to warp the plastic or not. For now, I'm very satisfied with these. As soon as they arrived, I washed them and started storing food in them.

And now that I've had them for a month or more, I can tell you that the only way to get the containers to warp is to forget to vent the lid. If microwave with the lid on, which is not the way to use these, then you need to make sure there is ample space for the container to vent, otherwise, it will warp. I learned that when a friend, who ordered these, forgot and tossed one in the microwave without venting.

title_review: Almost as powerful as my Ninja, easy to use & clean. Works fine with frozen ingredients
text:
My friend gifted me this unit a few weeks ago as her self inspiration on her own health kick for the new year - her theory being that if we both had a new smoothie machine, then she would eat better because she would company (Me!). So...I now have a NutriBullet Magic Bullet 12 piece system to use alongside my Ninja Auto IQ Blend machine. I've actually had some fun comparing the two machines and texting photos of each morning's smoothie choices to my friend and laughing at her selfie photos with expressions of horror and disgust back. The system is working though - she's eating/drinking fruit & veggies and her blood sugar levels have dropped a bit & she's lost a couple of pounds.

So far this Magic Bullet has proven to be almost as powerful as the Ninja - it technically has less horsepower than my Ninja, but it's handling the frozen fruits without any trouble. The Bullet is just as loud as the Ninja and I find that equally obnoxious, but it's only running for about 90 seconds at a time, so not a deal breaker. I do like that the Bullet takes up less counter space than the Ninja and the smaller footprint means it's easier to store in the cabinet as well. The cups etc are all holding up fine in the dishwasher top rack - sorry, but I do not have time to hand wash anything around here. Kitchen things in this house need to be wash and wear with the exception of my Great Grandmother's fine china, crystal and silver. Anything else that cannot go in the dishwasher goes in the garage sale.

The photos show a typical mix before, during and after being blended into a smoothie with the NutriBullet. It's a cup of fresh frozen fruit - strawberries, blackberries, cherries, and blueberries - a half cup of spinach, and 3/4 cup of blended yogurt and whole milk. (No added sugar or sweetener and no added powders of any kind.) I haven't experienced any leaks and the lids are easy to attach and remove, but you do need some elbow grease or one of those little rubber pad things to help get a grip on it if you don't have a lot of hand strength. This is equally as good as the Ninja - the Ninja does have the simplicity of the one button pre-programmed settings so you can just push the button and walk away and it shuts itself off. title_review: Love this machine! In a category of its own!
text:
I was debating whether or not to get this after watching an infomercial. Yes, I was sure it is a good thing, but how does it compare to the Ninja? I couldn't decide so I got this and the Ninja Pulse and they don't even compare! I am so glad I bought the NB and tried it for myself.

After 20+ years of juicing and always wondering what to do with the pulp (sometimes I would eat it, bake with it, or throw out the stronger tasting pulp), I really like the idea of consuming the whole vegetable the way you can with the NB. I made my first smoothie with celery, spinach, mushrooms, ginger, and 1/2 apple. When I took a sip, I actually said, "WOW, this is good!" It did liquify everything and it really did taste creamy. That concoction remains one of my favorite mixes, but I also love beats, beat tops, pineapple, or pretty much any fruit. I love that you can throw anything into this, especially leafy greens which give you almost no juice in a juicer.

Since I bought this a month ago, I have used it almost every day and find it so unbelievably easy to use. With a juicer, it was always a big ordeal - clean a lot of veggies, juice, clean up - clean up was the most time consuming step. Now I clean a fraction of the veggies because you use all of them instead of just extracting juice, and clean up is so simple. From cleaning veggies to clean up being complete, I can really be done in 4 minutes. This is a primary reason I use it so often.

Yes, I did have a leak issue too, but that's because I didn't tighten it enough. I learned my lesson!

In summary, what do I love most about this?
Drinks taste great!
Easy to use and clean - 2 simple parts to clean which make the whole process quick and easy.
Perfect size - 1 smoothie gives me a good amount of veggies and fruit
Perfect for on the go - I make a smoothie in the morning and bring it to work with me.
I feel healthier because I know I am doing good for my body.

How does it compare to the Ninja anyway? The Ninja is more like a traditional blender. It does puree things, but it doesn't pulverize like the NB. It is great for other things such as soups, which I happen to be obsessed with making since I got the Ninja. The taste is different - the same ingredients I put into the NB will not taste as creamy or be as liquified in the Ninja. The Ninja has only a few parts too, but I find the NB easier to clean.

Price - I bought mine at Kohl's just in case I want to return it locally. It was on sale for $100 and I had a 25% off coupon. For $75, it was totally worth a shot and after trying, I am confident in saying it's worth the full price if you cannot find a deal like I did.

I hope this helps with your decision!

text: At some point the gasket will fail. The container is both upside down and has no way to relieve pressure buildup. When this happens, you will not immediately know that a disaster has occured because the gasket joint is carefully designed to be hidden by the rim of the base. You will know when your smoothie ozzes out of the base unit. Knowing this will happen, the mfg punched a drain hole to make sure no fluid is visible until it is too late. An inverted cup could have been put on the drive shaft to deflect fluid away. But no, the leak will go right down the armature & bearings. Oh, the microswitches will also gum up. To make sure the unit can't be fully tightened, the outside surface has no ridges. I'm an engineer; this is an "F"

text:
I wish I would have read the reviews that indicated that you can buy this product at BB&B or Target for much less than Amazon and the infomercial. That said, I bought this product from the infomercial (which I hated, by the way).
I love this little machine. Anyone who has a juicer, complains about how tiresome and bothersome it is to clean. Not the Nutri-bullet.
I am delighted with this purchase. I have used it every day for over a week now and have not had any problems with leaking. Just read the directions and follow them. I make a nutri blast every morning and take it to work in the cups that are provided. I drink it for lunch along with a salad or some steamed veggies. I find that the drinks are very filling and delicious.
The Nutri bullet actually does what it says. It emulsifies the fruit, veggies and water into a delicious, nutritious drink. The clean up is a breeze - a little warm soapy water and that's it.
One of my co workers has a juicer and he was surpised to hear that I can use a banana in my bullet. His state of the art Jack LaLane won't do bananas.
So, if you are looking to improve your nutrition and have a machine that is easy to use and clean......buy it. You won't be sorry.
I'm looking forward to experimenting with more veggies and fruits!
It's 10 days later now and I have experienced leakage but I take responsibility for that as I do believe I over filled the cup. HOWEVER, in looking thru the recipe booklet, most of the recipes are fruit and a green - there is a paucity of recipes for actual veggies. I am wondering if it's because veggies don't emulsify as easy as fruit. I'm going grocery shopping today and plan to experiment with veggies. I'll keep you posted.
Also, I'd like to hear from someone who has used this product for more than 6 months. It doesn't seem to stand up to time.

title_review: So much easier, and better than a juicer IMO :)
text:
I just purchased my Nutribullet at Walmart for $99, along with a two-year replacement warranty (in case I have a problem. I never used my juicer much -- too messy and way too much waste unless you love to cook and can use the pulp elsewhere! I also compared the Nutribullet w/the Ninja, which cost about $20 less. I made my choice based on advice of the customer service manager at the store's return desk.

I habitually ask the return folks which brand(s) are returned most often, and the reasons for the returns when making my more costly purchases. The manager, who now knows me, told me the Ninja motor burns out quickly. He wasn't familiar with the Nutribullet, which is either a good sign, or means the product is new to Walmart (I neglected to ask).

Either way, learning about the Ninja problem swayed me toward the Nutribullet. It came with everything on the infomercial with the exception of the book: "The Healthy Green Diet," which can be purchased from Amazon for about $10. I used my Nutribullet for the first time this morning, and was pleased to find such a nutritious breakfast drink both easy to make, and easy to clean up afterwards. We're speaking of about five or so minutes.

That said, thanks to suggestions of other posters, I'll use frozen fruit and spinach next time to ensure the beverages are cold. I'll also save money by purchasing the non-organic fruits wholesale. The Nutribullet comes with a buying guide on which fruits and greens should be organic, and where the extra expense isn't necessary.

Thanks to all posters for your great input. You convinced me to try the Nutribullet. I hope others deciding whether or not to buy this product will find my comments helpful. Since I'm new to the product, I'll update this review if it doesn't wear well, or if I run into problems to note :)

title_review: Brown flakes pollute the mix (scary!).  Leaking (worsened over time).  I returned mine.
text:
A real rollercoaster ride here... because while Nutribullet excels on concept and marketing - I found it failed on execution (for me, at least).

An amazingly convenient way to prepare nutritious, tasty smoothies! I blended...
* veggies (fresh baby spinach, or frozen kale, celery, red pepper),
* fruit (apple, pear, fresh pineapple, kiwi, banana, sweetened dried cranberries)
* liquids (skim milk, kefir, yogurt)
* sweetener (stevia)
.... adding vegetables effortlessly to the diet... without processed sugars and salts... in a nutritious, frothy blend.

But joy turned to disappointment:

CHRONIC, WORSENING LEAKS
(Even if just partially filled)

Several design flaws induce chronic, small leaks:
1. Canister opens from the bottom.
2. Tightly screwing it closed, still doesn't seal it water-tight.
3. You rotate the canister contrary to the rotation of the seal to mount/dismount from the motor base.
4. The motor vibrates the seal at high speed, shaking it slightly open no matter how tightly you close it.
5. When contents drip into the locking mechanism, that food sits there for the life of the product because the locking mechanism can't be opened for cleaning by the consumer.

I've seen some fans of the product "blame the victim" for leaks... and I'll agree with them on one point: you dare not overfill (I made that mistake once myself - disaster). If their units are better specimens off the assembly line and never leak, I'm glad, but in my own trial, NutriBullet leaked a few drops into the base about 20% of the time despite my careful use and tight attempts to seal it (with real "guy hands," no less).
-

MYSTERIOUS BROWN FLAKES GET ADDED TO EACH SMOOTHIE you will be drinking
("Deal-Killer")

One reviewer spoke of finding brown powder in the blade mechanism, thinking it was chocolate, but discovered it was apparently lubricant from the blade mechanism. I also found the same brown residue and thought I hadn't cleaned properly (had made a cocoa blend - actually a pretty delicious mix). So I did some googling and found a customer service blog where others discuss this leaking lubricant, even when they do a sample blend with just water. (Search for: "A NutriBullet Customer Service Update: NutriBullet Blog.")

I tried their test: add pure water to the canister. Examine it first, to confirm absolute clarity. Then blend for half a minute: and find fine grit and small brown flakes in the water. (If this were a smoothie: you'd be drinking that down, with your smoothie.)

I thought, okay, handwashed canister, thought it was properly cleaned, blender's been used only a dozen times: let's rinse and repeat. Same results.

This is getting interesting. Now let's rinse, wipe out carefully with a towel, and rinse again, and repeat. Same results.

And a fourth time. Same brown residue and flakes mysteriously show up in the water. Same results.

Inert, safe brown flakes? I hope so.

But I won't be a lab rat, personally.

Back it went, for full credit.

text:
I purchased this drying rack just over 2 years ago and it has slowly become more and more broken and now I am shopping for a new drying rack, trying to decide if it’s easier to just replace it with another cheap one and repeat the cycle or buy a pricier one (of course, I could have bought the pricier one the first time for what I’ll pay anyway now).

What’s happened is the bars of the rack pop off one by one. You have to then line them up while holding up/together the rest of the rack since it will not stand upright until it’s put back together while you put them back in, and since they are held in by tension it usually takes several tries and often multiple additional bars pop off. Each time you line up one bar to fix it back into place more pop out.

To avoid this rack is now held together almost entirely by duct tape and so it cannot be collapsed to be put away.

It stopped working properly after about a year and has had to be duct taped together for ages now— and I don’t really have the space to keep it out all the time, it wasn’t attractive to start with and is super ugly now that it’s taped together... and I’d like a folding laundry rack that will actually fold up without breaking into pieces.

My suggestion is to spend a bit more since you will have to replace this brand every few years at the most.

At first I was trying to figure if I had gotten $20-whatever dollars worth of use out of it before it broke, but it’s still really frustrating and a poor business practice to sell stuff that’s so cheaply made it’s just disposable and lasts such a short amount of time. I wasn’t expecting to get a lifetime’s worth of use out of such an inexpensive product— but it should have lasted longer than a few months before falling apart.

title_review: Decent set but retain too much heat.
text:
The fit is spot-on for our IKEA queen foam bed. No issues with the pockets. The top sheet is a bit longer than most.

The finish is soft and feels good against the skin. No rough areas.

The material is 100% polyester and Made in China. The sheets were wrinkle free after first wash.

My biggest concern, and loss of 2 Stars, is the heat from these sheets. They're so tightly woven that they don't breathe. In the winter we normally sleep with a heated mattress pad, top sheet, fleece blanket, and pseudo-down comforter which keeps us quite cozy. These sheets, however, made us toss off the comforter and blanket during the night. Not a bad thing for some, but it felt like summer and became uncomfortable.

If you can get over the heat retention then these sheets are for you and at a decent price point.

title_review: Perfect and the correct size for my new mattress
text:
Fits perfect. I recently bought a new bed mattress for myself, and my father, and have noticed that some of the older sheets that normally sit on the mattress were too loose or when you lay on them, the sides un pinch them selves or barely hold on (overly loose).

Keep in mind that my old mattress was a standard classic mattress from at least 22 years ago.

All the new mattresses they sell now are a hybrid or gel and tend to be either 14 inches or 12 inches sometimes even smaller or higher depending on the variety. If you’re like me, it’s easier to buy the bed sheet for the exact size of the mattress if you buy these.

For example, a queen bed would get a queen mattress covers, but make sure the bed sheet can wraparound precisely on the mattress size.

Try to avoid, for example a 14 inch, that can accommodate an 18 or 17 inches 'deep pockets'. Through personal error, I have found out there either too loose, shift constantly, or they slide loose and sometimes they’re not tight so it ends up overly loose in the center.

These bedsheets from Amazon are perfect. Tightly wraparound and hold on almost like stockings. I very rarely have to slightly push it to the side from the middle after using it for a week it’s retaining structure. Very happy with it and they don’t break the bank either. Nothing negative to say they are a little bit see-through probably 5 to 10% but nothing major.

UPDATED: 2/17/2023

Everything I said in the review is still stands, has not come undone. The bed that I have the image is a hybrid 14inch. It has mini coils (3 inches) the rest is a foam/gel type liquid contouring type of bed. (soft top/medium firmness). Stayed on perfectly after I decided to wash the covers.

I then remove the same cover from my dad's bed and noticed that it was only very tiny lifted in the portion where he was sleeping, but did not come undone. His is a 12 inch version of this one but it's 100% contouring type of bed that molds towards the body, so obviously it constantly shifts with movement.

It stayed on, never came undone and no longer slides off by one of the sides and ends in random places. Very happy with it! Yes. buy the exact type of size mattress cover and avoid the deep pocket variety or the kind that say they can handle your mattress size, but go 3 to 4 inches more.

Those are better for classic bed spring.

Newer bed factors play a role like pure gel/foam/hybrid etc. Using common sense, the constant shifting and contouring toward the body of anyone on the bed moves around little by little the softer it goes. A lot of deep pocket variety don't have a string you can pull if you have a 12/14 inch newer mattress.

Very happy I don't have to waste time every morning now because it slid off on one side or came almost completely undone in the center, instead, I can just do a tiny touchup on top by hand, (flattening) pinching the sides (or where its needed). But rarely needed. I have also slept on the bed a few days with just the new sheet covers (no flat-sheet/comforter or pillows) and they still don't come undone. Great product.

title_review: Once it's assembled, it's not too shabby
text:
These are really great! They fit in a closet, the fabric baskets fit in them nicely, and they're a great storage space option with some lovely customizing options.

BUT...the little brown, wooden pegs that you use for assembly are very weak and break easily. We attempted to assemble this thing from the middle outward (as per the instructions) but had it up as it is pictured, not lying on its back. When we attempted to move it, the whole thing came apart with a terrible crash and cracking of tiny dowel pegs. We found replacements at Home Depot, so were able to assemble it after all, but the Home Depot pegs were made from a much better wood.

Other than that, I've loved having it.

title_review: Not 3 cups uncooked rice capacity, but works great regardless
text: Using 2 cups of uncooked rice will fill this little cooker almost to the top. I would say 2.5 cups max can be used. Definitely not 3. Works very well. Keep in mind it won’t manually shut off. It goes from cook mode to keep warm. So you can dry out your rice if you don’t unplug the cooker within 20-30 minutes after the rice is done. I suggest you set a timer to make sure you don’t forget it’s been left on. Other than that, I’d buy it again. Works great and I like the square design as opposed to the traditional round pot.

text:
This is my first rice cooker. We eat rice a couple of times a week but I just made it in a pot with a tight fitting lid on the stove. To be honest, I couldn't understand what the big deal was about rice cookers. Yeah, I get that they will keep rice warm. If we ate rice every day, several times a day I get why that would be a great feature. But it just seemed like another, single use appliance to take up valuable counter space in my tiny, crowded kitchen.

We usually eat rice twice or three times a week and usually it's for dinner. The leftovers are reheated the next day and leftovers from that are made into fried rice. Such is the way we eat.

But this rice cooker was super duper convenient and it was a lot easier to clean than than my stovetop pot because their was no bottom layer to scrape up ( always have a slightly brown bottom layer of rice). Also, I think I might be able to make a few different kinds of rice in this cooker. There is also a steamer tray, which could be used to steam a teeny tiny portion of vegetables.

text:
I have some seed throwing pet birds and a dog hair filled mini van. Over the years I've had different variations of this product none of which was completely satisfactory. This one works and works well. It comes with a charger, mounting bracket and screws, crevice tool and brush attachment. Both attachments slide on, The instructions say to charge fully before first use. Mine was already charged I left it on over night just to be sure it was completely charged. I do wish there was an indicator to let users know when it was charging and completely powered up.

That being said, this is very easy to use. The suction is great and it cleaned up those stray seeds and bird debris. It made sort order of dog hair, dust and dirt in the vehicle. It seems to be most effective on smooth surfaces but did okay on the carpeted areas of the van. It was very easy to empty and the capacity is somewhat larger than most similar products. It has a filter which should be replaced after six to nine months depending on use. Filters currently run about five dollars.

I really like this dust buster. The cordless convenience can't be beat and it is pleasingly powerful for its size and weight. It is simple to use and not awfully noisy. It comes with a two year limited warranty.

title_review: Flexible Blades Perform Like Old "Rubber" Blades
text:
Recently, I purchased a Rubbermaid spoon-shaped spatula to replace an old one (with a "rubber" blade) that had been in my kitchen drawer for more than 10 years. Unfortunately, the new Rubbermaid spatula had a stiff blade (probably silicone) that didn't perform nearly as well as the old "rubber" blade. The stiff new-model blade didn't conform easily to the sides of the bowl or pan that was being scraped, and it left behind a lot more ice cream, icing, sauce, and gravy than the old "rubber" blade.

The blades of this wonderful set of silicone spatulas have exactly the same flexibility as the blade on my old "rubber" spatula. All of them, but especially the spoon-shaped spatula, make it easy to scoop out thick mixtures quickly without leaving a lot of the mixture behind. I am really pleased to have found this product, especially because the 3-piece set cost less than the single replacement ([[ASIN:B0000VLZK8 Rubbermaid FG193300WHT 9-1/2-Inch Spoon-Shaped Spatula]]).

Other reviewers report that the spatulas are not durable, and that the blades come off, especially with dishwasher use. However, for me the spatulas rate 5 stars, because what I need most are the flexible blades. I use them for scraping bowls, not for mixing thick batters or for cooking on the stovetop.

title_review: Maximum oven temperature needs to be included in the package
text: These brightly colored AmazonBasics silicone baking cups are rather small by comparison to others I have and many paper liners, but I must say that I love the set.  Fortunately, I received a pack of 24, enabling me to bake a couple dozen at a time without switching them.  Since I tend to bake in large batches, I like being able to use the same style of liners for the entire batter.  As I said, the colors are bright and rainbow like, not primary colors, so they are suitable for all ages, not just youngsters.  Being reusable, they last  for repeated uses, but I was disappointed to see no directions for use on the packaging.  I mean, there is no maximum temperature listed on or inside the box.  I would definitely not use these under a broiler, but that is just my instinct, and I would not bake at a temperature higher than around 400 or so.  The size of each cup is 2" at the base, just under 1.5" tall, and around 1.75" at the top.  When filled, the cups relax a bit, so they open up at the top a little, but not as much as paper liners.

title_review: Great sheets, 5 stars based off a set that is going on almost three years now
text:
Our original set of these sheets were purchased in September 2015, we got the navy blue color. That has been our main set of sheets that we have used ever since. When we wash them, they go right back on the bed. Now granted, we aren't the type to have several different sets in rotation, but we have never felt the need to replace them with anything else.

I recently bought the light blue shade for a different bed and I'm sure we will love those too. If I had any suggestions though, I wish that this set would come with four pillowcases or have an option to pay more to choose a set that comes with 4. Also, it wasn't an issue before with the navy, but this light blue color is just a bit on the sheer side. You can see the pattern of the pillow through it. Not a huge deal, its for a childs bed. But it would be nice if it was just a bit more opaque.

title_review: Not bad but not great either!
text: I purchased these in a queen size in taupe and they did arrive quickly in a zippered plastic case. The color is not quite the same as described of as pictured - they are more of a camel color than taupe. The set comes with 2 pillow cases as described, not 4 as with some sets. My only issue with these sheets is how they fit! I don't have an oversized mattress or overstuffed pillows and these are a tight fit on both. I managed to get them on my bed and pillows with no room to spare. Other than this they are fine for the price as I've spent a lot more for only one sheet. For those people who are confused about what they are made of they're a brushed fabric as the manufacturer states. Personally I would have liked the sheets and pillow cases to have been made a little larger than they are but for the cost I won't complain.

title_review: It does NOT "Lock" into place - be careful! And it's not quite 9 inches tall.
text:
I, like a couple of other reviewers, bought it as a footrest, (helps lessen lower extremity edema while working at my desk) and in that capacity it works fine. I do NOT think I'd feel safe, however, using this as a step stool. I'm around 190 lbs. which the paper tagged ON the product says is only ten pounds from its limit of 200 lbs. It snaps back into a thin easy to carry thing quite effortlessly; however, "locking" it into position is next to impossible. Oh it has four thin metal strips you can see when you slide it open, and you can see the gaps they're supposed to "snap" into (see photo 1) -- problem is, as another reviewer pointed out already, they do NOT "lock" into place at all. I would have MUCH preferred seeing something sturdy slide into a virtually unmovable location at the top with a knob you turn and push to actually "lock" it. No such luck! The thin metal strips that slide into a rather wide gap in the top piece, can slide back out as easily as they slid into place. This would make me feel very uneasy in any kind of dangerous situation. I would NOT let a child use this to stand on. Incidentally, I find it odd that the very picture illustrated at the top of the page on Amazon is exactly what the paper on the item tells you NEVER to do (see photo 2). Finally, and this isn't nitpicking because I need nothing less than 9 inches of elevation for my feet... this is barely over 8 and a half. It just is NOT 9 inches tall (see photo 3). I show where the top is and it is barely over the 8.5 inch mark and if anything, I'm angling the tape slightly in so that if it were perfectly vertical it would show clearly it's closer to the 8.5 (black line) measurement. Now to be perfectly fair, if none of this bothers you, it might make a handy book stand, or, an 8.5 inch foot rest. Otherwise, I'd be very careful using it to support the full weight of a human bodyl

UPDATE: 2-14-22. As stated above I only wanted it for a footrest, I felt a piece of plastic sticking out and when I pulled it from under my desk, the plastic fell to the floor. (See 4th picture.) It was one of those "alleged" LOCK tabs that DO NOT work. I simply tried to "lock it in place" and this tab broke off. I did not hammer it, bang on it or anything that should have done this. I WAS going to order another as a footrest for my front room but seeing this thing literally falling apart before my eyes, I cancelled the order. I reiterate... if you want something to hold a few books or something like that--you should go for it; but caveat emptor (buyer beware) after seeing how this thing is so cheaply built and has pieces break off, I can't recommend it in all good conscience because if someone fell off and hurt themselves, I would feel terrible if they read this review and thought it safe to stand on--I don't.

This lid is perfect and also the right size for many other pots in my kitchen as well as some casseroles.

Love the little steam-release hole in the top. Perfect for when you want to use your Instant Pot as a slow cooker.

The quality is great and would make a great addition to your pots and pans collection.

title_review: Budget-Priced Stick Vac Has Strong Suction--Does Good Job on Carpet, Great Job on Hard Floors
text:
The power and versatility of this budget-priced (about $42 on Amazon) BISSELL FEATHERWEIGHT STICK VACUUM (Lightweight Bagless, Blue) simply blows me away. It's a dustbuster with three attachments (a crevice tool, a floor sweeper, and a handle for use with the floor sweeper) that will be all the vacuum you need for a dorm room or a studio apartment.

The suction is really strong, and it “picks up” better on pile carpet than my Dirt Devil stick vac that has a floor sweeper attachment with a powered brush. This Bissell vac has no brush (just suction and a small rubber sweep), but it does a good job on carpet and a great job on hard floors. Without the floor attachment, the dustbuster does a good job on upholstery (with or without the crevice tool) and in cleaning up non-liquid spills.

The vacuum is easy to assemble and disassemble. The dirt cup is easy to remove, empty, and replace--no bags are needed. The filter for the motor is also easy to remove and replace, though it takes a little effort to brush off the fine fuzz that it collects. The filter can be washed if it gets too dirty, and replacement filters are available if the filter gets completely worn out.

This stick vac takes up little space in a closet. It’s very lightweight, so it's not tiring to push around. It has a long electric cord, and, unlike a cordless model, it's always ready to go when you need it.

title_review: I mean, it's a lightweight dust vac on a stick...
text:
It's a fine light duty "a hit, a lick & a miss" kinda vacuum. I honestly have a handheld dust vac that has more suction, just isn't on a stick for doing floors. And cost a good bit more. The cost: Well, you get what you pay for...

So, why did I buy it? Why didn't I return it? My 'kid' is (cognitively) 2 (in a 24 year old body). And he wanted a vacuum. Letting him play with my new $$$hark was not an option. He's obviously too big for one of those little working kiddie Dirt Devils. Purple is his favorite color. So for about the same money as a toy vacuum he can now vacuum up whatever makes his heart happy and I don't have to worry about my primary vacuum getting clogged with legos or socks or whatever else he gets fascinated with seeing 'disappear'.

text:
I don't really like cleaning the floors, but this vacuum is so easy to just grab and clean something up real quick.. it's awesome. It doesn't have a brush, so it's good for hardwood floors. I used it on a new walnut floor and it didn't make a mark (walnut is soft). It picks up pretty much everything, except for large heavy objects like a screw. My place was under construction, so I've used it for plaster dust and other fine sticky dust and it worked great.

The cord isn't very long, it would be nice if it were longer, but you could always leave an extension cord on it. It'll get most of a room on its own.

I like that you can easily switch it from floor to handheld.. and it's light enough to easily weild on the stairs. Or pick up and vacuum a coffee table if you want to. It's easy and not too messy to clean the filter, but there is sometimes a little puff of dust when you first turn it on after cleaning it.

I've had mine for 6 months. It seems like the clasp that holds it together where the filter is might give way at some point, but otherwise it's pretty good for the price.

title_review: clean up the messes for less
text: This little, inexpensive stick vacuum is one of the better ones out there. It doesn't have a power head, but what you are doing with a stick vac doesn't require a power head. That is what your regular vacuum is for. This is for cleaning up messes quickly and efficiently. It is good at cleaning off the sofa when the dog gets sand on it, same thing with the floor in a small area. If you use it to clean your entire floor, be prepared to empty the dirt receptacle and you will need to replace the filter from time to time. Even though it has a 15 foot cord, you would probably need an extension cord to clean out your car. This is great for those times when you need a quick touch up and not a full blown deep cleaning. For the price point, it is worth every penny. I am seriously thinking of taking this with me to the beach because it seems like there is always sand in the rooms when kids are running in and out

title_review: Where have you been all my life?!
text:
Where has this been my whole life?! It’s like a powerful Dustbuster with a long handle so perfect for little crumbs. I have hardwood floors throughout my house and only carpet in the kids bedrooms with 1 rug in the family room. I rarely brought out the vacuum because it was big and bulky. I would sweep multiple times a day and still felt like the floors were still dirty. I had a
Roomba at one point but our dog decided it was an intruder and “took care of the problem”.

Pros:
-lightweight (3.4lbs)
-works on all flooring types
-easy to empty
-bagless
-turns into handheld
-attachment for crevices like between couch cushions.
-not as loud as regular vacuum
-sucks up items as large as Cheerios

Cons
-short cord (15ft)
-no hook or anything to hang it on a wall for storage
-small collection chamber but it’s a little vacuum so it’s expected!

All in all, this is great for a quick run around the house and picks up crumbs, dog hair and snacks left behind by little ones!

text: Our cordless Dyson bit the dust (batteries failed every year, and the cost to replace them quickly added up above what the vacuum cost new...Dyson telling us to drive 200+ miles to the nearest service center was the end of dealing with it and will not get another Dyson...anyway...) so was looking for a 'temporary' vacuum as we have a long haired cat who loves to throw cat sand from the litter box like it's her job and dark hard wood floors that show everything so vacuuming daily is pretty much a necessity. I actually laughed when I opened this together because it felt like I was playing house, the vacuum is just so small and light. Then I spent the next hour or so vacuuming everything. It is SO light. The simplicity of it is expected with the price but also works super well functionally - you can just take the roller head right off and use it as a hand vacuum, and when you're done, just press it back in to the roller head and that's it. Just press the button in the middle to unclick, remove filter, and empty. The only thing I would change is the cord which is annoyingly short, even for our 1100 sq ft apartment. I have to plug it in a few different times just to get all the areas, but am surprisingly shocked for ~$35. Will it replace a regular vacuum? No, definitely not, not even close. I have to go over some pieces a few times to get them but was not expecting ground breaking suction at this price. If you are looking for something that will get things clean looking and not break the bank? This is it. If you are looking for something to clean your house well and be a workhorse, this is not it and for the price, you really shouldn't expect it to be.

text:
This is a really high-quality mattress pad. Please note it is NOT waterproof and is not meant to be. Waterproof pads have their uses, but they can be uncomfortable to sleep on, in that they can make the sleeper hot and sweaty, so some of us don't want waterproof mattress pads for that reason.

This pad is not sold as, nor is it meant to be, a "pillow-top" type mattress pad. It is simply a standard, quilted, fitted pad which is created to protect a mattress from dust and sweat, thus increasing its lifetime. For this advertised purpose, this is a high quality mattress pad. It also doesn't have an odor, which is a nice change in a chemical-laden world where almost everything one buys seems to reek of toxic chemicals.

I pre-washed this pad before using it the first time. I set my washer for cold-water, gentle cycle, and I put it in the dryer on low heat, the latter per the manufacturer's recommendation. Unlike waterproof pads I have washed for family members, it does not get destroyed in a dryer.

The green color is a soft sage green. They are perfect with my bedroom decor, which is Colonial Williamsburg colors.
A bonus is having two extra pillow cases.

title_review: Fits our split adjustable bed better then xl twin sheets
text:
These fit our split adjustable bed better then xl twin sheets. The pockets are deeper and don’t fall off. We just got this bed a few weeks ago and learning what type of sheets to buy for it.

These have not been washed or dried yet. Usually I wash em before putting on but I wanted to see how well they fit and ended up just leaving them on. When I do wash em, if the size changes I’ll come back to update my review.

These sheets are soft and comfy. Thin but in a good way. We don’t like heavy sheets or blankets because we get too hot at night. So these are perfect for our preference.

You get two fitted sheets for each base. But you share the flat sheet. Other sets we’ve bought cams with two flat sheets so we’d have our own.
But we prefer to have one large fitted sheet.
As long as the price doesn’t increase and they don’t shrink and fall off after washing and drying we will definitely buy more in different colors.
