text:
This is a nice brush for cleaning glasses, mainly, although I find the bristles to be a bit soft for my liking.

I have another bottle brush that I use for bottles and glasses, as it has a longer handle, the neck is thin and made of twisted wire, and it has firmer bristles. I actually find myself pulling it out pretty often because this one just isn't really cutting it for me.

I do think this one will be great for cleaning my crystal and other delicate glassware, so it's not a loss. However, the one with the long, thin, wire neck and firmer bristles is far superior for cleaning BOTTLES and, since this one IS called a bottle brush yet it isn't all that great for that task (because of the width of its neck and how short it is), I think I'd have to recommend the other one over this one.

title_review: Soft and surviving multiple trips through the laundry nicely. Thinner than expected
text:
On the one hand, I really like this towel set. Each piece is a functional, useable size and the cotton is very soft after four trips through the laundry. None of them have shrunk or shown any signs of coming apart, nor have I seen any loose stitching or hems.

The hand towel is getting a lot of use here because we wash our hands a lot throughout the day. It's very absorbent and feels nice. The bath towel is a tad smaller than my guest towels, but it works as a basic towel for wrapping up wet hair. The wash rag is super soft for face cleaning.

My one star deduction is because these are all quite thin. At this price point, I don't expect plush, luxury type towels of course. However.... These are thin enough to remind me of lower end motels that I stayed in as a broke college kid on shoe string road trips. I would buy a set to keep in my barn rest room or actually to take on my road trips now.

title_review: Wow, these are perfect and holding up better than any pillows I've ever used
text:
I admit I'm shocked. Like many of you I'm sure, I've gone through so many pillows only to find they are disappointing, either from the start, or after a short time of using them. So I didn't have my hopes up, but I was desparate and didn't have a lot of money to spend. Besides. I've never found that spending more resulted in better pillows anyway.

These are truly amazing to me. They are both soft and very supportive. I'm a side-sleeper, with past severe whiplash injuries and other issues, and the fact that I have zero discomfort from these at all has made my sleep actually restful. I don't wake up in pain, or with a stiff jaw from having been grinding my teeth from discomfort in my neck etc.

The are nice and thick but not overly so, and very soft without collapsing on you at all. I mean, I've noticed no reduction in puffiness at all. The go into the pillowcases no problem.

When I got them, per the instructions, I ran them one at a time in the dryer to puff them up. Haven't needed to do it again. I'm not sure how these were made that they are so superior to other pillows, but dang, get some and try them, seriously.

text: I washed one of these in my large-capacity front-loader washing machine, and it barely had room to move around. I washed it alone, and placed nothing else inside the drum. This pillow struggled to move around inside the washing machine, and I felt that it was not getting thoroughly washed. It was jammed inside and barely moved inside the drum. THEN, to make matters worse, here I am still waiting for it to dry completely after having run my dryer for nearly an hour FOUR times. It still remains damp, and it was the only thing I placed inside; it was not competing for space with any other item. It was literally sopping wet when I first removed it from the washing machine, so much so that I could barely lift it from the washer. It was THAT heavy because of the water it had retained. This was likely due to the fact that it was unable to move around or rotate inside my washing machine. I regret having purchased two of these because they're too bulky and dense, which results in their being unsuitable for a residential washing machine and dryer.

Bubble pockmarks on surface. Where is the quality control. Or is this a returned item? Or the factory doesn’t care and that is what they are sending out - just junk? Unacceptable

UPDATE 2023-03-03
2nd one arrived without the blemishes. hard to find faults with this design, but let me try... ok the pour is nice, the infuser is deep - has a little handle, the lid can be managed with one thumb, the whole pot can be managed with one hand, ceramic seems good.... what to pick on... what to pick on... ok... ok I got it. These are REAAAAAALY dumb things, but hey, I can't leave it well eough alone... 1. Not easy to clean the infuser - tea bits get stuck to the bottom so washing it is a pain - I'm sure there's a nifty way of cleaning it that I don't know, that saves time and water. 2. the plastic neck shroud should have been white... although... I can see the reasoning for black - wont get stained over time. 3. the handle could have been just a bit more ergonomic, like, include a curve where your ring finger goes to support and lift... 4. the bottom of the pot is concave. So if you put it on one of them pad warmers, it doesn't make solid flat surface to flat surface contact.

Man you know what? Ok, I like this one. Not a bad piece of engineering.

on and 5. would've been nice to include a little recess in the spout so when you're done pouring it doesn't drip...

But... it's good... no its really good. I'd buy it again if I had to (hopefully won't)

text: I overall love this teapot. It’s sturdy, looks nice, and has plenty of space in it. I’m taking one star off for two reasons. Because of the taller design, it can be difficult to scrub the bottom of the teapot. I have to force my hands through the top hole in order to reach the bottom, or really stretch my fingers. This may not be an issue if you have smaller hands or use a scrub brush as opposed to a regular sponge. Secondly, the handle for the infuser tends to pop out fairly easy which can be inconvenient when washing. Other than these two things, I’ve thoroughly enjoyed this teapot, and would likely still order it again.

title_review: You get what you pay for, I guess
text:
So far, I’m not very impressed.

Back story: I have a 20 oz ceramic-lined insulated travel mug that makes a wonderfully strong cup of tea that stays warm for a very long time even without the lid, which is great except I have to wait at least 45 minutes for it to cool enough to drink, so I ordered this thinking I’d get something that would allow me to keep a large amount of tea warm while also being able to easily pour some out into a mug where it could cool faster.

Unfortunately, what I’ve found myself with instead is weak tea doesn’t stay warm for very long—it’s been lukewarm within 30 minutes every time I’ve tried to use it. I even used my ceramic mug to measure out the water to use in the pot, to see if my water-to-tea ratio was just off, but it still made very weak tea in comparison.

I am returning this and will try again with a different brand.

text: This is such a versatile appliance because not only can you make rice but many other things as well. I bought this to use in my tiny camper because it is only 200 watts and I can use it with my small portable generator. Since it's not camping season here currently in the wintry northeast, so far have used it in my home kitchen for making soup, casseroles, oatmeal and even steamed salmon (water in the rice cooker with steamer on top). I put a small pizza pan underneath the cooker when I'm using it in case of a spillover from foods that foam like oatmeal. A small pie pan or just a plate could also be used. This mini rice cooker comes nicely packaged and includes a beautiful recipe book with everything from mac & cheese to chocolate cake recipes with full-page color photos of most of the dishes. I'm looking forward to trying the turkey chili and banana bread recipes. The perfect size for 1-2 people, this rice plus cooker is super simple to clean since the pot is removable. With such a small footprint, it doesn't take up a lot of counter space and it's easy to store. There are no dials to change temperature or time, just ON/OFF...easy peasy! I love the many colors it comes in so you can pick your favorite. I own many Dash appliances and love all of them but this is one of my favorites. If you are thinking of getting this mini rice cooker, don't hesitate, just do it!

text:
Edit: After 5 months of using this 2-3 times per week, I threw it in the garbage because I feel it is now unsafe. A couple of nights ago, I was making rice and noticed a very strong hot electrical smell. Burning wire and plastic. Rice was about half way through cook time. I grab a towel to unplug it, which created a large spark. I let it sit about 10 minutes, then lifted the small pot out of the cooker. Very strong hot/burnt plastic smell arose from the cooker. I let the device cool down all the way and placed it a plastic grocery store bag, and took it out to the dumpster. Lesson learned. Never buy cheap plastic appliances. It's too bad, because it's the perfect size for a single senior like me. I only add rice to the 1/2 mark on the included measuring cup, so that's a perfect amount for dinner. Most other rice cooker are huge in comparison. I guess it's back to using a pot for me!

I love handy little gadgets! So easy to use. No babysitting the pan to make sure it doesn't boil over. Always rinse your rice, and don't overload it. It's not designed to make heaping piles of rice, lol. It may take a couple of uses in order to determine the perfect amount of water that's needed for the amount of rice you are trying to make. Then, you're good to go! I just bought this, the egg cooker, and the mini griddle. Love them all!

title_review: Great beginner rice cooker, limited versatility. Great for dorm rooms!
text:
Hi!

I purchased this rice cooker for use in a dorm suite and it has worked great! We use our favorite Japanese rice from our local asian market and this makes the dorm room feel a bit more like home. We've used the rice for onigiri, kare (curry), sushi rolls, donburi, etc, etc. We make plain rice along with rice with nori (seaweed) and mushrooms.

The downsides to this rice cooker is it is relatively small, you can maybe squeeze in two cups of rice with the needed water. It also has no adjustable cook time so we sometimes have to run it more than once to get the perfect cook.

Overall, I give this a 3 star for its convenience and cooking quality. If you factor in the low price, I'd move it up to a 4-4.5 star. Thus, for your first rice cooker, someone on a budget, or someone with minimal kitchen space, this would be a great addition!

title_review: Good Travel Mug; a Couple of Gotchas to Keep in Mind
text:
I have been using a Contigo sealing travel mug for my morning coffee for ages. I like it because it doesn’t spill, even when I knock the whole thing off my desk onto the floor (which is the exact reason I started using it in the first place). This one by Contigo is a fine mug that will see much use, though I offer a couple of words of caution.

There are 3 sizes to consider here. There is a 16 oz. size, a 20 oz. size and a 24 oz. size. I have the 20 oz. Sake model which is attractive though not flashy. There is a variety of colors available so you can find one that suits your preference.

The lid is of course the open secret to this mug. It has a snap top that opens and allows for easy dispensing of liquid (hot or cold), and when closed the mug prevents the liquid from leaking. It seals well enough with silicone (?) gaskets and seals to prevent even a small leak from occurring. The seals also help retain temperature. So far I have only used it for coffee, and it keeps my coffee hot for at least 4-5 hours.

I have learned a couple of things about Contigo’s mugs that need to be mentioned. My original Contigo mug is nearly identical in operation and mechanism, and with it I’ve made two unpleasant discoveries. First, it isn’t safe to keep the mug in a bag, as the snap top can get knocked open. I had this happen and a book I had in the bag was drenched. Second, and more serious, is that there is a gasket under the lid that creates the seal with the main barrel of the mug, and this can get dislodged when cleaning. If it does come out, it is very difficult to get it back into the lid and seated properly. I have had this happen twice. I suspect this is the issue that has caused others’ mugs to leak. Both of these issues are not show-stoppers, but they do prevent this product from being truly outstanding.

This is a fine travel mug, that does a good job of keeping drinks hot and preventing spills and dribbling. It isn’t perfect and there are a couple of things to keep in mind about it that relate to sealing properly, though the issues are not absolute deal-breakers if you keep them in mind and work around them.

text:

It not only allows for liquid to pool, which if hot is guaranteed to burn, but also the drinking area is so wide that the beverage spills out the sides and down the front of my shirt. And it is not possible to unlock this with one hand without enrolling in a body building class and bulking up first.

I purchased the Contigo Autoseal Travel Mug - Stainless Steel Vacuum Insulated Tumbler - 2 Pack last year and am MUCH happier with this model. Doesn't spill, can be easily unlocked with one hand, and hot liquid doesn't pool in front of the drinking area.

title_review: The BEST Amazon Has to Offer Their Loyal Customers
text:
I don't write many reviews on Amazon but when I do, it is usually really great or really bad about a product. In this case, I am ABSOLUTELY IN LOVE with this bedding set. Purple (whether light or dark) is my favorite color and was looking for bedding that affordable, came in a set, and that really suited my bedroom color palette as a whole. I decided with all the other rave reviews that I give AmazonBasics a try. I do not regret this purchase at all. It comes with a comforter that surrounds every inch of my bed, bedsheets, the sheet that goes in between the bedsheets and the comforter that sometimes I will use as a light, summer blanket, and 2 pillow cases.

The only minor negative things about this product is that some of the threading, particularly on the comforter & I think maybe even the bedsheets DOES COME APART easily, even before use/as you are unboxing it from its nice storage plastic. It can be a minor fix if you cut the loose thread with sewing scissors (DO NOT PULL IT or it will make the situation worse) and reinforce it with some stitches (if you have the time & sewing skills to do so). Also, the comforter is not as super thick as I would like it to be. But it does indeed keep you warm & snug throughout the cold, winter nights. And it is light enough if you just want to lay on top of it during the spring/summer time. I would love it even better if it was just a plain Royal Purple without the generic flower design. Simplicity is key to a home.

Overall, if you are under a budget, and not super picky about the quality or the finer details of what you would like your bedding to be, then this is the perfect bedding for you! I think any demographic would appreciate this in their home/apartment (great for kids, for guests, college students going away, etc). Thank you Amazon!

title_review: Helped me make the best of a less than ideal situation.
text:
We are renting a house that has really no pantry space and old cabinets that aren't quite right to stack anything in. Plus we order a lot of our canned goods and pantry items from Costco to be delivered. No Costco in our city! :( That means we have to order $75 at once to get free shipping.

I got four of these, hoping they wouldn't look too bad stacked just right out on the kitchen counter with my Instant Pots that I use every day and therefore don't put away. I stacked two in the kitchen and put two stacked beside a makeshift pantry shelf to the left of our unused fireplace. And it all looks good! Holds a lot of stuff. I even was able to put my large plastic 20 oz. spice jars lying flat, two side by side, in the center with rows of cans on the left and right and can see them well enough. So all of Sig-O's canned soups and stuff, along with snacks, are on the stack in the living room and all my cooking-type canned things and spices are in the kitchen.

Hey, it's not as good as a nice big country pantry, but it sure does make my life easier. I'm glad I found these.

title_review: GREAT cup of JOE, Compact and EASY to use!!
text:
I love, LOVE my new little coffee maker.

Tips:
I did run vinegar and water through 3x to clean and then water 3x upon receipt. I use water from a supplier out of my water cooler.

I use my Glass Measuring Cup to pour the water in.

I did notice it must have a temp regulator because when using hot water from water cooler it speeds up process and the temp of the coffee comes out the same as when tested using normal water from the tap.

I bought refillable k cups to use and it has made perfect hot cups of coffee and tea. I do notice LESS IS MORE when using refillable k cups. The more coffee grounds you put in (overfilling it) the weaker the coffee. Fill them about 1/2 full. You only need 1 tea bag to make a nice cup of tea, as well.
(The k-cups I bought worked GREAT!! Maxware 4 Reusable Refillable Coffee Filters For Keurig Family 2.0 and 1.0 Brewers Fits K200, K300/K350/K360,/K450/K460, K500/K550/K560 (Purple, 4) https://www.amazon.com/dp/B06WWFTQLC/ref=cm_sw_r_cp_apa_i_bBqRCb1G0ZRSG n were only $8.25/4)

I drink dark roast coffee because I have stomach issues (darker the roast the better for these issues). I use Seattle's Best 4th Street Bristo most of the time(think they changed the name but that's what I know it as) it comes out better than any coffee shop coffee does for me and doesn't upset my stomach at all.

This was the perfect replacement for my Farberware one that decided to just DIE!! In fact, I think it works TONS better. Great purchase and it's nice and compact!! I could easily pack and travel with this. Would BUY AGAIN!!
I haven't cleaned this yet other than initially and I use water out of my water cooler to keep it cleaner, as well.

text:
[[VIDEOID:f2f71e3024faa3424f3d188e624fb87]] * i received this product at a discount for my honest and unbiased review. i was not influenced by anyone in any way.

When I first saw this single service coffee brewer it looked super simple to use... and it truly is. We have 2 keurigs and a VUE. Now, I will have this one for my shop and I will give my daughter one of my keurig machines, since she doesn't have a kcup coffee maker.

This machine is also really easy to clean. I poured in 15oz of water and it fit just fine. I made sure I measured it out first using a measuring cup. I didn't use 15 full ounces though in my cup of coffee, I filled my own cup to where I wanted it to stop and then poured the water inside. I gotta have room for my tons of creamer I always add to my coffee. Like they say, "have a little coffee with your creamer?" That about sums it up for me.
(laughing out loud) My coffee came out the same as when I use my keurig. Really tasty! The area that I am doing the review in, it's a small space, so this will definitely work in a small space. As for instructions, I didn't even look at any, that's how simple it was. But! you have them right there on the side of the coffee machine. How simple is that?

I also read other reviews saying it was definitely not 15oz, so I ran 15oz of plain water through the machine to see and, Yup! exactly 15oz came out, and the temperature came in at 183°F. I tried different coffee brands of kcups and they all worked. My only drawback was when you take off the extended part to put your coffee mug, it's not very sturdy there. I don't think the mug would fall over, but there is still a chance.

There are a variety of colors to choose from to match your decor.

HOW LONG DOES IT TAKE TO MAKE A CUP? It takes only about 2 minutes. The water needs time to get hot, but when it starts, it comes out pretty fast.

'compact

'uses your everyday kcups.
'coffee mug fits perfect

CONS:
'where the coffee mug goes, the holding plate is not sturdy.

Overall, this coffee machine is a great buy. Works well and would make a nice housewarming gift, gift for college student, for office or shop. I highly recommend it. If anything happens over time with it, I will be sure to come back to update my review.

I hope this review has helped you with your buying decision. If you have any questions, please feel free to ask.

title_review: Changed original 5 star review to one star
text:
ORIGINAL REVIEW MAY 2019
Just coming off back-to-back bad performance with the famous K makers (one leaked, one kept clogging and had trouble heating the water), I was ready to try something drastically different and ended up here by chance as my kitchen is mostly red. I'm glad I did as the Chulux is in every way superior. Even if I start with cold water, which I usually do as it's filtered and waiting in the fridge, the coffee is sufficiently hot even when a liberal amount of cold creamer is used (see picture). I make two cups in the morning and two more in the evening and I get consistently perfect results every time.

I love how easy this thing is to clean as well, just twist off the nozzle under the pod and give a quick rinse, no turning the unit upside down and poking at it an impossible to see into space with a paperclip ever again! Perhaps best of all this maker has a tiny footprint, about twice as high as your cup and just barely wider... small enough and light enough it can easily be put in a cabinet out of sight when not in use, if desired, something you could never do with the bigger models. I'm going to order a second maker to take to work. Highly recommended.

The only thing that could be improved on a just a little is the appearance. I really enjoy the fun array of colors, but the dull silver knob on top and dull metal band around the maker in chrome or a shiny material would dress the maker up quite a bit, but in regards to functionality it's perfect.

UPDATE MARCH 2020
Unit stopped working today. Powers up, the light comes on, the water heats, then stops and never comes up through the tube. It's a shame as this is a great little design but at $40 it should last longer than 10 months.

title_review: The YouTube instructional video is a MUST
text: Forget about the instructions on the inside of the box; go to YouTube and find Rabbitgoo’s 2.5 minute instruction video. You don’t need the install kit if you’ve got some ‘redneck ingenuity’ - lol. I used a Starbucks gift card for my squeegee. In the comments under the video I got the idea to use spray glass cleaner with a few drops of dish detergent (my dish detergent is pretty cheap and watery, so I added more than just a drop, maybe 1/2 teaspoon). I had bought the film about a year ago and decided I knew how to install it. WRONG. I did everything bass-ackwards and ended up taking hours per window, in tears, bubbles never gone. I’m usually pretty smart but my blonde was totally involved in the first attempt at installing. I was also thrilled to see, via Rabbitgoo’s response to a question by a YouTube viewer, that the film can be applied inside or out (or both of you want to really obscure view). My kid is Autistic and in 4 years he has tore down $300 of the $4 to $10 Walmonster blinds. I have neither the patience nor the finances to continue supplying him with blinds. Now if he decides to jump out the bathtub and run to his room, jangling his junk, passing cars won’t be getting an unexpected peep(ee) show. I was seriously scared!!

text:
Buying more! I'm renting and wanted something I could do to the windows for privacy and lower AC costs. I don't know how well it works for reducing AC costs as the outside temps dropped around the time I installed it. It lets a lot of light in, so I'm a little skeptical on that end, though maybe it keeps out enough UV etc so that visible light comes through without the same heat gain. It's not perfect for privacy by itself, but combined with the sheer curtains I have, the two are perfect. I'm getting a different film for my bathroom. If you've got your nose up to it, you can see pretty well outside (and probably in), but the further away from the film the viewer is, the more privacy. So from the street, I'm sure it's sufficient from the street or from inside my neighbors houses.

I had a million tiny little windows pains to apply it to. Things that helped: a sliding rotary paper trimmer, a little squeegee (the cheap on Amazon recommended), cutting the film a tad smaller than the surface (applying and then cutting sucks, but since there's not a difference in color, slightly smaller doesn't look bad). After a while I got lazy and stopped using the soapy water and just used regular Windex, and that seemed to work fine. Double check for bubbles at night, but once I got used to it, there were no bubbles.

text:

It has a beautiful iridescent look to it, and I love the rainbows when direct sunlight hits the window. I did 3 windows and have already bought more film. [[VIDEOID:7c5d73c4be523751050d1fb3f6e51246]] Everyone who has seen my new windows loves them! My husband said it feels like walking into a magical world. I pre-cut the sections for the french doors and I prepped by wetting both the glass AND the film wet enough to be wet but not wet enough to bead or drip, so basically damp.

FOR THE STUBBORN EDGES I waited until the next day when everything was dry as a bone, then I sprayed a q-tip with a generous amount of mega-hold hairspray. I rubbed the q-tip under the edges that were curling up making sure to get the hairspray both on the glass and the film. I pressed the film down in sections and held them long enough for a bond to form, around 5 seconds. All sealed up! You're welcome. ;)

title_review: Works like a charm... when the seals are in place
text:
[[VIDEOID:11a1a881d5ae64d2e50a27907f12f930]] So I was over at the grocery and they had wild caught salmon on sale! Woohoo! I decided this was the perfect way to try out my new food saver system. I bought two fillets then cut them into smaller "servings".

First, I tried putting 2 servings into one of the bags that came with it... couldn't get it to work... several tries... no luck. Finally, I took a look under the lid and found the rubber seal had slipped out of it's slot. I pushed it back in and suddenly everything was right! (That last picture shows me pointing at the seal in question.)

So, with everything working, I sealed the first pair of salmon servings with that bag... then used the roll to seal the next two pairs of servings. (The 4th pair of servings laying on the cutting board is for dinner tonight!) Everything worked like a charm!

So, I do recommend this product... just be mindful of those rubber seals. If they come out of their slots, it's easy enough to just push them back in... but this unit wont work until you do.

title_review: An okay food vacuum for light-duty sealing.
text:
I have used this vacuum sealer now for quite a while. I have found the one I bought a few years ago is alive and still working pretty well. The included bags are really high quality and are easy to use. One thing I have found lacking in this unit is how sometimes the unit will not vacuum the air out of the bag. I will have to take the bag out and put it back in and try again. Sometimes it will work right away and sometimes I have to try a few times. I find that the unit struggles if you do not make the opening of the bag that is being sealed smaller than the other edges of the bag. Basically, you will want to make sure your bags are rectangular and that you are sealing up the bag on one of the smaller edges.

Recently, I tried buying two more units and I found that those units did not work correctly. I had to return both of them. So, I am not sure what is up with the quality control over at Foodsaver but it has taken a bit of a turn.

Dimensions of the unit can be seen in the photos I have attached.

Included:
-The vacuum unit
-Plastic hose for air tight containers
-one roll of plastic for making bags
-a few pre-made bags

Pros:
*Cheap
*Comes with everything in one package

Cons:
*Can be a bit finicky with how it vacuums(-1 star)
*Lots of Dead on Arrival units(-1/2 a star)

Additional Considerations:
If you are looking to do a lot of sealing, I would spend a bit more money and get another machine. These can be a bit annoying to use daily.

title_review: Good basic large slow cooker without bells and whistles.
text:
Good basic large slow cooker without the newer bells and whistles. Excellent cost – to – value ratio.

I am a dedicated and experienced home cook who has used a wide variety of equipment types for decades, including slow cookers.
In fact, my first experience with a slow cooker dates back to the 1970s!

I've been using this crockpot model for several years now, and I am satisfied. The price point is excellent for a product this solid and reliable.

Note that this is a very large crockpot – – check out the volume and the dimensions and make sure that you need/want a crockpot this large. Slow cooker recipes intended for smaller crockpot do NOT do well when cooked in larger ones.

If you are new to slow cooker methods, you are better off using the "low heat" recipe options at first rather than the "high heat" recipe options. Over time, you will learn how to judge when the high heat setting is appropriate for the particular food in question, especially if that food is not high in moisture content. I suspect that some of the reviewers complaining that this model is "too hot" are simply inexperienced. The temperature settings of this model are in line with other slow cookers I have used.

This model has been durable for me and continues to perform well. The interior is still smooth and unchipped despite some rough handling, and the mechanical performance has been stable.

One tip for using this slow cooker, or any: whether or not the recipe calls for it, it's smart to spray a bit of Pam inside the cooker's interior crock before you add your recipe ingredients -- this makes clean up quick and easy. You don't want to have to scrub so hard at cooked-on residue that you scratch or dull the ceramic glaze of the crock.

Best of luck with your choice.

text:
King size navy blue (jewel tone) polyester "satin" pillow cases are GREAT!. So soothing and comfortable. I did not expect that. I bought these "satin" pillowcases so I would have less hair tangle and friction against my face. I have tried "satin" pillowcases before, but they were too slick, and I didn't like the overall feel. I didn't use them for long and I don't know where they went. I either tucked them far away or donated them. BUT, Wanting to try again, I randomly purchased this brand (likely a combination of decent price, size and colors available). THIS BRAND is awesome. I am so surprised by how comfortable these pillow cases are- not just for "satin" but for all else I have every used. I use two king sized pillows. The bottom pillow is has a pillow protector and a regular pillow case, then the pillow I put my head on is a king sized pillow with a pillow protector on it, and I think I kept a regular pillow case on it. Then this "satin" one is slid on top. The material is sleek, yet I don't feel like I am sliding around on it at all. Smooth but I stay in place. It feels cool or neutral- never too warm. I really don't know if it is overall helping my hair or face, but at least I am hoping. I dont know why, but the feel of this pillow case is unexpectedly comforting. Why is that? Too feel that sensation is something worth giving 5 stars to.

Edit: I continue to use these, and the pillow cases are still in great condition. I wrote original review in December 2018, and now almost May 2019 I still love them. I have 4 or 6 in King sized blue.

text:
First off, I was very disappointed to find a bucket half the size of the one on the dehumidifier I replaced after more than 40 years of service. And the added inconvenience of having to go downstairs every day at this time, is considerable.
Then there is the precaution noted in paperwork, not to use the water. I used the distilled water produced by the old one for dyeing fiber, in the washer, and for activities requiring distilled water.
I’d really like to know why the water should not be used.
On the basis of these complaints and negative details, I am extremely disappointed with this product. It does fill up the bucket; more often than I can empty it . . . and whilst hauling it upstairs to empty, water sloshes all over the place. I definitely do NOT recommend this unit for basements, or for those who are using it for production of useful distilled water. Or when emptying more often than once a day isn’t practical, or if wet steps and floors are a hazard or drawback.

title_review: Love it! Trending towards a great decision!
text:
8/12/2020 update: no significant raise in the electric, it being the middle of summer. I compared it with last year's electric consumption for the same month and cutoff and I see at least 150kwh less consuption this past cutoff. My electric is also about $65 less compared to last year's bill. I think it has mainly to do with the dehumidifier helping keep the indoor humidity down. I don't run it 24/7 too. I have humidity monitor and only run it when the indoor humidity goes over 55%.

I have also noticed less indoor allergy issues for my family. So far, so good! Very happy with it.

House area: 2020 sq ft livable space. 2 storeys, 3 bedrooms, 3 baths, 2 living areas

Initial review: 7/24/2020
Delivery: super fast! Came the next day and it saved us from a weekend of humid junk!

Ease of use: very easy to understand the information with the help of the manual. Had to keep the unit in the upright position for 24 hours before first use. We did so.

Efficiency: worked great right away. We managed to bring the humidity in our main living area on the ground floor in 2 hours. It does emit warm air so clearance spaces around the unit have to be observed to work efficiently. We only have this for a week after our electric cutoff and we use it a few hours during the day after the initial massive dehumidifying we did after the first day. The tank is large capacity and I only empty it once every 2 days at that rate with a humidity maintenance of 50%. It does make a huge difference. We have it set to 45% and the unit does a decent job of bringing it down to 50% right away and it seems to maintain that level even when I set it to 45%. Not a big deal for me. Bottom line is we sleep very well at night and helps the ac not run quite as hard during the day. On decent days, we maintain an indoor temp of 68F and we all sleep well. Before that, we had to crank up the AC to 65F to cope with the indoor humidity.

I will add an update after the bill cutoff and more after that to see if there are any significant impacts to the electric bill.

title_review: This unit was never able to get the humidity down to an acceptable level. Plus its LOUD.
text:
I have a 14x16' size bedroom. I wanted to get the humidity levels down to 45% for more comfortable sleeping. I was never able to get the humidity level less than 59% (this time of year the humidity level at the highest in there is 64%). It was filling up the tank with water so it was working from that perspective.

Now according to the specifications this unit is more than adequate for my size room and they also claim that humidity levels are customizable from 35-85%. That was the fine print I guess, it's customizable for sure, whether it actually gets the humidity level down is another story. I had all doors and windows closed to the room so it was basically confined to the bedroom only (even the door to the bathroom was closed).

That was the biggest issue. Now don't let anyone convince you that this unit isn't loud. It is extremely loud. With all the doors closed I could hear it running in the living room. I could have dealt with that if the unit would have performed as claimed (earplugs).

I sent it back.

title_review: The white plastic grid on the back is the “filter”
text:
This machine seems to function well for removing moisture from the air. I attached a drain hose to continuously drain water to the sump.

After a couple of weeks of operation, the filter light came on. I removed the white grid on the back of the unit to look for a filter inside. I did not find anything Inside the grid that looked like a filter, so I called homelabs customer service to report a missing filter.

The nice woman I spoke with explained that the white plastic grid itself is the filter. This grid has a fine metal mesh screen that will prevent most dust from going through to the cooling fins inside.

I know it costs more, but you'll be glad you splurged. The cheap ones will likely kill you due to the bacteria that gets trapped in the slider part of the lid. You can never get those things clean. I would put this design up there with the guy who came up with Post-It Notes. Yea, it's that smart!

Well, I paid a reasonable price and waited with baited breath.  Opened the bag that it came in (not boxed, no bubble wrap, just a plastic bag inside another bag).  I opened it, took it out and to my pleasant surprise it was in PERFECT condition!!  Not a dent, scratch and my husband was totally excited.  Yeti is an awesome brand - these tumblers will outlast me, they keep the cool and the hot inside wayyyy better than any cup I've purchased at TJMAXX.  You can't go wrong!  Enjoy!

My wife has been using styrofoam cups for her ice water. But, after constant using, they eventually get soft.
My daughter suggested that she should purchase a Yeti cup. Because she drinks so much water during the day, she went with the large 30oz cup.
Tested it the first day it arrived. Placed ice and water in the cup at 8pm. At 8am the next morning, her cup still had ice sitting in it. Tested it some more and at 2pm, there was still ice in the cup.
I was so impressed that I ordered another 30oz cup. I love it! We bring our cups everywhere we go. When we're going shopping, we leave the cups in the car. Even when outdoor temperatures are in the upper 90s, we get back to the car and are able to drink ice cold drinks.
Very impressed with how well this cup keeps my drinks cold for way over 16 hours.
I haven't tried it with hot coffee so I can't tell you how long hot drinks last. But, for cold, this cup is the best.
The only thing I wished it had was a handle of sorts. It's not impossible to hold but the 30oz cup is big and it's a little hard to carry around.

text: What a joke. After seeing the commercial all over the channels I decided to read the reviews. I thought maybe there could be a chance this pillow may work. Lots of good reviews but now I am wondering how many are true. In any case I ordered the firmest pillow. Upon arrival all the air in the pillow was sucked out for packaging purposes. It took a while to return to its "original" size. I even threw it in the dryer to see if it would puff up and it did. It took a couple of days to feel firm. But even then sleeping on this pillow flattened out real fast. Throughout the night I could feel my head laying on my mattress. It's Shape appears firm. When squeezing it, it feels firm but sleeping on it is a joke. I found myself flipping my pillow through out the night. I ended up going back to my Malouf pillow which is firm (also sold on Amazon),  supportive in the neck and I have had it for a year and I NEVER once had to flip it or scrunch it up for support. That pillow is the best pillow EVER. I cannot say that for MyPillow.

title_review: Not a replacement for a down pillow
text: Had high expectations for the pillow, and ordered according to the information required to get the best pillow for ones size, sleeping habits etc. As indicated by the manufacturer. Received the pillows in a timely fashion did exactly as the instructions said put in dryer for 15 minutes, where they fluffed up properly. ( purchase two pillows one for wife one for myself ).The issue is that it's a pillow filled with foam so it was very springy and spongy like a pillow I would buy for $5 at a big box store. I use a down pillow and this is anything but head conforming. My wife is keeping her pillow as she uses a foam pillow. I believe that the advertising is misleading in the sense that this does not adjust to your head positioned, at least it didn't for me and I tried it for two nights every which way I could, and just ended up with a stiff neck. It may work for a majority of the people, but if one uses a down pillow this foam pillow does not translate into replacing a down pillow. Update, My wife returned the pillow after a week as it did not form at all to her head. Gave her bad neck cramps. The wife purchased a $12 foam pillow from Bed Bath & Beyond that she said was soooo much better. Don't waste your money, there are much better and cheaper options out there. And the commercials running every ten minutes 24 hours a day are enough to drive one insane.

text:
Got it on time. Washed first once as a test. A-OK. Put it down in front of the sink as splashing on the bathroom floor needed a fix. It is indeed no-slip. And protects the floor. So it works. Better than our traditional knit cotton bath mats. Hence will buy a bigger one for the sink and move this rather small one for stepping out of the bath/shower. Thank you people at Gorilla!

Updated 2020-12-10: Bought a bigger size and it, too, washed in the washing machine just great. Thought it might be too stiff but no. Did not overbalance the drum and came out of the dryer great. Again: Thank you people at Gorilla! Love your glue, too...

text:
If you have always tried to have both a cat and a bath mat, you will feel me :). Mine have always put pulls all over them, they’d always end up wadded up in a corner or destroyed. Then there are the cheap bathmat problems. The rubberized bottom of the last one I got left a white rubbery residue all over the floor that won’t wash or scrub off! After a few washings, the rubber flaked off the mat completely, making the dryer look like a snow globe. Then there are the fuzzy ones that are cute for a month, then get matted and funky looking, and turn crispy in the dryer.
These are PERFECT! I love the nice chenille look, they’re very absorbent, they stay where you put them and are indestructible by cats. They wash extremely well. I have one in both our bathrooms, a small gray and a larger black, and I’m sure they’re the only brand I’ll ever buy again. Thanks!

title_review: Bought it for rice, but it's a real boon for rinsing kefir grains
text:
I killed my kefir grains a while back, so I ordered some new ones from Dom that were dried. Early in the reconstitution process, those grains were mighty small, so I'm really glad I had this rice washing bowl handy. The drain holes in the bottom are very tiny, so even those tiny kefir grains couldn't slip through. After the grains began to grow and take on curd, I found that gently rubbing the grains against the bottom of this bowl, like with a washboard but not too hard, helped liberate the grains from the curd. Then it was just a matter of tilting the bowl and letting the milky water run off through the larger slits in the pouring side.

One thing great I discovered about this bowl, which will be appreciated by wild fermenters everywhere, is that the four "feet" on the bowl fit inside a canning funnel perfectly. The drainage holes all feed directly into the funnel, then into your mason jar. How great is that? No spills!

I also like that I can leave my rice grains to sprout a little in this bowl before cooking it. That punches up the nutrition and makes the rice cook better. I'm really glad I got this bowl. It would make a very nice gift for all your mason-jar-fan friends.

title_review: Don’t let the size fool you- this is amazing!!!
text:
Well.. with the airlines struggling through Covid19, i’m pretty sure I know what they’ve been up too-
Building fans!!! Did not realize what an amazing jetstream the Amazonbasic 3 speed fan was going to give me- I AM FOREVER IN THE DEBT OF THE CREATOR OF THIS FAN...!!!

After being quarantined for far too long… I’ve begun to notice, a claustrophobic feeling- and prob. I need out but, on lockdown.. a fan was the the next best option!

For 7 inches this is small and compact but, really packs a punch. The cord length is adequate and removed from package it is ready to plug-in and go! HACK: to increase its mobility I suggest using an indoor small extension cord… This will allow you more movability as you putter around and save the searching for an outlet.

The fan is quiet but, not silent… However I would equate the sound to a methodical hum, no rattles or mechanical sounds. This could easily be used at work or, in a babies nursery and not cause any disruptions. Yet, for those who sleep best with a white noise background- this is perfect!!

Truly, I did not realize somethings so small could bring such a cool burst of relief.. and this hits the mark on every level! So much so, I ordered one for my baby sis who is 38wks pregnant, in quarantine and has no AC… When she called after receiving in tears of joy, I couldn’t think of a better endorsement!! She states this will take her thru the next 2 weeks with the ability to stay cool- and that is good enough for me!!

The only thing missing and it’s not a dealbreaker, is access door to clean the blades. However, I can of compressed air and a wet cloth will be able to help remove dust from the interior you cannot reach. Just be sure before you plug it in again the fan is completely dry 100%- safety first!!

Overall, this is worth every penny and perfect for personal use or small spaces such as dorm rooms or apartments, cubicles, bedroom.. You get the idea. I hope this info helps- feel free to let me know!

For me that's fine in many settings and this fan still has plenty use as I randomly have a use to dry something with a fan and this will be easy to move around from it's size and being so lightweight.

I've been using this to circulate heat by my floor furnace and it's absolutely pushing plenty of heat down my hallway and helping heat up the house!

This fans the same size as other box fans (20 inches) but it's slimmer and super lightweight. Which I think is pretty amazing, it's very easy to move around and not clunky like other metal framed fans. This fan would be terrific for people who have lifting restrictions and can't lift heavier things.

Overall, very happy with this!

title_review: Thick and gentle on my hair
text:
I purchased this pillowcase looking for not only a satin case, but one with a zipper in it as I hate when my pillow slides out during the night. The zipper on this one is not located at the end of the pillowcase, but a few inches below the end. This gives more strength and prevents to zipper from pulling apart or slipping stitching.

My previous pillowcases were of a thinner fabric and the last one literally began falling apart in less than a week. The fabric was so thin that the stitches began pulling the weave apart quickly. This one is so thick that there has been absolutely NO budging in the weave after one month of constant use.

I only wash this in a lingerie bag and dry it flat on my bed in front of a fan. It still has the wrinkles in it from its original packaging, but I'm OK with that. My hair is not a tangled mess by morning and my face loves the feel of this pillowcase.

I would recommend this to anyone that is looking to increase the health and condition of their hair and face. Out of 3 different companies....this is the absolute best pillowcase I have purchased!

title_review: These really do keep out the sunlight and darken the room; they are not the highest quality but they function as designed
text:
I ordered these to put up at my boyfriend's house. Years ago he purchased blackout curtains for another room and they worked very well. They were extremely expensive curtains and he does not remember what ones he purchased. As a result, he decided to purchase a set of "blackout" curtains at Walmart and they are horrible as most sunlight gets through.

It was after this Walmart purchase that I suggested he try these. These are cheaper than the original blackout curtains he purchased on Amazon years ago and are not as high quality but they do the job as you can see from the photo. In the picture, the full sun is on the window. The only light that gets through is in the line between the panels.

Since he has to sleep in the afternoon due to working the graveyard shift; it is perfect. However, I do not feel these will hold up in the dryer as it feels like it has a plastic-like backing. Nevertheless, it is rarely necessary to wash the curtains, so for the price, they are perfect.

title_review: Simple style, neutral dove grey color. A little light still gets through
text:
I replaced a set of 15 year old, true black out drapes with these. I loved my old ones because they could turn the entire room dark at noon and we're very heavy. However, the looked seriously dated and were definitely showing wear and tear.

This set is a nice, neutral dove grey color that sort of blends with any decor. The material is very light weight and a little thin. I'm using them in front of a glass French door on the North East side of the house - we get morning sun through those French doors. These block about 90% of that sunshine, but there's still a hall of light around them. On the plus side, these drapes can easily be tossed in the laundry when needed.

title_review: Very effective at light control; not all that stylish
text:
If you primarily want curtains for effective light control, these are perfect. It blocks 100% of the light, especially if you use a rod that is designed for blackout curtains (one that has a curve on the side next to the window so the curtain can wrap and seal out any light leakage on the side). These are also very effective for temp control (e.g., blocking out the sun to keep the room cooler in the summer).

They are not all that stylish, however. They are not terrible by any means, but they hang rather limply and don't dress up the room at all.

The fabric feels nice and is decently thick. There is a white liner on the window side of the blind which again, is great for light and temp control, but not so nice in terms of style.

They arrived with some pretty serious creasing. Some were eliminated by letting the drapes hang for a day, but I had to get out the iron to put a dent in the most serious ones. This material is hard to iron -- took some time to work out the creasing and even then, some creasing remained.

If you are willing to trade style to gain excellent light/temp control function and don't want to spend a lot, these are a good choice. If you're looking mostly for style, pass on these. I wanted mostly light control to keep the glare off of a TV, and these are working great for that - a solid 4 stars (1 star loss due to the stubborn nature of the creases).

title_review: Easy to Use and Works Well
text:
I selected this avocado tool (couldn’t think of a better or more descriptive name for it) to work with avocados. It’s an odd looking beast and I wasn’t sure how well it would work out but it has proven to be a worthwhile tool.

At a glance it looks like a green and gray blunt-nosed lawn dart. The gray fins are rigid while the green one is more pliable. Think of the difference between a plastic spatula and a silicone scraper in terms of hardness and pliability and that is a fair approximation on the difference in the fins. The hard blades are rounded and are suitable for scooping the flesh from an avocado hull without difficulty, while the softer blade is a good scraper. When stood upright, the whole works as a good masher/chopper.

This does not do as thorough a job as an immersion blender or a food processor, of course, but the idea here is to mash and pulp, not liquify. As designed and in its intended role, it works very well and cuts out a lot of the mashing process, saving time versus a regular mortar and pestle type of tool.

I have not used this often but it will see much more use in my kitchen as time goes on. It makes the job of processing avocados a lot easier.

text:
First the good news: The OXO avocado slicer does what it says it will do. It will cut open an avocado, help you remove the pit, and produces thin slices for your sandwich, salad or whatever. It's a nice, sturdy kitchen gadget and lives up to the OXO reputation. Unfortunately I found the grip a little awkward. Possibly it's because I have smallish hands, but cutting the avocado open was a little more difficult than it would have been with a knife. Still, I got it open which is the main thing. Don't let the fact that the blade is plastic fool you, it makes short work of tough avocado skin.

The pitter is simpler to use; place it firmly on the pit and twist, then turn the avocado half over and the pit will drop out. No more swinging at it with your knife! Yeah I know you do it; you can get a nasty cut like that! Believe me, I know. Finally the slicer slides through your avocado smooth as Cary Grant, producing slices which I frankly found a bit thin. If it made four slices instead of six I think I'd be happier with it. But heck, it makes fast work of something which I've found difficult in the past, so I'm not going to complain.

The only thing I'd say here is that unless you use a lot of avocados, this might be one of those extraneous gadgets that sits in your drawer most of the time. You don't really need it but it's cool. Still if that and the fact that I'd have designed it a bit differently are my only complaints, I think it's an overall winner. Give it a shot if you love your avocados.

text: If you live at a higher elevation like me (5k Colorado) just know that after the buzzer beeps you might wanna leave the hard boiled eggs inside the steamed cooker for another minute or two if you want the egg cooked all the way through. I also add a bit more water than the fill line says, but again that’s bc of my elevation & it evaporates quickly.  It’s not any quicker than I used to make them, but it’s a lot less water. I’m disabled & have a TBI rn so the auto-cutoff was a no-brained for me. I bought the blue bc it was cheapest.  My service 🐶  🐶 love hard boiled eggs too so we are enjoying this new addition to our kitchen.  My only regret is that I did not buy it sooner & that Amazon never has the color I want for the cheapest price, but I can live with the bb blue.  We have used it 3x & so far it’s working okay. Oh- don’t place it under upper cabinets as it has a vent hole & it will vent & it will make the cabinets sweat.  Give it some room to breathe imo.  I keep a pair of tongs handy to unload the eggs & dunk them in my ice bath. Yes. You end up using water again, but I have house plants I’ll use it on anyways so it not just wasted water.  If it holds up & doesn’t break down it will truly be one of my top 10 if not top 5 amazon lifetime purchases.  It’s that good.  Nothing is worse than watching eggs boil. Lol.  I start this up at the same time I start my tea brewing and go about feeding the wildlife in my backyard.  It’s just a very peaceful start to my day. I know ppl have said stuff about the buzzer, but honestly I happen to be hearing impaired in both ears & my service dogs are trained to hear for me. I like that it’s loud enough that if my pups are outside & I am in my living room or just outside on my patio with them & my screen door is open then they & often I can still hear it.  I wish appliances had volume options on their alarms, but until then I am very happy with this one.  I am just extremely happy with this purchase. It’s been a long time since I could say that. Lol.

text: I usually don’t have single function items in my kitchen. But I have a 9-year-old who wants boiled eggs all the time. I’m not comfortable letting him use the gas stove on his own, so I thought maybe this little device would give him some egg freedom in his life. I tried it the first time to make sure it wasn’t going to be too dangerous for him. But it was fine. I actually didn’t read the directions, so I didn’t know about poking a hole in the egg the first time I tried it. The eggs turned out fine. The second time, I stabbed holes in the eggs per the directions, but I still have no idea what it accomplished other than making weird webs inside the thing. Anyway, back to the purpose of this purchase. I explained the process to my 9-year-old and gave him warnings about how hot the eggs would be when he opened the device. He was able to cook his own eggs start to finish without help. He used a dish towel to remove the hot eggs from the tray and place them in a bowl of ice water. So now, he won’t be bugging me to boil him a bazillion eggs every day. He’ll just be bugging me to buy him a bazillion eggs. As an adult, I can get the exact same effect with a pan of water. But for a kid, this is easy and much safer than using the stove.

I purchased this on Woot! (an Amazon subsidiary), so it's not showing a "Verified purchase," but I DID buy this and I've been using it for several months. I got the cobalt blue color (not that that matters much since all colors have the same identical cooker part ... )

Anyway -- I love this!! I'm single, live alone, and I'm always looking for convenient USEFUL kitchen gadgets. I also love hard-boiled eggs -- just by themselves or made into deviled eggs.

This cooker does a great job cooking the eggs to perfection but you might need to experiment a bit to get it "just right." I tend to use extra large eggs and I've found I need more water (for a longer cooking time) to get them done to my liking. Others have mentioned this as well. Just find what works for you -- you won't waste eggs as you can always put them back into the unit with more water to finish cooking. Once I found what worked for me, I wrote a note on the outside of the cover with a permanent marker showing how much water I needed. Easy peasy.

The eggs come out easier to peel, too. I think it may have something to do with the little hole you pierce into the bottom of the egg. At any rate, I haven't had a problem yet with peeling.

Seriously, you can't go wrong with this -- great price, lots of colors to choose from, cooks 6 eggs at a time. Would make a good holiday gift. It earns 5 stars.

text: I wanted an egg cooker for hard boiled eggs. The other options are a bonus for me.  I had already read many of the reviews so I knew what I was getting. When I used the measuring cup for the hard boiled option, they come out more so like soft boiled eggs. This wasn't really an issue for me. The one thing that is a little off putting is when I used the omelet option. I used 1-2 eggs with cheese and sometimes cooked meat. I do not use the omelet level on the measuring cup. If I used it, they would not be done. I use the hard boiled egg water level. Even then, they are not cooked all the way. After they finish the cycle, I have to turn off the alarm, then unplug it. Then plug back in and add more hard boiled egg water level and cook a second time. Only after the second cook are the eggs cooked. If I were super hungry and wanted to eat ASAP, this would be an issue for me. Normally for me I am doing chores while all this is taking place. If you are in a rush, I probably would not use for an omelet. I love poached eggs but I have not used that option yet. Once I do, I will update my review.

title_review: Have a healthy breakfast - and - get to work on time.
text:
This little gem is NOT one of those small appliances I get and put on a shelf until the someday that never comes. I LOVE THIS EGG COOKER for lots of reasons. The key to me is I set it up for the eggs I want, add the level of the water for soft, medium or hard eggs -- now get this -- turn on the machine and WALK AWAY. I can go get ready for work and my eggs are ready for me in 7 minutes or less. There is no worry about the cooker causing a problem overheating because the unit turns off by itself. If I forget I cooked some eggs for some reason, I don't have to charge back home and turn it off. There is no concern of overheating and starting a fire. I appreciate that because I can eat healthier in the morning and save the expense of the drive thru with hardly a blip of time in my routine. It's a great comfort.

I've been telling friends about it. My office-mate is going to get one for her son, a budding wrestler, who likes hard boiled eggs. This is something an 8 year old can use easily.

Another reason I LOVE THIS EGG COOKER is that it makes beautiful hard boiled eggs without a fuss. It comes with a tool to puncture the shell of the egg to avoid cracking. This gives you a uniform hard boiled egg for snacks and deviled eggs. It is so easy to do 7 eggs at one time, I don't see myself ever using a pan method to hard boil eggs again.

If you are looking for a downside, here it is: It has a pretty small omelet tray which can handle a few veggies and a couple eggs. I made one attempt with just the eggs and was not impressed with my result. But I didn't try it with any fixings. At the moment, I'm not a convert from the pan. However, I'm not ruling it out when I have a little leftover veggies or bacon.

Since I was little, I loved poached eggs. I was a bit put off by the shape of the poached egg tray, being somewhat oblong. However, it is a non issue after the second time I made them. So they are not round, they taste great! Another press the on button and walk away winner.

The size of the egg cooker is rather petite for a kitchen small appliance. I would think it would work well for a singles and small families. It's about the size of a small Honeydew melon. I have mine huddled between my pot of utensils and tea pot because it gets a lot of use. It's earned it's spot on the counter.

title_review: Great results, loud buzzer that stays on till you shut it off!
text:
Great little egg cooker which consistently turns out perfectly cooked eggs, whether you want hard boiled, poached, etc. the cooked eggs are easy to peel, and the results are consistent. Mineral build up happens on the base, as it does with any similar device (eg, electric kettle). This is easy to remove by running the cooker with some vinegar in it - the minerals lift right off.

My only minor complaint about this product is the buzzer - when your eggs are done, the cooker does indeed turn itself off, but it also produces a loud, shrill, continuous alarm that will go on forever until you turn the power button off at the base of the machine. Not sure why a loud, continuous alarm is necessary when the machine already shuts itself down? Anyway, it’s a minor thing and I still strongly recommend this device for cooking eggs!

title_review: PERFECT Omelets and Hard Boiled Eggs!! LOVE this product.
text:
Can I just say, A BIG THANK YOU to Dash for their nifty little product! I love this device. It is small, so it does not take up much space. I bought the cream color because it blends in well with my kitchen colors. I've made hardboiled eggs and omelets so far and it come out great.

For the omelets, I have 2 eggs, chives, dill, mushrooms (cook them first), and chopped tomatoes, and some salt. Put a little spray on the bottom of the tray. Mix all my chopped up yummy ingredients with the egg. I used the measuring cup provided, but noticed it was not cooked enough, so I use the hardboiled egg measurement for my omelets and it comes out perfect for me.

I've purchased one one for my parents, siblings and now thinking Christmas gift for friends. Some things to remember.
1. Always turn it off by pushing the button once it the melody comes on. DO NOT UNPLUG before you do this or it will turn on the next time you plug it in.
2. Always wipe the hot element (bottom) down with a wet cloth after you are done. You can clean everything else with soap/water.

Enjoy your EGGS!

title_review: I love Dash. The egg cooker is my first love.
text:
The egg cooker is the first product I bought from Dash. It started my love affair with the Dash company and I am a serial buyer of now four different products and counting. And no, I pay for them all and have zero connection to the company. I’m just a big fan of their products.

If you want consistently good hard boiled eggs, just follow the instructions. If you want to customize your experience and be a mad scientist and play around with timing and with water temp and levels, you can do that too. But as long as you make sure to rinse the just-cooked eggs in cold water using the cute carrier, then you will get the desired soft to hard levels on the continuum of cook by using the included and equally cute water measurer/egg piercer. And you won’t hurt yourself like you would by doing the bone head move of handling flaming hockey puck eggs with your bare hands. Don’t be an idiot. Use the carrier.

I have no comment on the included omelet holder. I tried it once and found it suboptimal and more time consuming than just using a frying pan on the stove. In my estimation, it’s worth playing around with only if there is no access to a stovetop.

I like the alarm and auto shut off. I like the fact I can run to the bathroom without fear I will forget about it and burn the house down. The cooker will alert you and shut off as the water fully evaporates. But, keep in mind those flaming hot eggs will continue to cook inside the shell while you ignore the alarm. Don’t blame Dash for your being neglectful about your role as safe egg retriever.

And yes, I bought this egg cooker as a replacement for the one I bought my mother several years ago. I bought her first one soon after I bought my own. Hers aged poorly due to hard water and suboptimal maintenance, so I got her a new one. Mine has been treated with relative care and kindness and is still doing great years later.

If you live in an area with hard water, you’ll either need to use purified water or be careful about maintenance. There can be hard water deposits on the bottom or even scale build up from water sediment (in few places, but they do exist). If you have build up on shower doors that’s not soap scum, then there can be build up on the bottom of your egg cooker. But don’t be an idiot and use standard cleaning products. Do you want to eat abrasive cleansers or lime scale remover? NO, you DO NOT. Use baking soda and a toothbrush on it every so often and you will prolong the life of it. And don’t attempt to clean it while it’s still very hot. The water evaporates too quickly and leaves a pasty mess. You could also burn yourself and have only yourself to blame. See above: don’t be an idiot.

I live in an area with soft water, so I’ve done a couple of good cleans and it is still going strong. And the truth is, I had to clean it cuz I broke into mad scientist mode with it and should not have. I steamed veggies in it and tried to warm chicken nuggets. The residue of my experiments messed up the surface temporarily. title_review: Easy to Use, Difficult to Clean
text:
While this is certainly a convenient little egg cooker, my main complaint is that if egg EVER gets onto the metal plate which heats the water, it’s nearly impossible to clean off. As a result, every time you cook eggs afterwards, you get the benefit of smelling burnt egg remnants.

The good side: it’s very easy to make hard boiled eggs, medium boiled eggs, soft boiled eggs, and poached eggs. The plastic pieces are very easy to clean, very easy to store.

The bad side: the metal plate is difficult to clean if any egg leaks onto it. The beeping when it’s done is insanely loud and startling. And I mean LOUD. The first time it went off I thought the fire alarm had been triggered in my apartment.

title_review: Easy to Use, Perfectly Cooked Eggs Every Time
text: VERY easy to use! Has an auto-off timing feature which, when the water in the device is gone, it automatically shuts off. You determine the desired level of doneness of the eggs - soft boil (runny yoke), medium boil (soft yoke), or hard boil - and add a specific amount of water to the machine to achieve it. Once the water is gone, it stops cooking. Allows you to multitask and not have to worry about over or undercooking your eggs. Set it up, add eggs, add what level of water you need to cook to your desired doneness, turn it on, and walk away. A chiming alarm lets you know when it is done. It can also poach eggs and make omelets but I have not used those features yet. Cleanup is easy - wipe the heat plate down, and the lid, egg holder, and other attachments can be hand washed or put on the top rack of the dishwasher.

text:
SooOOoOoo easy to use and clean.
I've made hard boiled eggs, poached, a mini 1 egg cheesy omelet and steamed some broccoli. ALL with great results.
Tip One: 1 egg beaten to fluffiness using the round omelet tray will puff up to ridiculous heights during cooking.
I would not attempt to use 2 eggs as it will definitely make a not so easy mess to clean up.

Tip Two: After using there may be a light residue left in the metal boiling tray reservoir created by the evaporated water during the steaming.
Just use a clean 1/2 sheet of paper towel to wipe the water sweat (it will be hot, so take care) from the inside of the clear plastic lid. Then use that same warm damp towel to wipe down the metal tray and any other trays you used.
Your cleanup will be done; which in my book is the real seasoning and enhanced enjoyment of any meal.

title_review: Works well; with a couple of caveats
text:
I'm at 6250' altitude; so, water, here, boils at 200 deg. F, not 212. Meaning, one needs to add ~ 1/3 to 1/2 more water, to get the desired result; since Turn-Off is predicated on the water level lowering until the over-temp sensor kicks in, and the slightly annoying 'Finished!' jingle initiates.
A small amount of water remaining, after cycling, is normal.

Simply great for quick & handy/easy/simple boiling of eggs!
The 'soft boiled' (i.e., solid whites/liquid yolk) tray works well; but, at my altitude, required a little experimentation to get the preferred results. If you're after 'hard whites/runny yolks', like in a regular, pan-fried egg... it works... but, of course, you won't have a nice, crispy-browned bottom. :-)

The omelette function requires I over-fill the boiling surface/portion of the device pretty much up to the lower surface of the six egg-holder plate holes; but, works fine (takes 15 mins, here) - if you don't pile too many other ingredients into the two whisked eggs.
If you do... like this morning, for me - you'll end up with a somewhat runny omelette.
Best, to only add a moderate quantity of sm-cubed cheese, and maybe some minced onions (a can of chopped anchovies, with cheese cubes, went well); and to not fill the little tray past the rim (the added egg-soaked/covered ingredients sticking up, in the middle, above the liquid level).
Regardless, you won't get, again, the nice, browned skin you get with an omelette pan.

BTW - this: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B01LNFYCHM/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o03_s01?ie=UTF8&th=1
is sold as a 'milk frother' (for which it works great), but... it also works super for 'whisking' eggs for an omelette!
Makes for a uniform, excellently-firm consistency to the finished omelette!

text: I bought this egg cooker 3 yrs ago and only used it once. (My boyfriend does most of the egg cooking in our house and he is old school.) Recently, I told him I wanted to make hard boiled eggs and he begrudgingly agreed to try it. Now he's addicted. He used to fry eggs every morning to make an egg sandwich, now he makes (5) two-egg "omelettes" and puts them in the freezer for the week. You only need to use a little cooking spray, so less fat. Each omlette only takes a few minutes to cook. Now, every morning, he just microwaves an omelette (from the freezer) to make his sandwich. We also make hardboiled eggs, which we take to work for a snack. A couple of things: When it chimes (which is pretty loud so you can hear it from another room) press the button to turn it off. Do not unplug it when it chimes. You need to press the button to stop the cycle. Also, don't be surprised if you put scrambled eggs in there to make an omelette and it puffs up. It will flatten back down as it cools. You can add spices, small bits of cheese, meat or veggies to your omlette. (I wouldn't t use raw meat.) You can also make poached eggs, 2 at a time. I would highly recommend this for simple, easy cooking. It would be great for older kids or teens, if they are leery about using the stove. Or take it on vacation if you won't have a stove.

text:
I have always felt slightly deficient that I could not boil eggs in a regular saucepan without screwing them up. (Under cooked, overcooked, eggs exploded, etc.) I read a review of this cooker somewhere and decided to give a try. Much to my pleasant surprise it works really well, and if you follow the instructions pretty hard to screw up your eggs. The idea is pretty simple each egg style requires less or more cooking. There is a measuring cup included and depending on style you want you simply choose the recommended amount of water, pour it into the cooker and place your egg into the appropriate holder type. Close the lid and turn it on. Once the water has boiled off (ostensibly having cooked your eggs to the desired consistency) the unit beeps and turns off. That easy. For my personal taste I think the water amount recommendations are a bit too little leaving the eggs a bit watery, so I always add a bit more to get a firmer egg. However that being said the recommended measures are pretty spot on for the different varieties. So start with those and adjust to your own taste.
I have done hard boiled, soft boiled, and poached in the little trays. I have not used the omelet insert as it is pretty small and I would usually eat a larger portion.

!Double Thumbs Up recommendation!

BTW - Go look for the YT video for peeling HB eggs using the drinking glass and water method. Really works. I cooked 6 eggs and had them peeled and cleaned in under 2 minutes. I would rarely cook HB eggs because peeling them was such a PIA.

title_review: Convenient, but doesn't fully cook extra-large eggs
text:
I like the simplicity and compactness of this appliance. Plus, once you've set it up, you can just walk away and forget about it, until its obnoxious chime-alarm tells you your eggs are done. Except, in my case, the eggs aren't done. We buy extra-large brown eggs, and the yolks are still wet (but not runny) after we hard boil them with this egg cooker. Poached eggs are way undercooked for my taste... the whites are very runny and slimy.
My workaround is to leave them in the cooker for 4 minutes after the chime goes off. I set a common kitchen timer, and as soon as the cooker chime sounds, I shut it off and start the four-minute timer. After the timer goes off, the eggs (poached or hard-boiled) are done perfectly for me.
Again, the egg cooker chime is grating and obnoxious, and there's no workaround for that.

I had been hopeful for how useful this machine would be for our home, but it's met and exceeded our expectations- thank you!

We don't have much experience with the poaching or omelette features- only doing it once for each. The poaching possibly needed more cooking time?? It was very watery. And the omelette only appealed to my spouse. But that doesn't really matter to us- I bought it mainly to make soft/hard-boiled eggs and it works perfectly for that.

title_review: Amazing and no ear piercing sound!
text:
This thing is beyond easy to use and clean up. The newer models (what I got today 2/25/2022) do not have the awful done alarm. It has a generic phone alarm jingle loud enough to hear it in another room or upstairs. I 100% believe negative reviews are human error or being to rigid with fallowing directions to the T. I used large eggs that were fridge cold. I filled the little measuring cup almost all the way to the top (past the hard boil measurement) and then just let it cook. After cooking I moved to an ice bath to cool. The bottom of the pan was visible dirty after but wiped off with a damp paper towel.

The basic instructions are definitely for room temperature eggs and why so many had undercooked eggs. It make take some trial runs to figure out what works for you but it's definitely worth it!!!

title_review: Easy, quick 15 minute breakfast and out the door!
text:
I used to have an older egg steamer similar to this and miss it a lot. This one's perfect and gets the job done with easy clean up. Nice little jingle to let you know it's finished cooking. Marks on side of the water measuring cup are suggestions, You'll have to play around with the amount needed to achieve the desired hardness or softness for the style of eggs your cooking.

* Poached eggs without the boiling-water-on-the-stove-top mess anyone? Just spray the tray with non-stick spray and fill water cup to about the poach mark +/-. Use tongs to pick up the hot tray when done. Carefully pour the moisture off the eggs first using a utensil to keep them from sliding out, then slide them onto your plated toast. They'll slide right out! Delicious!

* Try this; Spray the pan that comes with it with your favorite non-stick spray..Use a fork to fluff and stir two eggs in it like you would for scrambled eggs. Fill water cup to about the MED mark +/-. Toast two pieces of bread. When cooker's finished use a set of tongs to pick up the hot pan, then place one piece of toast over it and turn the pan upside down placing the egg on your toast. Salt and pepper or garnish to taste, then add the other piece of toast. Makes a "fluffy" egg sandwich that will definitely fill you up!

Enjoy!

title_review: Good for cooking eggs, but one major problem...
text: I bought this because I have hardboiled eggs all the time. Yes this cooks the eggs just the way I like them and it's a piece of cake to use. The problem is after the eggs are done there is a burnt residue left on the hot plate. This problem is only when you make hard boiled eggs and not when you use the poaching tray. This seems to stem from how the cooker knows when the eggs are done. The cooker comes with a measuring cup that shows you how much water to add to the hot plate depending on how "done" you want the eggs. When the water fully evaporates, then the machines alarm goes off telling you to turn it off. Problem is, you poke holes in the eggs, some of that seeps out while cooking then that residue burns when the water fully evaporates. So, yes the poached eggs come out fine, the boiled eggs also come out great, but beware you will HAVE to clean the hot plate after every batch of hard boiled eggs. For me, simply wiping the hot plate down does not work and I have to soak it in a little vineagar and water solution. I'll keep using this because I don't wan't to put more money out but I'm not sure if I would buy this one again.
