title_review: A MUST HAVE in my kitchen
text:
I am in love with this gadget. It’s perfect for “tiny home” living or anyone living life on the go. 6 Hard boiled eggs ready in 15 minutes. This morning, I perfected 3 rounds of 2 poached eggs each time. Gifted one each for 2 other family members & 5 stars all around. Some things to mention after product use in “the kitchen lab”:
- Make sure to read all instructions throughly. Some users get so excited, they miss the part of punching a hole in the bottom of the egg (with measuring cup provided) with that end facing up before hard boiling.
- Had to add a little more water in the measuring cup than the omelette/poached water line indicates to get my poached eggs cooked to my liking.
- Clean up is easy peasy. I also make sure to wipe the stainless plate with a very damp cloth/paper towel after each use.
I highly recommend this product.

text:
Super easy, small and helping me eat healthy. I work from home, zillions of online meetings which means I often miss meals or grab something processed for a snack (yes I go on mute if eating). I'm also a vegetarian, and eggs are a great source of protein. Now what I do is hard-boil a bunch of eggs on Sunday afternoon, put in icey water after to stop the cooking. Take them out and let them dry off, and put in a bowl in the fridge. Then when I'm in a rush and need something healthy for a snack or mini meal, I grab one or two, peel them quick, cut in half, sprinkle with salt and pepper or paprika, and can eat that at my desk, no mess no silverware, no chemicals from processed food, and the eggs are perfect every time.
I've got a lot of pans and kitchen stuff so I really don't want anything extra taking up cabinet space, but this little thing has earned it's spot.

The cooking time depends a little on how you like your eggs done, but our batches take like 8 minutes. I can have a dozen hard boiled eggs in less than 20 mins and NONE of them are broken! Love it. One key is to have an ice bath ready & move your eggs quickly when the chime goes off. A small pair of tongs is invaluable for this step.

The Dash is not only easy to use but it’s relatively small and can even be taken on car trips to anywhere than has power. It takes like 3-4 tbsp of water per batch and the parts go right into the dishwasher. To clean the stainless bottom, I use a little bit of Barkeeper’s Friend and a Dobie sponge and just carefully rinse so I don’t get water into the cooker itself. Easy peasy. I like mine so much I even bought one for my 2 girlfriends for Christmas last year and they love theirs, too!

I started off by using 150% the amount of water the measuring cup states you need and letting it cook till the chime sounded. It was almost completely cooked this time. I did end up adding about 25% of the initial recommended water amount to the base again to continue cooking and that seems to make the eggs just right.

It seems that adding anything to your "omelette" (i.e. cheese, peppers, anything...) reduces the efficiency of this egg maker. As you can read below, when I put a few pieces of chopped up peppers in my omelette, it took three cycles of cooking for the eggs to get done properly.

I'm not thoroughly impressed over-all with the product, but it is easy to use and is easier to clean up than using a traditional frying pan.

As I state below in my initial review.... as long as you don't mind figuring out all the water levels, egg quantities, and time frames needed through a series of random tests.... you may enjoy this little egg-maker! You aren't going to find this info in the instruction manual.

--------------------------------------------------

First impression... This is a great idea in theory. However, they did a very poor job of delivering the "whole" product.

My personal expectations were to open this product and place a few eggs inside, fill the base with water and push a button.

To my surprise, the device says that it will do more than just hard boil eggs. It will also make omelettes and poached eggs. So I decided to have a very basic omelette for breakfast. (2 eggs with some diced up peppers)

Well... I went to the instructions to see what I needed to do. Disappointing instructions to say the least. There are no directions on how many eggs you can or should use. Just says to spray your dish with grease spray, put in your eggs, add water to the base, and turn on the power and wait for the chime.

I put in 2 eggs, added a couple of pieces of chopped peppers and turned on the machine. a few minutes later, the most obnoxious and non-ending music starts playing to let you know the eggs are done. I opened the lid and the eggs were still liquid. Edges were slightly cooked.

So I added a little more water and turned it on again. Waited for the chime..... Nope... still liquid. So I stirred up the eggs and added a full measure of water to make an omelette from the beginning again.

Third time was the charm. It finally cooked them completely. Unfortunately I didn't watch the time to see how long this took, but I would guess it took about 15 - 20 minutes to cook a very small 2 egg omelette.

My biggest complaint about this product is there lack of information on cooking different types of eggs. If you want hard boiled eggs, the instructions seem to cover this pretty well (Although I haven't attempted to make any hard boiled eggs yet.). If you want any other style of egg.... good luck guessing your way through!

I plan to try adjusting water levels from the beginning until I can setup my own # of eggs / Time table. Hopefully I can develop a method to perfect the use of the machine.

Cleaning the machine seems pretty simple. No complaints there.

Pros:

* Great idea if you can get it to cook your eggs timely.
* Easy clean up.

Cons:

* Annoying buzzer. They need to add a way to silence the buzzer (other than pulling the plug).
* Instructions are TERRIBLE
* Doesn't cook your eggs in one cycle.
* Very small unit only allows you to make about two eggs at a time (poached or omelette).
* Doesn't seem to save much cooking time.

"A" for idea. "F" for execution.

Do I recommend this product?

Well, if you don't mind playing scientist and figuring out everything on your own through a series of experiments.... why not?!? However, If you want something that you can just plug in and use with instructions, I'd probably say that this isn't going to be a fun experience for you.

text:
This is a concept of “Fast Food” eggs! Yes, it works as designed and described, making a quick and fast turn around. However, on the downside, the eggs are dry and flaky. You get convenience of rapidly prepared eggs, but you do not get the real texture and taste of a boiled eggs. Conventionally, when you boil eggs in water the protein within coagulates to form shape of the shell, however, water retains moisture and texture along with firmness of boiled egg. These rapid steaming devices makes the egg dry and loose it’s correct texture. So, I reverted back to conventional boiling practices.
However, as a very practical alternative, this is great for college students and for people who do not have time to setup a kitchen, and still can enjoy the healthy benefits of boiled eggs on run.

title_review: One of my favorite kitchen gadgets
text:
I bought one of these about 4 years ago and it's been a favorite kitchen gadget since. I use it pretty much weekly to make hard boiled eggs and they cook perfectly every single time, 100% of the time! No more peeling half the egg with the shell, no more under cooked/over cooked yolks either. It's super easy to use and it shuts off automatically when it's done cooking.

When my old gadget broke, I bought another one immediately. They come in a wide assortment of colors, too. The only reason I'm not giving this newer model a perfect rating score is that now they come with a loud alert to indicate when it's done cooking. The old model didn't have an alert which I prefer. The alert sound itself is pleasant (melodic versus an obnoxious beep) but it's really loud and it has to be manually turned off otherwise it goes off non-stop forever. I find this alert incredibly annoying and unnecessary. Even so, I think this gadget is a must-have.

title_review: Easy to use, fast, makes cooking eggs a breeze | Small footprint - excellent for small kitchens
text:
I've always avoided making eggs (except for omelettes) since I never know low long to boil them for the desired consistency.

This cute little appliance makes cooking eggs easy, quick and painless.

It comes with a small measuring cup and "pin" for making a hole in the large part of the egg.

One must use water that turns to steam, thereby cooking eggs to the desired consistency.

The measuring cup has fill lines for different consistencies, like soft, medium and hard-boiled eggs. However, this is a guideline only since cooking time will vary depending on how cold your eggs are when placed in the cooker. Room-temperature eggs will cook faster than cold ones.

I've made medium eggs whose yolks are "spreadable" and are totally yummy.

I have yet to prepare poached eggs or omelettes, but will do so soon. For now I'm enjoying being able to prepare a quick snack as needed.

This little appliance has a built-in on/off switch and timer function that sounds an alarm when the eggs are ready (this is determined by evaporation of the water you place). People complain about the loudness of the timer, but I personally like it since it is audible.

The appliance shuts off automatically regardless, which is a great feature.

Finally, this appliance has a teeny tiny footprint and is lightweight, making it perfect for small kitchens like mine. When not in use, I store it in a Ziplock bag inside of a cabinet.

Note: it's best to use distilled water. Otherwise, you'll need to clean water minerals/ residue from the heating plate more often. Not a big deal but something to keep in mind...

If you like eggs but never know how long to cook them for your desired consistency, this little Dash egg cooker is a godsend. Great value for the price, too.

title_review: Smart little gadget. Not BPA free. Do not believe reviews or Q&A responses that say it is.
text:
The device itself is a clever little device that works well. I mainly bought it for egg poaching, which it does neatly — if you add a bit more water than recommended. And make sure you hit the tray with a squirt of spray oil for easy removal.

One wishes the poaching tray had a bit more volume for jumbo eggs, and that the device auto-shut off, instead if requiring a 2nd press after the musical tone sounds.

It’s cute & clever — all parts stack neatly for storage inside its domed lid.

BUT!

In the Q&A section, there are several responses suggesting this product is BPA-free. NOPE. It is NOT BPA-free. The product contains BPA. The package is clearly labeled: "WARNING: This product can expose you to Bisphenol A, which is known to the State of California to cause reproductive harm."

Sellers are responding to this question and are trying to dodge the issue by saying that the trays/egg holders are BPA free... which is true, as far as it goes (the trays are recycling type 05 (PP), indicating Polypropylene, which is BPA-free). However this answer is deceptively incomplete. The lid is NOT BPA-free. It is a recycling code 7 (PC), indicating a polycarbonate that DOES contain BPA.

If you are trying to avoid BPA, you may wish to avoid this product.

I will be returning it.

title_review: So Simple - Eggs Benedict! LOVE IT!
text: LOVE this handy-dandy little cooker! Hubby loves eggs benedict/poached eggs and I do not-so I have always been less than thrilled with making it. However this cooker makes the whole process a piece of cake! So easy and simple to use. Instruction guide is easy to follow and not a bunch of variables or ways to screw things up. I also use it for hard boiled eggs, however I've never really found boiling eggs a huge hassle. (Just let them boil for 10-15 min & then submerge in cold water immediately after removing from water. Trick to knowing if they're done is spinning one on counter top, if it spins easily like crazy they're hard boiled & done!) BUT, I'm so happy I purchased this simply for poached eggs/eggs benedict. I've made eggs benedict on stove top in boiling water the regular way and it's always a hit or miss as to the outcome. But with this cooker no questions, perfect every time and done in 5 minutes. Clean up is a breeze! So happy hubby can now have two perfect poached eggs with little effort on my part. (I wish they could be round shaped like when I scoop them out of hot water, but that's by no means a big deal in the big scope of making eggs benedict. And I now have the time to devote to stirring that darn hollandaise sauce :-) )  WISH I WOULD HAVE PURCHASED LONG AGO!

title_review: Perfect eggs, easy to clean, pleasant alarm
text:
After reading other reviews complaining about the air-raid-siren level of noise from the alarm, I was a little hesitant to get this egg cooker, but I took a chance on it anyway.

I’m so glad I did! I followed the instructions, and the eggs come out perfectly every time, and clean-up is a breeze (I wipe a little olive oil on the trays first).

About the alarm: It’s a little loud. It’s not horrible. I wouldn’t say it’s worse than the volume of my oven timer: you can hear it clearly a few rooms over, and you maybe wouldn’t want it going off if you have light sleepers in the house, but it won’t scare 10 years off your life unless you’re REALLY easily startled. As a bonus, the chime has several notes to it… so not only does this lovely little thing make me a perfect breakfast, it sings me a song when it’s ready.

If you love eggs and hate cleanup and the fuss of making them, you need this in your life!

title_review: This may be the greatest invention in the history of mankind!
text:
That's my headline and I'm sticking to it! I recently visited my wife's family and her uncle had one of these machines on his countertop. As he's a widower, he doesn't need to cook for more than one many days. I looked at it and shrugged my shoulders. He asked if I wanted a poached egg. I said, "Sure."

The egg was delicious. Perfect, even.

As soon as we got back home, I ordered one. It arrived today, just in time for lunch. Guess what I did? I made myself an omelet!

Well, it was more like scrambled eggs. I'm not quite sure how to make it an omelet, but there's plenty of time for that. Here's how difficult this was:

1. Take some cooking spray and coat the omelet tray.
2. Crack two eggs and whisk them in a separate container.
3. Pour the eggs into the omelet tray.
4. Fill up the measuring cup to the line that says "Poached/Omelet"
5. Pour the water into the bottom of the cooker.
6. Put the top on the cooker, and push the power button.

The eggs are done when the cooker runs out of water, and the heating element then automatically shuts off. There's a nifty musical chime that rings repeatedly until you come over and turn the power button off.

No worries about overcooking things. No worries about forgetting to turn off the unit.

So, how did my omelet turn out? The eggs were light and fluffy. Really fluffy. I was shocked how big the eggs got, it was sort of like a quiche. Once the lid was removed, the eggs shrank back to what I'd have expected. They were perfectly cooked, they were delicious. I stuck the omelet between two slices of toast and cheese.

My wife saw what I did and begged me to make her an omelet, too. I simply wiped down the omelet tray and repeated the six above steps. The exact result happened again.

This is suddenly our favorite kitchen contraption! Ten stars out of five!!!

text: This is a fantastic little device that I wish I knew about years ago! The soft/hard boiled eggs always come out perfect and we love making omelets with it, as well. To me it's more like a frittata, but either way it's good. I tend to use slightly more water than it calls for and let it sit for a couple of minutes when it's done. Kind of trial and error until you figure out what works best for you. The supposed "rust" everyone is going on about is not rust. It's just mineral deposits from hard water which is why we buy a jug of distilled water and have no issues. If you don't want to buy distilled water you can simply scrub it with the stiff side of a damp sponge and it will come off. The chime when it is done cooking is quite loud but it doesn't bother me because I just walk into the kitchen, click the button off and then unplug it to reset it. No biggie. Great price too, so I'll probably giving a few of these out for Christmas.

title_review: Nifty little egg cooker that works...
text: This is a nifty little egg cooker that works.  It's hassle-free and produces perfect results every time, over and over again, consistently.  I travel extensively for my job and spend about 150+ nights a year in a hotel room.  Often times the hotel microwave is too low-powered to properly poach an egg in a microwave clam shell poacher.  This gadget produces up to 6 soft, medium or hard-boiled eggs perfectly each time.  It comes with a measuring cup/punch that allows you to add water to the unit depending on soft/medium/hard cooked egg settings.  Just punch the bottom (fat part) of an egg with the punch (contained in the measuring cup) and put the pointy end in the tray.  Cover, push a button and it plays a "song" when done (about 7 minutes for HB eggs).  Lightweight, easy to clean.  Something that actually works and fits in my checked bag or carry-on.  The only "negative" is the hotel room water occasionally stains the bottom of the unit.  No biggie, just give it a swipe with a wet wash rag or sponge.  I like this so much I bought one for the road, one for my home in the U.S. and another for where I live when not in the U.S. (Philippines - Use 220/110 converter).  For under $20.00 you've got something that works, makes sense, is easy to use.  I recommend filling the sink with water and ice to "refresh" the eggs when done cooking.  Stops the cooking process and makes it easier to peel the eggs after you plunge them into an ice bath.  Great product.  Even colors to choose from.

title_review: Easy to learn and use, small footprint
text:
Pro: 1) Has a small footprint, won’t take up a ton of space. 2) Really easy to learn how to use, and simple enough to remember. 3) Set and forget, until it chimes.

Con: 1) Will take some experimentation to figure out how long to let the eggs sit after the chime in order to get actual hard boiled eggs. When using the Hard water measure, the yolks come out on the harder side of medium, definitely not cooked all the way through but not runny. That’s how I prefer them, though, so it’s actually a plus for me. 2) The chime is awful; I’d prefer a beep. Many kitchen appliances have beeps, and I’m used to the sound. The musical chime is really startling to me. 3) Might not hold up to prolonged daily use. The plastic seems like it could easily crack, especially the lid.

I’m really glad I got this. Most of the time I see single-function electric appliances as a waste, but this has made my mornings so much easier. I’m spending more time in aggregate steaming eggs every day instead of doing 18 at once, but if you don’t have a stovetop, space to keep a big pot, don’t have an instant pot, don’t want to deal with instant pot setup, pressurizing and depressurizing, or don’t want to waste so much water in a boiling pot, this thing is a dream.

title_review: I CAN NOW PEEL MY OWN EGGS!
text:
I don’t normally write that many Amazon reviews, but I was so pleased with this purchase I had to pass on my thoughts. For all my life, I have been a big fan of hardboiled eggs but could not peel one without destroying it. For the last year or so I have been buying hard boiled eggs from Costco, that is until they were no longer stocking them no doubt to current Covid supply issues. Realizing after several weeks that the eggs continued to be out of stock, I turned to Amazon to try the Dash egger cooker.
• I found to my surprise, peeling eggs are now quick and easy. I have made several batches and they are all coming out great.
• I have found that making my own eggs was costing me less than half of what the store-bought were priced at.
• I am using large eggs whereas the store-bought hardboiled were medium size.
• I feel better that the eggs I’m eating are fresh whereas the store bought are vacuum sealed and dated to last several weeks. However, making my own, I must use them within a week’s time.
• With a little practice, the egg poacher and omelet pans work fine adding variety to your egg dishes.
• I do suggest that you poke a hole in the top of the eggs as directed. Also, like so many others that purchased this item, I quickly misplaced the measuring cup with the pin in the bottom and the handle to the egg holder. I had to buy a second unit and I now have a place where I always store these items when not in use.
Enjoy your eggs.

I got this on a whim because I've never had much luck making hard-boiled eggs in pots, and for $20 I was willing to take a flyer.

Well, I made my first eggs today and they're just fine. But I was crossed up by all my preceding reviewers who complained about the "buzzer" alarm and its volume. When this version of the gadget was done it had a nice musical tune announcing it had finished, and it took me several minutes to figure out what that music was behind the NPR program I was listening to. title_review: My Favorite Purchase for My Kitchen
text:
I have always struggled to make boiled eggs. I have either under cooked or over cooked eggs on the stove along with the eggs sometimes cracking in the pan. I thought I would try this egg cooker that I saw online that had rave reviews.

I LOVE this egg cooker. It is so easy to use it. You put the water and eggs in the cooker and wait for the timer to go off. The timer plays a song to let you know when they are done. The shells are easy to peel off which is great especially if you are making deviled eggs.

My only tips for using the egg cooker is:
* It needs more water than what is on the measuring cup. I initially followed the directions for the boiled eggs but they were under cooked so I had to experiment with the water level so it would cook the eggs the way I liked it.
* I do not use the pin to pierce the eggs. I used the pin once to pierce the eggs but it made a mess in the cooker along with the boiled eggs looked odd afterwards because the eggs ooze out of the holes.
* I put vinegar in the metal tray of the egg cooker for a few minutes after it cools down to get it clean because there will be a brown film on the bottom of it. The brown film will disappear without scrubbing it if you use the vinegar.

I would highly recommend it. I also bought one for my son for college and he loves it. It has come in handy when he is hungry and he wants an easy, fast breakfast.

text:
I bought this and it was delivered to my home on May 31st. The first couple times I used it, it worked great! Cooked the eggs perfectly, played a little tune at the end, it was very cute. I’m on a special diet where I eat lots of eggs, so I was very satisfied.

Around the third or fourth time I used it, I noted that about a centimeter in the center of the egg yolk was not cooked through. I hadn’t changed anything I was doing, I’d followed the instructions the exact same way each time. But I dismissed it as user error, maybe I HADN'T done something properly.

Fast forward to today, June 23rd (less than a month later). I was attempting to make some eggs for lunch later today. I hadn’t used it in a while because I’ve been eating away from home a lot. I did everything correctly and turned it on, then went about my morning routine and waited for it to go off.

Well, it never did. I looked over at my little egg cooker, full of six eggs, and the light was off. Except it was actually on, just very dim. My eggs were BURNT. This thing never alarmed, and never turned itself off. To be sure it was the cooker and not me, I tried again with two more eggs. Again the light turned on, then eventually went dim, with no alarm, and continued to cook the eggs.

title_review: My insights and tips.  I love it!
text:
It does what it's supposed to do. What you need to know is, there are lots of variables involved in getting the boiled egg you like. It's a matter of trial and error until you figure it out.
-- size of egg matters; the bigger the egg, the more water & time it's going to need (more than it says)
-- temperature of egg matters; whether it's lukewarm from the hen-house or just out of a cold fridge
-- your personal take on what "soft," "medium," and "hard" is supposed to be like

I started off with an Extra Large "Country Hen" brand egg (just one egg) and filled the little cup to exactly the "medium" mark. I did not puncture the egg. It steamed for around 4 minutes and the music came on. I turned off the music and let it sit in the unit another 30 seconds, then transferred it to a bowl of cold water for one minute, then started peeling it. I got most of the peel off one-third of the egg and was having trouble getting the peel off. Then I realized the egg was really, really squishy and not cooked. So, I deposited the partly peeled egg back in the unit and filled the cup to the "soft" setting this time. At the end of 2 minutes the music went off and I could see that the white of the egg looked a little firmer, so I removed the egg (with a potholder) and tried peeling it again; it was still kind of squishy. I repeated this last process one more time, filling the cup to "soft" and then was able to peel the egg; still a little difficult to peel but I was finally able to slide a spoon under the egg's membrane and got it loose. The photo is what it looked like after I placed the egg on toast and chopped it up. All I can say is it's an egg, and it came out the way I intended it, but I need to figure out the water measurement better next time so I didn't have to go through all that rigamarole. I provide this description of what I did for others who find that their egg is not quite cooked enough; you can stick it back in the unit and cook it some more! It works.

As for the unit itself, there are a lot of things I really like about it:
-- The overall shape is pleasantly round, and not bulbous or squarish like some of them. It's more organic looking with roundy legs and not stick-like legs.
-- The cord is white, not black like some other brands, and blends in better with my kitchen counter. It's not super long, but it's long enough.
-- I got the yellow one and I'm really pleased with the color; it's the same soft color as a cooked egg yolk, and not glaringly yellow.
-- The top part of the unit can be secured onto the bottom part by turning the top so that it "locks" with the bottom part; the instructions say not to do that, though, while it's cooking. But this makes it easier to lift the unit together with its top and parts inside it, instead of having separate pieces that can fall off. Some of the other brands don't have this feature.
-- The unit only cooks 6 eggs at a time, not 7 like most, but that's fine with me because I only need to cook eggs for one or two people.
-- The fact that it only does 6 eggs means that the center of the egg holder is free for a little spindle that can be placed there before cooking so you can lift the entire egg tray up and move it to cold water. Other brands don't have that.
-- The alarm is pleasantly musical and not too loud, unlike some other brands with a loud buzzer that knocks you off your feet.

Cons:
-- The measuring cup is not marked with ink, just raised indicators same color as the clear plastic. You have to hold it up to the light to see how much you're putting in there. I may order a better measuring cup for teaspoons, tablespoons, and ounces.

Anyhow, I think I've gotten the best egg cooker available. The price is right, the unit is cute, it works, even if you flub up and have to keep putting the egg back in there, even partially peeled, it will still cook you an egg. And mine came out just fine even with all that fuss. I plan on getting better at it.

I will report back if I come up with more tips.

Update after 5 uses: I decided to punch a hole in the end of the egg, and this does seem to make it just a little easier to peel. I'm using Extra Large eggs, and it definitely takes a lot more water (= longer time). I've filled the cup to the "Hard" level, as well as a little above that, and the egg comes out more like soft/medium-boiled (but not runny). I don't leave it in the machine; I take it right out and lower it into a bowl of water with ice cubes for a minute. Every morning I can look forward to an egg now, without the hassle of getting out pots and pans and trying to guess how long the egg is going to take or winding up with a harder or softer egg.

text: Does this make convenient easy-to-cook eggs?  Sure.  Are you going to have to fiddle around with the water level depending upon original temperature of the eggs, size of eggs, personal preference?  Yes.  But does it make a perfectly cooked egg?  Definitely not.  Everyone knows that when you boil eggs, you never actually "boil" them.  You simmer them.  High temperature creates a rubber-like texture.  Well, this cooker boils (steams) the eggs at 212°F.  If you value convenience, this is for you.  However, if you prefer perfectly cooked velvety soft boiled or poached eggs?  Go sous vide, and cook them around 50 degrees cooler.

title_review: Works great.. easy to make hard boiled eggs
text:
I bought this product to make hard boiled eggs easier. I bought the one that does 6 .
I love deviled eggs but HATE when eggs are NOT cooked through properly & especially when shells stick to the white while peeling them! This stops that pain issue, so I make deviled eggs more often, as well as just hard boiled to eat more often.
This is easy to use & is timed so you can go about doing other prep for breakfast or other… then ends automatically when eggs are done. . Sound alarm goes off.
After eggs for hard boiled is done, I found if I add additional 2 mins, I use stove timer on .. letting eggs sit in unit longer, this makes egg perfectly done with no bit of dark yellow yoke.
Best is the peeling off shells … they don’t stick!
My husband ended up loving it as well for his eggs in morning.. no boiling, guessing & turnout perfect each time..( extra 2 mins sit time). He gets his toast & pour through coffee ready while eggs are cooking.
The best kitchen tool added recently. Love it.
I also made soft boiled & is great. Again no worry on timing, be busy preparing rest of meal. I learn about this cool tool from my friend who also hated egg issues when making deviled eggs. So glad she shared this product.

text:
It does great job for boiled eggs, poached eggs and omelette. I tried many times without failure. I am not sure why many people have bad experiences. A few tips to help you get the desired results:
- use room temperature eggs
- if you use ice cold eggs from refrigerator, add 10% or 20% water to the measure cup
- do remember to spray a bit cooking oil and spread to the poaching or omelette tray first
- for omelette, be sure to beat the egg (1 or 2) very well in a bowl first
- when it's done (music alerted you, then you press the front button to turn music off), LEAVE the eggs in for a few more minutes, let the steam continues to work at it a bit more
- the alert music is not loud at all for me. if the highest ring tone volume for a mobile phone is 10, I'd say this alert music is like 3 or 4. If you can help it, cook it in a different room or in garage

text:
I love this thing, but it has some quirks you have to learn to work around. I use it to make hard boiled eggs at least once a week and then move them to an ice water bath until they cool down so the shell comes right off. Don’t leave the machine under or facing your cabinets or it could cause problems for your varnish as the steam comes out pretty steadily.

I have learned to overfill the water by about a teaspoon or two or hard-boiled eggs come out a little less than hard-boiled, etc. I have not tried to poach eggs yet.

We also use it for ‘omelettes’, which really come out more like egg patties for breakfast sandwiches. I do wish that the omelette tray was metal instead of plastic. I overfill the water a little and let the patty sit for about an extra minute after I turn the machine off so that it cooks a tad bit more.

Don’t let the brown residue build up much on the metal plate or it is harder to remove. I take a magic eraser to it after each use and then wipe it with a wet paper towel. Some of the whiter spots on the metal are permanent, but the brown stuff usually wipes right off. The plate does not actually contact the food though, so it doesn’t have to be perfect.

title_review: Works great and shells peel easily!
text:
We used to get eggs with several plans for them. But unless it was for baking, we often ignored them until just before the Use By date because we never wanted to deal with boiling or the pain of peeling them. I saw this contraption, added it to my wishlist hopefully, and received it as a gift.

We actually use our eggs before the date now! It's quick, super easy to use, easy to clean, and it makes peeling so much easier! You can even add cheese, pepper, bacon bits, or whatever else you want to each egg!

Things to note:
*It is semi loud but tolerable to me. I would definitely be next to it when it goes off to press the power button if someone is sleeping, though!
*I recommend lightly oiling the poaching/omelette accessory...the eggs tend to stick if you don't.
*For poached eggs, I fill the water halfway between the medium and hard boiled line...the one time I filled to the poached line, the whites were still pretty runny. The line for hard boiled works perfectly for hard boiled, though.

text: This is my second Dash Egg Cooker. My first one’s timer shut off malfunctioned after several years of use and sitting for a number of months when I was eating mini quiches for breakfast. Love this new one!  It has a melodic chime to tell you when it has finished cooking, which is so much nicer than the buzzer of my previous one!  I have been using distilled water in it rather than tap water as I used with my first one which eliminates the mineral build up on the heating surface. Unfortunately, I spilled some of the raw egg white into the cooker when I was placing the poaching tray into the cooker once which I didn’t realize happened until it was cooking my eggs. I thought at first that I hadn’t rinsed all the soap off the bottom of the tray when I washed it after the previous use, but realized what had actually happened when I was cleaning it afterwards. I am much more careful placing the poaching tray in the cooker. I highly recommend the Dash Egg Cooker!  I also recommend using distilled water in it as that will save you from having to clean off mineral buildup from the heating surface!

text:
I've made soft boiled and poached eggs so far, and they've turned out perfectly. This is such a neat little gadget and it takes up next to no counter space! I love how there is basically no need for directions (though they are provided with detail), because all you need to do is add water according to what you want. The timer goes off LOUDLY, but I must not have read the instruction manual because I thought it was someone's phone alert.

Additionally, due to the high high heat of the device, I recommend hard boiled eggs (rather, all eggs cooked in shells) be immediately put in an ice bath if not used right away as they will continue to cook. Another thing is that the poached eggs will have a small layer of water on them. Nothing that will ruin a dish, but I have yet to figure out how to get rid of the water and NOT break my egg (oops).

The recipes included look great, and this is aesthetic enough to earn its place in a visible spot. It's also great for my ADHD (executive dysfunction and time blindness) because I get to set something and leave it until the timer goes off. No more ugly poached eggs or separating the whites.

10/10, recommend for foodies, unskilled cooks, and people with executive dysfunction.

text:

For example: I wanted soft boiled eggs, so I filled the included measuring cup to between soft and medium. What came out was too soft. The whites were runny. So much so that I fed it to my dogs when it cooled down.

I really want to know why only half of the unit boils.

title_review: Was skeptical, but wow, it worked
text:
first impression at unboxing was, this is a cheap piece of plastic, will it work. hmmm, ok, so I read the manual and the next morning followed the instruction for 4 hard boiled eggs. It cooked them in about 8 minutes. (old fashion way was 15). ok, so half the time, that is good, but will they be cooked through, I was surprised, but they were. Oh but wait, what about the finish timer screeching. It really wasn't that bad. maybe they changed the sound from something in the past, but it was not bad at all. So what about cleaning. no problem. I have hard water at my house, so it did leave a mineral deposit, but it cleaned up with a paper towel and vinegar. Use distilled water if you want to avoid this. Lastly, what about lid durability. Wellll, I put in on my counter top to dry and reached for something else and it fell on the ground (4') crash!!! well, it is plastic, so it was fine, no cracks. yikes, glad it didn't break. Still, I would recommend being careful, it is lightweight plastic. So overall, I was impressed with how this little $20 gadget performed. We'll see how it goes over the next few months. IF you want something a little better made but for double the price, then I'd think about the Cuisinart, it is all metal and reminds me of what my mom has been using for 40 years.

Bottom line: for $20 this really does work for hard boiled eggs. I'll try to poacher and omelette feature another day

title_review: Great Invention - Well Worth the Price
text: My husband was having trouble getting his soft boiled eggs the way he likes them.  My son had bought this egg cooker and told me how much he liked his.  Got this for husband's birthday.  One thing we liked:  the instructions were so easy to follow and had color photographs that anyone could figure out.  So many products come with poor instructions and often use international symbols rather than words.  It has a measuring cup that shows how much water to use for each type of egg:  soft boiled, hard boiled, poached or an omelette.  You can adjust how hard or soft egg comes out by either using a bit more water or less water.  Also you can leave the egg in a bit longer after the timer chime goes off.  With a little trial and error, you can get your eggs to turn out exactly to your specifications!  Also, poached eggs usually stick to metal egg cups but with this plastic poaching tray,  the cooked egg slides right out with the use  cooking spray as suggested.  Cleans up easily.  As with anything, if you read the directions first, you won't have problems as these directions are very good.  Also, we have not found that it rusts as someone mentioned.  It does leave a mineral residue if your water has minerals in it.  This residue can be easily cleaned off.  Good value for your money.

title_review: I hope this review helps others when purchasing
text:
I primarily purchased this for poaching eggs because I suck at doing it in with the regular boil pot method and I figured this would simply making eggs Benedict. AND IT DID!

BUT however, it’s tricky so read carefully the instructions. I wasn’t going to leave a bad review due to user error since it has taken a few tries to perfect this little handy machine.

Main tip is to use eggs that are not directly from the cold fridge. Let them sit out at room temperature for 10-15 minutes before using them however in the cooker, for any way, whether it’s hard boiled, scrambled, or poached, the result is better with eggs that aren’t straight from the cold fridge.

With hard boiled, the egg peels so much easier than the traditional way and I’m super thankful for that.

It does rust a tad bit after use, but I did the vinegar trick, leaving it in the bottom for 5 minutes and it cleaned up like new easily with a towel!

My only reason for 4 stars and not 5 is just the chime is super annoying. I read that they updated it from an alarm to a “cute” chime, but it’s still annoying and I just turn it off so I don’t hear it’s anymore.

Overall, this is a fantastic little product and I definitely recommend it, but be sure to read the directions!

text:
I am an instant fan of this adorable egg cooker. I found out about it only a few days ago and I am so happy I got this.

To start, my boyfriend suffers from a highly sensitive egg allergy, to the point where if he's in the kitchen while someone is frying eggs he will feel unwell from the fumes. As a result, I gave up cooking eggs for myself for over 5 years.

This device is a blessing because I can finally eat eggs again without worrying about bothering my boyfriend. I might not ever make fried eggs again but being able to enjoy them boiled, poached, or as a tiny omelette is more than enough for me.

The domed lid keeps the "fumes" contained pretty well until I have to open it, but since all the cooking is steam powered it's really not bad. This morning I attempted soft boiled eggs and as you can see I think they turned out wonderfully. My boyfriend didn't notice any discomfort in the kitchen either.

So so happy this is in my life. It's very easy to clean and I love that you can set it and forget it, since it plays a little tune when it's ready.

I love this product. I didn't expect it to be that great but I have been so happy with it
There was a short learning curve where I had to figure out how much more water to add to compensate for the lower boiling point of water at 7000 ft.. If you aren't happy with the consistency of your egg add more water. I added more the first time out and a little more the second time because the whites were too runny on my first try. Also, since I cook mine directly from the refrigerator I think I would add a little more water even if I were not at high altitude. You just need to give them a little more cooking time and that's how you do it - adjust the amount of water.

title_review: Makes perfect eggs of all types
text:
I’m not one to have a lot of specialty appliances in my kitchen. But I love this little egg cooker. I’ve never been able to reliably make medium soft or poached eggs—now every batch is perfect. Hard-boiled eggs also perfect.
After reading many reviews with hints for use, I second-guessed the directions and made changes from the recommendations in the product. What I found was that using eggs straight out of the frig and following the exact directions made the best eggs. Egg size, frig temperature, ambient humidity and personal preference for yolk softness are going to vary. So try the exact directions to start; you might be surprised how easy it is.
One note: I’ve always put my in-shell cooked eggs immediately into ice water to facilitate peeling. This step is still needed.

Update: still very happy with this cooker. A few reviews mentioned rust on the heating base. Though there is brown stuff on the base after use, it’s not rust. It’s cooked albumin from the egg white , leaking from the tiny perforation you place in the top of the egg. It cleans off easily with a non-scratch abrasive side of a sponge. title_review: Not good for soft boiled or poached
text:
I bought this for soft boiled and poached eggs. (I only like solid whites). I’ve used this probably a dozen times now and I still can’t get it right. I’ve followed the directions exactly. I tried poaching twice and both times it was undercooked with runny whites- retried them and of course overcooked. Every time the soft boiled egg is either overcooked to the point of hard boiled or so undercooked that the shells are ripping off the white and the innermost white and uncooked yolk are dripping in my hands. I’ve tried using more water, less water, I’ve tried letting it sit in the steam for a minute or two after, I’ve tried taking it out and letting it sit for a minute or two. I’ve left it in the ice water for various amounts of time after as well. I’m using fresh, large eggs, either one or two at a time. I’m tired of struggling with this and only seeing positive reviews. I do not understand what I’m doing wrong.

I also posted this as a question, and if I get any helpful pointers that guarantee me a good soft boiled egg (solid whites, runny yolks) then I will change/delete this review.

Update: no helpful responses. I returned it. Great for hard boiled I guess, bad for everything else. If it was only advertised for hard boiled, I’d give it more stars, but seeing as they promised easy and perfect soft boiled and poached and can’t deliver, it’s one star. For poached and soft boiled, it’s easier and more reliable to just use a pot on the stove.

text:
We always boil jumbo sized eggs and like our eggs cooked medium, meaning a fully cooked white with partially soft yolk. We may never use the poaching tray or omelet bowl.

Our first use of the Dash Rapid Egg Cooker with six jumbo eggs resulted in perfect eggs. This was after reading the manual, slightly overfilling the water level past the medium mark, and leaving the eggs in the cooker an extra minute after the buzzer sounded. The result was a yolk that was just between runny and hard, which is exactly what we like. So why only four stars?

Our previous two egg cookers which lasted us approximately 10 years together were branded Sunbeam and Salton respectively but were exactly the same machine which were oval/rectangular in shape vs. the round Dash. We believe they are now out of production/unavailable. We're comparing this Dash model against them.

Dash positives:
- Cute (wife wanted red)
- Easy cleanup of metal cleaning plate

Dash Neutral:
- Pretty chime vs. very loud buzz in the old model

Dash negatives:
- Jumbo eggs fit on the boiling tray tightly packed with no space between them
- Egg piercer is very thick - double the thickness of our previous models. Why a two-piece egg piercer?
- Imprecise water measuring cup - guesswork left to user (with the price of eggs yet!)
- Boiling tray handle remains in cooking area - very hot to handle when lifting out completed eggs

Compared to our old model, which is no longer available, the Dash comes up short in these areas:

- Our old model had very precise water measurements on its one-piece cylindrical measuring cup with incorporated egg piercer for 1-6 eggs, labeled with soft/medium/hard markings for any quantity. There was no guesswork involved.
- The lift handles on our old model were outside the cooking area which allowed a cool grab of the boiling tray when the eggs were done.
- With jumbo eggs there was space remaining between the eggs.
- The egg piercer was half the diameter of the Dash model, meaning no major ‘crunch’ resulting in various sized holes as with the Dash.

Limiting this Dash review to four stars because we have yet to resolve what guesswork may be involved in cooking fewer than 6 eggs. We plan to update this review accordingly.

Just curious: While the Dash has a pleasant chime vs. the extra loud buzzer on our old model, why not incorporate an auto shut-off along with the buzzer/chime?

title_review: LOUD Sing-Song but Perfect Boiled Eggs
text:
So I bought this device because I'm lazy. I admit it. But I also had been considering taking it to my office where myself and four other ladies like to make free meals during the week. We all love eating eggs. Morning or Lunch.

After I bought it I had to test it out and so far; it's been great. I've used it SEVERAL times to get the most PERFECT hard boiled eggs. Each time I've done it and even completing two-dozen in back-to-back rounds. It worked like a charm.

The eggs once chilled and ready to be peeled have been an breeze. No crazy 'hacks' of vinegar in the water or baking soda. Just an ice bath to cool and stop the cooking process and peel. Lovely.

The -ONE- drawback is I also love me some poached eggs. I have not, in my 25+ years of cooking experience (I was a late bloomer here), been able to perfectly poach an egg using any other 'tips/tricks/methods/hacks'. So I was excited to use the poached egg feature on this machine. Ran two eggs through and the tops looked PERFECT. I was so egg-cited. But sadly, they were only half cooked through. The bottom half was all uncooked egg and I could not enjoy my breakfast.

Now, I did read a comment here from someone who has a great point; I was trying to poach eggs directly from the cool fridge. So maybe a combination of slightly warmed eggs and touch more water will improve this function of the machine for me. I shall give it a couple of test runs and return with an update.

For now, I love the machine even if it's just for hard and medium boiled eggs. It's been fantastic and I plan to use it a TON more. ESPECIALLY with Easter around the corner!

OH and the 'loud shriek' is not a shriek. For my machine (maybe just the newer version) it's a song. An extremely annoying and LOUD song but it gets my attention while I'm wandering my kitchen and house listening to my audio books on headphones. And there -IS- a way to silence it now.. turn the machine off. It's what I do. :)

text: I've been using this for over 3 years and still love it! I got fed up with egg white adhering to the shell so tightly that I was left with ugly pockmarked peeled eggs and a lot of wasted egg white attached to shell in the trash. This marvelous piece of equipment really does work, and I now have beautifully peeled eggs. I actually haven't used any of the accessories--I only make soft-boiled eggs--but it's nice they're available if I become adventurous. The alarm truly is loud enough to scare the bejeezus out of anyone, so I actually keep my finger on the button when the time nears for the buzzer to sound, so I can save my nerves (and ears). Though I use only distilled water, I still periodically have to soak the heating surface in white vinegar to remove deposits that form. A minor inconvenience for all the convenience this item offers.

title_review: Water level not correct- badly cooked eggs
text: In the instructions they say eggs should cook for 7-9 min for soft boiled (and other times are listed as well).  These times are nowhere near what the water level gives you.  For example, the first time I had two eggs and enough water for "medium".  The cooker ran dry in 5 minutes, and the eggs were basically raw.  I experimented a bit, and found that 1/4 cup takes about 8 min to run dry, and 1/3 cup takes about 11 minutes.  Further, the water only boils on one side creating hot spots- you have to be careful about placement in the rack- kind of a pain; I will probably go back to a frying pan.

text:
This egg cooker is a dream. I've always used a boiling pot of water to hardboil eggs for salads and egg salad but I've been using farm-fresh eggs lately and they are VERY difficult to peel when cooked in boiling water. The steaming method of this egg cooker allows super easy peeling of hardboiled farm-fresh eggs. I have adjusted the amount of water I add to the cooker to get the amount of time to my liking, but that's easy - just add a little more water to get more cook-time, less water for less cook-time.

The device itself is small and easy to store. It fits compactly in a little gadget drawer with my handmixer, electric chopper and pourover coffeemaker. I have wellwater, so the heating surface isn't easy to clean but that's due to the water hardness. The chime noise it makes when it's done is not obnoxious like others have reported, so maybe they fixed that.

This egg cooker is simple to use, compact to store and makes cooking eggs very easy - highly recommend!

title_review: Nifty little gadget!  And no more loud alarm, now it's a chime
text:
Even though I am not big on single-use machines, I'll make an exception for something I can really use, like my Zojirushi rice cooker. I love eggs and I'm forgetful, so this little machine was a perfect solution.

So far I have made hard- and soft-boiled (my favorite!) eggs following the directions, and they came out perfectly. Poached eggs required a little tweaking; following the directions got me eggs that were slightly underdone, so I increased the amount of water called for by half again and got perfect, slightly runny, delicious poached eggs. I haven't tried the omelet (more appropriately a frittata) pan yet, but I have plans to.

And the horrible "alarm" sound of previous reviews is gone! Now when the eggs are done, there is just a soft, pleasant chime to let you know.

Steaming eggs, as this machine does, is healthier than frying, and if you have a tendency to let your eggs boil too long on the stove or to forget and over-poach them, this egg cooker has you covered. title_review: I should have bought this years ago
text:
I love this thing. I love hard boiled eggs but often don't eat them because of the hassle of making them. When I do make them, I tend to not eat all of them, or by the time I do, they have lost their flavor. With this egg cooker I can make them on demand with pretty much zero effort. I also love fried eggs over medium but it's such a pain to always get out the frying pan etc... I just make medium boiled eggs with this and it's pretty much the same! I tried doing the poached eggs, but could not find the best amount of water/time to get them cooked right. I could get the yolk perfect, but the underside of the egg white was still runny. Added more water and the yolk was almost completely cooked and the underside egg white was till runny. Not a big deal because again, I get exactly the cook I want with the medium boil and can do more eggs at a time.

I would have paid triple for this item it's that good. I don't really understand the negative reviews about the timer. It is loud, but not obnoxious and I can hear it anywhere in the house. The melody is fine, it took me a few times to realize it was the egg timer and not my phone ringing.

text:
I enjoy using the cooker. I got the updated version with a pleasant chime at the end of cooking. The color I chose was yellow. I like how simple and cute the cooker is! It is very small and easy to clean. A single button is used for on/off, so there are no timers to deal with. The amount of water you pour onto a cooking burner, and how fast it evaporates, determines your end result. It’s basically a tiny steamer.
I’m really happy making eggs in the morning and not worrying about the timing (as in, “a minute too late in a pot, and your soft-boiled egg is ruined”).
Within a week, I tried all the cooking modes. I used large eggs right out of the fridge. Here is what you need to know: this cooker still does not get the timing right (it matters how big your eggs are, and also their temperature). I wish it were a “fuzzy logic” cooker, similar to a rice cooker, but then it would probably be more complicated to use, and also more expensive. It’s no biggie, however, just know that you need to put your omelette and poached eggs through two cycles (add a little less water than during your first cycle, so it evaporates from the burner plate a little faster). For omelette, the maximum dish capacity is 2 eggs plus a splash of milk, beaten; I also added one diced tomato, some parsley, and feta crumbs. The end product, after 2 full cooking cycles, is a smooth and spongy egg patty, similar in taste to an egg cup.
The poached eggs (one in each half of the enclosed dish) also required additional cooking time. They came out nice and neat. Don’t forget to use the cooking oil spray beforehand for easier release.
Medium- and hard-boiled eggs (pierced per instructions) came out perfectly cooked and were easy to peel after one cycle. If you want a semi-soft egg to use in ramen, for example, you would probably use the medium-boiled egg mode and keep it in the cooker for a minute more after turning the power off.
Overall, it’s a small and inexpensive product that multitasks; I am happy with it for what it offers, at such a low price.

text:
UPDATE: I have used the egg cooker every day and have tweaked the water for the exact outcome I am wanting.

Using bottled distilled water was the answer. We have well water and have a filter and softener. Apparently the minerals or softener caused the slight scorched water in the base. It didn’t happen with the distilled water.

It is much smaller than I expected. The size would make it also perfect for a dorm room or a travel camper situation.
The little music chime when finished cooking is cute.
I used some of my really big fresh counter eggs. They touched the side of the dome lid. So egg size mattered a bit.
I haven’t tried the omelet pan or pouched egg pan and probably won’t. My primary reason is for boiled eggs. Particularly soft and medium boiled eggs.
I made hard boiled first and they came out perfectly without the ugly green rim around yolk from an over cooked egg.
I then tried medium boiled eggs. That has required a bit of a learning curve. I am having an issue figuring out how much water is needed to the the white cooked but the yolk still creamy. I am getting closer. I’m sure the egg size and the egg temperature (I keep mine at room temperature) may all play a factor.
The lid boiled water out one time but I think that may be due to a cracked shell.
I noticed there is brown scorched residue on the stainless steel heater plate. We have soften well water that may be h tho e cause. It is easily remedied by a small bit of baking soda and white vinegar. I will try getting some distilled water and see if that fixes the issue.
All in all it is a handy little egg cooker. I would and have recommended.

title_review: No better way to hardboil eggs
text:
This is our second one. They both work perfectly. They use about 3 tablesppons of water. More water results in firmer yolks. Add water half way above the medium line on the supplied cup so yolks are orange (i.e. somewhat soft). When all the water is evaporated a chime sounds and the eggs are done. Lift the egg holder with all the eggs out and put it in a bowl of tap water. Wait a minute and peel.

When cooking only 1 or 2 eggs, a little more water is needed to reach the same softness because the water boils off a bit quicker.

Contrast that with the conventional way of boiling a lot of water for a longer time and having to worry about timing to get the eggs just right. This egg cooker is a big energy saver.

title_review: Easiest way to make perfect hard boiled eggs
text:
Makes up to 6 hard boiled eggs perfectly and with minimal effort. Just follow the instructions. I myself went on YouTube and watched several people demonstrate using theirs. It takes about 16 minutes which sounds longer but really isn't when You count the time it takes just waiting for the water to start boiling. That's the beauty here... No watching, waiting for water to boil. Measure the amount of water. Place eggs in, cover and push the button to start. As soon as the water evaporates the device will shut off and continue to ding until the button is pushed again. Unplug, cool eggs in ice water and enjoy.. Egg shells peal quick and easy every time.. Also device heating element cleans super easy with some vinegar
and paper towel in between each use. TIP: When the alarm chimes indicating eggs are done it's important to place eggs in cold water quickly or eggs will continue to cook. Also if You don't shut it off the chiming will stop on its own but be aware as soon as the unit cools down it will turn itself back on again so be sure to tend to as soon as it chimes. Also I suggest unplugging as soon as You turn it off just to be safe. And cleaning each time is super easy but allowing build up can get very hard if not impossible to clean..I super recommend this gem to everyone!!
Good luck and enjoy!!

title_review: bought two, both failed out of the box, in a potentially dangerous manner
text:
We had an Elite version of this same design for 5 years, which had no buzzer, but otherwise worked well; but plastic became brittle and started cracking. This Dash looked to be identical, except it claimed it had a buzzer, and it sacrificed the egg slot in the middle for a better lid.
Out of the box, both failed to work: they started heating the water, the light went off (but no buzzer sounded), yet plenty of water remained and the egg was not cooked; if left on, it would start heating again and finish evaporating the water, but would not shut off... No buzzer or bell ever sounded.
Unusable and potentially dangerous, due to the restart of heating and no subsequent shutoff.
Calling the Dash service line twice (once for each) got us the same answer twice: "don't talk to us, just return it to Amazon". Which we did, but which does not say much for their customer service -- they did not even ask about the specifics.
Buy something else!

it's smaller than you think it will be - each time I take it out of the cupboard, I'm surprised all over again. It cleans up easily and is very easy to use. Turn the egg upside down and put the puncture hole on the same side air sac. Most people wanna put the egg with the pony side up I.E. air sac down, but by putting the air sac on top as the egg expands it simply pushes the air out of the sac. So bottom line poke on the more round in and face up.

Don’t make the same mistakes I have. text:
This product initially seemed great. My son is on the spectrum and this product was easy enough for him to use and have something he could cook that made him feel more independent while being safe enough to do so.

However, we have used it a total of 7 times since April. The last time there seemed to be no issues. When I went to use it today (To make deviled eggs for a 4th July BBQ), the timer never went off. I am unsure how long it sat there before I realized that they should have been done by now (It typically takes 15 minutes before the timer goes off), and I opened it up and all the water had been boiled away (which is typical), however, the bottom of every single egg and the bottom silver part of the tray was burnt.

I thought, well maybe I just didn't hear the timer. I let the unit cool down, cleaned it out, and then started another set of 6 eggs. This time I put an additional timer on the microwave for 12 minutes from the time I pressed the start button. When it went off, I went to check and I could clearly see again, all the water had been boiled away and the eggs were beginning to burn, as was the bottom of the tray again.

So, not only has the timer failed in this unit after 7 uses, but the unit has begun getting way way way too hot to cook eggs properly. I watched it for a third time and the unit boiled away all the water (even when I put more in than the recommended) within 6 minutes.

I bought a fire hazard. This could have ended so so differently. Frustrated, its a month after the return period, so I've just wasted money for a potential fire in my kitchen.

0/5 Do Not Recommend.

I use it probably 4-5 days per week.  It ships with a small graduated plastic tube with measuring marks on the side for "soft", "medium", and "hard" boiled eggs.  You add water up to the line for the hardness you want and pour it into the base of the machine.  Insert eggs, cover, and turn it on. title_review: I am rarely compelled to so easily
text: I have to be honest, I picked up my cooker at a flea market used so I am not a verified purchaser.  I had been curious about these for several years but never bought one because I was skeptical. Well let me tell you, as a person who loves boiled eggs and deviled eggs, you cannot find a better or easier product. I know it sounds elementary and that boiling eggs really isn't that difficult etc..., however this is a game changer. Often when I would boil eggs I would either overcook or undercook or the shells would peel off half of the white as I was peeling them. I have prepared somewhere in the neighborhood of six dozen boiled eggs in this device, and I can only recall one of the eggs that was even remotely difficult to peel. They all came out absolutely perfectly cooked the way I wanted them, and it takes exactly 16 minutes for hard boiled eggs. Clean up is a snap with just some simple soap and water and a scrub pad or brush. The only downside to this that I can think of is that sometimes, and probably because of my water quality, the eggs and up with a slight brown discoloration on the bottom of them. I was also warned in advance that using the little device that comes with it to poke a hole in the egg prior to cooking, works perfectly. So don't think you have to chisel out a larger hole. The little pinprick that it makes in the Shell works perfectly fine. If you have a need for boiled eggs or just enjoy boiled eggs I cannot encourage you enough to pick up one of these items.

title_review: A gimmick. Takes as long or longer than boiling
text:
I was excited to not have to fret when I made soft boiled eggs.

Right away I noticed it seem to take a long time. And if you use large eggs, you definitely need more water than they suggest. The cook time is linked to when your water evaporates, so more water, longer cook time. Then the alarm goes off.

So finally I timed it, to get the perfect soft boiled egg if you use LARGE (not small, not extra-large) takes 13 minutes. A hard boiled large egg takes a 18 minutes. And more water than the little container even holds.

Using the regular boil in a pot method on my stove takes 2 minutes less, respectively.

If you like gadgets or don’t cook much and need to help, buy it. Otherwise, it’s a cute idea, but takes up more kitchen space, storage space, and eventually is one more thing headed to a landfill. And it takes longer.

Check it for yourself. Or just don’t bother if you’re on the fence :)

text: This is awesome.  Clearly one can make hard boiled eggs in a pot.  But somehow this is so much easier.  Here is the deal:  You take it out, you measure out in a provided measure how much water to put in it (more for hard boiled, less for omelets or soft-boiled, you use the provided poker to put a small hole in the egg, you place it (up to 6) in the holder,  you put on the lid, you plug it in.  When the water is all gone, a gizmo trips and a noise becomes audible.  The unit turns off.  You (well this is what I do) pick up the eggs (careful as they are friggin hot!) and put them in some cold water to cool. Then into the fridge.  You wipe down the heating surface with a moistened paper towel (as minerals from the evaporating water collect).  Then you enjoy the eggs.  It is really easy peazy.  Mention from other reviewers of an offensive audible warning that the cooking cycle is done is just not right.  Maybe the manufacturer changed the noise to something less problematic?  Who knows. But in this day and age where we all perhaps snack too much, so we are looking for healthy snacks that are simple to grab, this is the bomb.  Highly recommend it.

text:
The reviewers complaining about overdone/underdone eggs are missing some important information: cooking eggs to perfection is all about temperature and time. The difference between soft-boiled and hard-boiled is just how hot the egg gets and for how long. If you start with eggs from the refrigerator you will need more time than eggs at room temperature to get the same effect. If you dunk your eggs in cold water as soon as they're done you'll need more time than if you just let them cool off naturally, because the interior of the egg is still cooking for a bit after the heat is no longer applied. If you leave the lid on the unit while the eggs cool you will need less time than if you remove the lid.

I like medium-boiled eggs, and my eggs are in the refrigerator at 38°F. I use 40 mL water and remove the cover when done to let the eggs air cool. Perfect every time. If I dunk the eggs in cold water right when they're done the yolk is still runny. The bottom line is that you will have to do a little bit of experimentation to find perfection for yourself, but once you find it this machine makes it easily repeatable.

The one annoyance about this thing is the loud alarm when the eggs are done. It's loud and continuous until you shut off the machine. There is no apparent way to disable it.

title_review: Cool device, but overhyped. See notes...
text:
[[VIDEOID:e5c918b28ea0f30cb3103ea9e2366439]] I kept hearing about this device, and it looks really cool, too... so I was delighted when my mom gifted this to me over the holidays.

Some pros:
1. The "ready" sound is beautiful! I've heard from others before that their older models had a really alarming, scary sound... so I'm glad this improvement has been made. (Though I also wish you could change the setting so that you can adjust WHEN the sound happens, depending on how you want to cook the eggs... similar to an Instant Pot. Right now the sound default happens when the eggs have been cooked / water has evaporated).
2. It works. That's the biggest thing, right?
3. I didn't realize you could also make an omelette or poach eggs in this, with the included accessories.
4. The packaging and design is quite cute and clever. From a marketing standpoint, their customer engagement on social media is also pretty impressive!

Some cons, though:
1. The packaging never tells you this from the outside, but in order to hard-boil the eggs, you need to actually poke a hole at the top of each egg. I honestly feel like it takes more effort and stress to make sure I don't crack the eggs while doing this... versus just boiling eggs the old-fashioned way. But maybe it's just because I'm not used to it, yet?
2. The size is limiting. I mean I like that it's small in the sense that it doesn't take up too much counter space. But if I want to make more eggs, I can't... I'm limited to the space they have in the device. So it'd be more worth my time (in my opinion) to just use a pot or pan.

So... even though the number of pros outweigh the cons, for me personally, I'm just not sold on this product yet. Maybe it's because I haven't used it very much and am still used to cooking eggs the old-fashioned way... or maybe it's because I prefer to cook more in bulk than in small portions. Either way, it's honestly quite puzzling to me why so many people love this product so much...

title_review: Nice product, but requires a little finesse
text: This egg cooker works well, but it tends to undercook based on the water measurements on the cup. I usually fill well over the line for the level I want an egg cooked. I typically cook eggs outside of the shell, so the following is regarding that. For instance, at the soft line, the egg white was runny as well. So this doesn't make it a bad product, you just need to be smart about it. For a runny yolk I typically fill a couple millimeters over the Medium line. For a hard yolk I typically fill to the very brim of the cup. On the plus side, I have never ever had it make a discolored/green egg/yolk. Just be smart about it and this is an excellent product. Also one more thing, I will say, the timer is quite loud, so don't expect to be inconspicuous in your egg making.

title_review: Is this machine broken or is there secret tech?
text:
I bought this to make my life easier when making my lizard eggs for feeding time.

After trying to cook two and half batches of eggs, I still don't understand why they are coming out undercooked. And I don't mean they are coming out soft when I want medium, I mean they are coming out raw when I want medium.

For my first batch, I made sure to pierce the bottoms of all 6 eggs and place the holes at the top. I measured the water using the provided cup to the medium level, plugged it in, turned on the button and walked away. I noted that the manual said this would take about 12 min. Only 4 min later, the timer rang from the cooker. I tried to repeat the filling of the water and turning on to get it to continue cooking. It rang after another 4 min. I decided to trust it and crack open an egg. The white was still partially raw. I repeated it again and only got 1 perfectly cooked medium egg.

This occurred again for another 6 egg batch the next time I tried. Then again for a 3 egg batch. Now I'm uncertain if my eggs are faulty, the machine is faulty, or if I am not following instructions correctly. I even made sure to follow a video when trying the 2nd and 3rd time.

I will be returning this unit. Perhaps it was faulty, but I am disappointed with my experience and will simply resume the old pot on the stove method.

title_review: A gadget I can truly love
text:
I have no idea how long this little gadget will last, but until it dies I am going to enjoy it. My wife likes poached eggs, and I like an omelet. We both like our eggs done---no runny yolks. I pay no attention to what the little filler cup says about how much water to use. I just fill the measuring cup almost to the very top, and it is perfect for us. No mess. No fuss. Directions say spray the trays with a spray cooking oil before using, and I experimented and found it is not necessary. The finished eggs slide right out onto the plate. Clean up is minimal. I like that everything fits into the cooker, so storage is no problem. It is small enough to fit on the end of the counter. People have complained about the residue on the cooking unit, and that is true. It is mineral deposits left as the water evaporates. The first time I used it, I did not use filtered water, and it did leave a mineral deposit. The next time I used it, I used our faucet filter, and, problem solved. Other people have complained about the buzzer being too loud. We find it enjoyable. It isn't a constant buzz. It actually sounds like music in a way.

I have no idea how long this little guy is going to last, but until it gives up the ghost, we are going to enjoy our eggs. I highly recommend this egg cooker.

title_review: Plastic cooker makes plastic flavored poached eggs
text:
Part 1. Cooking disaster.
Poaching bowls: slightly too small for standard USDA Large. (How odd.) Since heat expands, the heat pushed just a few drops of egg white past the lip, overspilling onto the heating plate below. That eggwhite immediately scorched onto the heating plate, which then tripped the temperature sensor, which then halted the cooking cycle (as "complete") - leaving 2 raw eggs for me to enjoy.

Took apart the mess. Minutes of elbow grease and scrubbing later: tried again.
Result: poached eggs, with uncooked egg white, too - not appealing, nor safe.

Part 2. Eating disaster.
So I had these basically cooked eggs. I tasted the cooked part. Learned a difficult lesson. A cleaned, greased vessel of low-grade plastic makes poached eggs that taste like: plastic. And I was still tasting that plastic flavor several hours later. That actually made me mad - mad at myself, for being duped. After all, I microwave cook food in glass and ceramic bowls for health and flavor reasons, but hadn't even considered that steaming in an inferior grade plastic would so taint the food. Lesson learned: "yuck."

Part 3. Not everything was bad.
Also tried hard boiling method. That worked. Didn't like how this steamer, like most I guess, wants you to poke a hole in the egg shell. Skeptical about the safety of an open hole in the shell for keeping cooked eggs. But if you eat them quickly enough, I'm sure you might like them.

Epilogue.
Huge mess, scorched egg, difficult elbow grease, hard scrubbing, plastic flavored eggs - ouch - back into the box it went, grateful for easy returns.

Hope my candid experience helps you. As you can probably guess, I received no bonus nor gift to write this review. :-)

title_review: Do not order this egg cooker
text: First of all, I have a Oster egg cooker and never had any difficulty with it. But it is old and discolored so I wanted to replace it. The first thing you notice is that trays that come with this Rapid Egg Cooker (REC) are flimsy thin plastic. There is a warning that the poaching tray and the omelette bowl should not be placed directly on the heating plat. Fine. But neither sit well on the boiling tray. The first poached eggs I did were severely undercooked at the sound of the chimes. Second time, they were cooked, but wet from the water from the cover / lid. Having learned that the chimes did not signal when the eggs were done, I let the chiming eggs cook longer and they came out over-cooked. So the chimes are useless for determining when the eggs are cooked. When the chimes sound, the power button goes off. The chimes keep going until the unit is unplugged. But this screws up the reset. Next time the unit is plugged in, the power button goes on automatically. I have not done  boiled eggs yet because the directions are incomplete. I have learned from the Oster that the fewer eggs the more water need. The measuring up has marks: soft, medium, hard. It is as if two soft eggs take the same amount of water as six. Even the instructional video from Dash states that is not the case. You need more water for two eggs than for six. I must emphasize that I have used an egg cooker before, successfully. Dash's Rapid Egg Cooker is a mess. I will be sending it back.

Just bought this egg cooker, and immediately was disappointed:

My reliable old Krups egg cooker was cracked and shabby looking after many years, so decided to spend $20 on a new Dash. Gave it a try and realized that there's no way to turn off the alarm with the front button. You have to unplug the cooker to make it stop! I suppose this "feature" is there because of the lawyers, so you don't go and burn your house down and then blame Dash? So why even put a button on the front then? It's not necessary if you're using the plug as your switch. Pretty silly design.

I'll be going back to my ugly old Krups with a proper switch, and tossing the Dash in the garbage.

text:

text:
I’ve been using this for a few days now and I absolutely love it except for one thing: the cook times/water amounts marked on the cups appear to be measured for room temperature eggs. If you’re somewhere where eggs are safe to be kept outside the fridge this isn’t a problem, but in the US we have to keep them refrigerated which results in slightly undercooked eggs. It’s not hard to compensate for, you just need to either set the eggs out early to come up to room temp or add more water if they’re straight out of the fridge, but it would be nice if there were recommended amounts for the difference so I’m not guessing.

Otherwise I love it, it’s the perfect portion size for one person and works well once you get used to what I mentioned above. Very easy to assemble, clean, and use. You don’t need to set a timer because as soon as the water boils off it shuts itself down and plays a cute song to let you know your eggs are ready.

I’m using it to make breakfast in the morning, because I only have two brain cells when I wake up and they’re both fighting for third place. This makes cooking actual healthy food nice and brainless, which keeps me from reaching for the pop tarts.
