text:
I like hardboiled eggs but seldom cook them. Partly its because I have a habit of starting them cooking, leaving the room, and forgetting I have water boiling. Then I put the eggs in and I forget to take them out in time. Then I hate to have to clean the pot and store the eggs. I hate to do it in small batches because of all the hassle. I hate to do it in big batches because then I'm stuck eating eggs every day for a week.

You can do everything this little gizmo does easily by yourself. But this is effortless and you only have to clean it every month or so (depending on how much mineral there is in your water). Cook just 1 egg if that's all you want. It's fast and there's no cleanup and the eggs are perfect.

The alarm that rings when it gets done is a bit loud. And while the heating element supposedly shuts itself off eventually, that alarm just keeps ringing. I guess that's good since the eggs may keep cooking for a little bit just from residual heat if you don't pull the eggs out. But it's slightly annoying. Sign me up for the next version where an automated robot opens the lid for you to let cool air in when they are done.

No winding long cords anymore! This basically changes through a charging pad you connect the base to. I keep the pad plugged into the socket in my cleaning closet and just return the vacuum there whenever I’m done.

title_review: Worked so well on cat litter & fireplace soot - I bought 2!
text:
I bought this for picking up stray cat litter that lands on the floor (my girls kick the stuff around) after my last one died. It does the job great. Nothing falls back out and clean-up is a breeze.
I keep it in the cat room and use it daily.

If I only have one small issue it's that the sound is a little loud. But since I don't need to use it for long, this is not a deal breaker.

It worked so well on the litter, I thought I'd try it on the soot in my fireplace. I use Duraflame style logs and some of the stuff falls outside of the tray. This machine picks it up with no problem at all and no dust-up either. And with the attached extension nozzle I can reach tighter areas with ease. It worked so well I bought a second one to keep in the livingroom.

I read all of the reviews and became so confused that I almost gave up altogether. So glad I didn't. Don't know what others are looking for, but if you need power and good suction, I think you should give this product a shot.

text:
Friend of mine on a choir where I sing happened to remark on the hordes of small moths that seem to have descended on our fair city. Enjoying a kitchenful of them myself, I was interested when she remarked that she'd decimated the little pests with "moth traps." Never heard of such a thing, myself...so I came to Amazon and found this product. The package arrived late this afternoon. I promptly pulled out three traps and assembled them according to the simple instructions. Installed two of them in the pantry and one atop the fridge. Then went off to this evening's songfest.

By the time I got home, the traps had already collected five of the little critters. These things are "Indian meal moths"...I think they came in on some dog kibble.

Looks like the thing to do is to throw out all the flour, dog food, nuts, dried fruit, and assorted other moth food; wash all the containers, restock the pantry cabinet, and be sure to close every container with a tight lid. My plan is to catch as many of my flying roommates as this package will nab; then shovel the chow into the garbage, and then buy ANOTHER package of these traps, which can reside permanently in the food cupboard to discourage future visitations.

text:
A few years ago we had a moth infestation that was caused by a box of cereal from a discount store. We saw a moth here, a moth in front of the TV, one in front of the computer screen, etc. We were just about to start packing to move. To say this was like a horror show is not an exaggeration.

After seeing more and more moths i looked for the source, again. When i opened the cabinet it exploded with moths. Like bats fleeing caves in the movies. It took 2 months to get it under
control. We had to throw out tons of stuff because we hadnt known we had moths for a while before we started seeing them. They destroyed books, clothes. Nothing helped. I washed with vinegar and water every day. i washed, vacuumed, threw things out. Still moths! We tried everything Home Depot and anyone else had.

If not for this product i seriously think we would have had to leave almost everything we owned behind. This product is miraculous.

Moths come out at night. The females will go sit on the wall, up near the ceiling, giving off pheromones to attract the males. The males are usually the ones you see flying around. There are tons more males than females. Females lay eggs that look like small sawdust. Hundreds a day. they hatch into rice-like worms that eat clothes, grain, glued labels...anything. The grubs spin little webs, then hatch.

This product, unlike many others, has very impressive glue inside from edge to edge - not just a square inside. All 3 sides are glue. They aren't moving once they get in.

There's a blue strip inside the whole middle of the item - not just a little felt pad like others. This strip gives off phermones to attract the males and omg it's like Viagara and 3 beers for moths! Every 2 nights we'd throw the traps out and replace them because they were so full. it was GROSS but very interesting.

Its recommended to space the traps apart. We are using them currently because it's an old apartment with old pine trees right outside and the moths come in from the trees and the street lights.

I put a trap, using blue painter tape, near the ceilings and in the doorways. You can put them on a table or shelf but up high is best as that's where any females would be ( they arent attracted to the traps but die alone or with your assistance.

You want air and space between distances of the boxes so there's not a big area putting out phermones but "an" area the moth will be attracted to and go into. The traps have no smell.

The closet traps didnt work as well; the pantry traps caught *everything* including pantry moths. We had grain moths but now have these little gold buggers from outside. These will catch them all. You still need to find the source if youre infested and clean, wash, kill those eggs. You can spray lysol or (my favorite) Home Defense, another great, safe product.

These traps also catch the occasional centipede or spider which are attracted by the smell of a moth smorgasbord. they also catch gnats and fruit flies.

These are all you need. I can't recommend enough. A rare product that goes above and beyond what it promises!

title_review: Bought for the baby's butt, kept for every other use
text:
bought to try for cloth diapers, at the raving of many in a social media group about how much they love using flour sack towels. They seemed fine for that, but I much prefer a birdseye flat for texture and comfort against my baby's skin. These towels have still been amazing for having a baby around though, and I can't argue with the value! I keep a stack of a few of them in "the baby basket" in most rooms of my house, plus the remainder in the cleaning closet.
Spit-up emergency? Grab a towel
Wanna give that baby butt some air? Set him down for tummy time on a towel (because that will be the moment he pees)
Forgot to grab napkins before bringing your dinner out of the kitchen? This towel is now a giant napkin

Kitchen gets a refresh of these daily for drying hands, drying dishes, or mopping up minor spills, then wiping down from a quick sanitization at the end of the day. With a baby (especially one in part-time cloth diapers), there's lots of laundry going through, but there are still enough in this pack for all our cleaning and drying needs every day and only getting washed once a week or so. They are holding up well to this abuse so far!

For years, I've watched the commercial on TV advertising My Pillow. I just rolled my eyes and kind of groaned each time the commercial came on. I mean, a pillow is just a pillow, right?
WRONG!

This pillow is unbelievably comfortable. It washes/dries nicely as well .

All pillows are NOT the same! If you want a longer, more restful sleep, get yourself a My Pillow!

title_review: A wonderful and adjustable pillow design, although the loft/firmness selection process will frustrate some.
text:
Made in the USA! This is my third pillow from MyPillow. Obviously, I find the company compelling. It had first been recommended to me by a fellow insomniac with neck and back problems. That said, I've hit some cons along the way, especially when it comes to selecting your MyPillow. And I have tips for caring for it (it really does keep on keeping on when cared for properly). One thing I should say immediately is that the "firmness" of a MyPillow has more to do with the amount of loft than with what one typically thinks of as a "firm material," as you can move the stuffing around in such a way as to adjust firmness from there, and it will stay in place. This fact seems to be confounding some reviewers, understandably so.

I have a separate review up for the MyPillow Body Pillow, which is hands down the best (of three) body pillows I have ever had and something I am tempted to buy in bulk and hoard if I ever have the money, lol. I am under medical advisement to use a body pillow and simply never found another as hypoallergenic, lasting, etc. as this one. And the U-shaped ones left something to be desired in the neck area. I've been using it for about five years now. Unfortunately, the second pillow I purchased, for which I also paid full price, was a total non-fit for me. Based upon MyPillow literature, children and petite women side-sleepers who normally wear a size small (which was my size at the time) do best with the "yellow" pillows which are still offered in the MyPillow Premium line. Since I had recently had neck problems from a pillow with too high of a loft (so high that it could scarcely be stuffed into the pillow case), that made sense to me. Unfortunately, no matter how much my yellow pillow was fluffed, that thing was entirely too flat--drastically so. So I found the charts provided by MyPillow to be biased toward the very low end. Granted, it is tricky to recommend pillows based on body type, as we are more individual than that; for instance, my heavyset neighbor cannot stand a pillow that is any thicker than a doubled-up comforter).

A general tip regarding all MyPillows: Do NOT skip the step of running this pillow through the dryer for 15 minutes before first use. It is absolutely essential for developing the structure and loft of the pillow. In the pictures, you can see how small the pillow is upon arrival versus after running through the dryer. Secondly, fluff your pillow every morning. Really. It takes a few seconds, but it allows for the re-establishment of structure and loft without "thin spaces." For very ill persons using a body pillow this may be a little bit of an issue, so caregivers should pay attention to that. For teens who are apt to never take care of things, running their pillows through the dryer for 5-10 minutes once a week might suffice. But really fluffing should simply be a habit if using MyPillows--not to mention, it allows you to calibrate the pillow (within the boundaries of the loft abilities of the pillow you purchased) to your precise desires. For instance, I fluff the body pillow both directions to air it but then fluff all the material toward one end; that makes the center of the body pillow extra thick, which is perfect for me. Someone else might want to fluff their body pillow evenly all around to create a less thick center.

Anyhow, after losing money on that second pillow, the yellow coded one, you can imagine my delight when an opportunity to review this classic medium/firm pillow at a discounted price (in exchange for leaving an honest review) came to my attention. While happy with my current shredded latex pillow, it is in need of replacing, and my allergies and prior good experience with MyPillow made MyPillow the target company I had in mind for a replacement. (In regards to allergies, I love that MyPillows are machine washable and hypoallergenic even for someone like me whose multiple chemical sensitivities prohibit the use of memory foam pillows--even though memory foam is supposedly hypoallergenic.)

I rested on this pillow the first afternoon it arrived and was pleased with the comfort during that short rest. It is without a doubt lightyears better than the pillows you might buy at Walmart that will go flat in 1-2 years and that are apt to lose their support even during the night requiring refluffing (MyPillows hold their shape during the night). And while it is definitely not what I would call a firm pillow, one can bunch the stuffing toward corner and come up with a fantastically firm corner--too firm for me, I discovered (neck crick). So you can experiment with adjusting the stuffing in different ways with this pillow, and it will stay when you do so.

However, I have to say that I was disappointed in the amount of loft and also missed the bounciness of my shredded latex filling, especially when lying on it for the longer stretch of night. Since this is advertised as Medium/Firm, I take it that means this pillow represents the border between the "green" and "white" fillings of their premium line. Since as I previously mentioned, the actual firmness of MyPillows has somewhat more to do with loft and how you position the filling in your pillow than it does with what would typically be considered "firm material," I am guessing that what I really need is a "white" or "blue" premium series MyPillow pillow for a higher loft. I decided to take out my yellow pillow, which I never had an opportunity to return, to compare the two. Although my yellow pillow is a queen size rather than a king-sized pillow it otherwise has the features of the current my pillow premium line. It has the 2 inch gusset. I am guessing that this extra gusset makes all of the premium line pillows have more loft than the classic line. Whatever the case, The size was nearly identical. By lying on my back and switching them out back-and-forth and back-and-forth paying a lot of attention, I could tell there is the slightest difference in the amount of stuffing. But it was disheartening to see just how close my yellow pillow and my green/white pillow really were. I suspect that a green or white pillow in the premium line would feel different, but this is just getting too complicated. And unless I manage to nab another discounted review, I'm probably just not going to be able to afford trying out two more pillows in order to get the right one from this brand. I really wanted this brand to work for me and really expected it to work for me. I love their whole premise, and I think they have a very smart design using smart fill materials. I also know people for whom this brand has been a lifesaver – – where they got pillows for their entire family and couldn't be happier and never have to replace them. But I think they really need to rethink the loft of their classic line and increase the amount of fill a little bit per color code, since it seems that a lot of people do have complaints regarding the amount of loft and firmness versus what they've come to expect from a similarly labeled pillow. (I am assuming that the premium line tends to have a bit more loft per color code with its 2 inch gusset, but that is unclear. I am hoping they decide to spell that out better in their descriptions, as that might help me to estimate what premium pillow might work for me.)

All that said, I know that this pillow will be perfect for many people. Its adjustability means that there is a fairly wide range of people for whom it will be perfect. I would be happy to be handed such a pillow at a hotel or while someone's guest, as it is better than some of the alternatives one is typically granted. But with my neck and back problems, I am like the princess and the pea. I need a precise loft and a precise texture for the best maintenance of my neck. This all worked out perfectly for me in the MyPillow BodyPillow. But while I will continue to toy around with my Classic Medium/Firm pillow, it seems it will end up relegated to guest usage and around the house lounging rather than night sleeping. I wish I had a similar opportunity to try their "white" or "blue" premium series pillow (or possibly the "green" if the premium is a higher loft), as I suspect one of those could be my ideal pillow. But MyPillow head pillows keep me guessing in regards to what I should select. I am certainly a long ways away from the pillow that their literature had recommended for my size and sleeping style and still feel very little improvement in "fit."

For families who are looking to replace all their pillows, this brand is a really good one to try. One can get a whole series of pillows and try them all out and send half back for different sizes if necessary. If just one person is buying the pillow it can get a little more pricey sending things back. But I know from my experience with the body pillow and from my friends' experience with using these pillows for their family, that when you hit the right one it is magic. And for those who don't have lots of neck and back problems, they're probably going to automatically find any of these pillows to be a lot better than the ordinary pillows that they picked up at a local store.

title_review: Great Heater, But...Needs a Handle and Better Remote
text:
This heater is great for several reasons but also has a couple of significant drawbacks. I bought two, one for the downstairs and one for the upstairs. WHAT I LIKE ABOUT IT: 1) it oscillates 2) it can be set to turn off after an hour or more 3) It can be set with the desired temperature and will turn off and on during the night to keep the room at that temperature
WHAT I DON'T LIKE ABOUT IT: 1) It is very difficult to move. It REALLY needs a handle on the top. Sometimes I want to move it across the room, or move it over just a few inches, or carry it to another room. The only way to do this is wrap your arms around it to lift it. Not convenient at all. 2) the remote is pretty useless, you have to be no farther than 5 feet away from the heater, be directly in front of it, and be holding the remote about 1 1/2 feet from the ground, even then it doesn't always work. If I had it to do over, I would probably try to buy heaters that came with handles.

title_review: 1st unit bad, sent replacement also bad. 2 in a row same problem
text:
UPDATE 12/8/2015 received my replacement
My replacement arrived yesterday (12/7) and I was banned form using it at the office again so I waited until I got home to try it out. I opened the box and immediately noticed that burning plastic smell! the unit comes wrapped in plastic and you can still smell it.
I took it outside and ran a extension cord and plugged it in and started it. After a few seconds of running at MAX you can really smell the burning toxic odor even out side I let it run a few hours and it seemed to be clearing up a bit. Ran it in the house and you could still smell the odor but it was much less than it was when it first started and is almost gone after a few more hours running inside.
SO I will still not recommend this heater the chances I got a defective one the first time seemed acceptable but the second one they sent me still has the toxic odor problem, now keep in mind this is 2 units in a row that have this problem and the issue isnt isolated. So take a chance if you want too but I would advise that you take it outside and test it to make sure yours does not have this problem, the smell stays and lingers indoors for quite a while and is at the very least a very very unpleasant experience.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------.
(12/02/2015)
Ok I was really excited to get this, it arrived fast and I plugged it in and immediately noticed a horrible chemical smell. The smell was so bad I had to open all the windows in our office yesterday and today as I am writing this I can still smell it pretty strong!
It ran for 30 seconds and died lights went off and completely shut down. I unplugged it and waited for a few minutes and tried to restart it and it went on ran for 15 seconds and blew the circuit breaker in my office. In just this short amount of time the fumes coming out really polluted my office I cant imagine what it would be like if it ran for over and hour.

So I ordered a replacement today and I will give the heater another chance could have just gotten a bad one, will change my review if the new one works out and if it doesn't I will post my results.

title_review: Great product except for hot cord
text:
I really like the Lasko heater. Using in a basement that stays nice and cool in the summers, but very cold in winter. Had a smaller Vornado heater for years that worked great, very happy with this so far as a replacement.

This unit is very quiet, quieter than the last unit (which wasn't noisy by any means) and has features the small Vornado did not have. I don't bother with the remote, don't need it. Someone on a video review pointed out the handle is not really effective and I agree. If using the handle in the back you have to stabilize the unit by holding the front as well, otherwise you could easily drop it.

Basement room is 25x13 ft. Does not take long for this to heat it, but haven't had that many cold days or nights yet. Others have pointed out the cord gets hot. To be honest, I don't think I ever checked the cord on my last unit so don't know if it got hot or not. I only checked this cord because of comments I read here, and it does get hot after even an hour of use. I ran the Vornado for most of the day on colder winter days. The outlet is not loose (some have said that could be the problem with the cord getting hot), but the cord at the outlet gets warm enough that it does concern me. Otherwise I would have given this 5 stars. I tried connecting the unit instead to a more durable extension cord, the entire extension cord gets hot so that was not a good alternative. A good thing is that you can the set timer on the unit so it goes off automatically. I would highly recommend checking the cord occasionally and do as the directions say and unplug the unit when not in use. But I only need to run it during the day and early evening, turn it off before I go to bed at night.

The settings are great. Temperature control so the unit stops heating when the temperature gets 2 degrees above my setting, then starts up again. Oscillates which helps to evenly distribute heat throughout the room. Timer is a very nice feature in case I forget I left the unit on, my Vornado did not have a timer.

Heating the basement actually lowers my heating bill, I find I don't have to run my gas furnace as much (can keep the thermostat on the gas furnace lower). However, cost wise it probably evens out since it may increase my electric bill while lowering my gas bill, depending how long I run it each day. Will have to see how much my electricity usage increases this winter vs the Vornado. Have only had this a month so need a few months to see how it compares.

Visually a nice slim unit.

title_review: Absurd button controls, remote not great, tips easy
text:
[[VIDEOID:bfd529bd99bb7eeca18993cd5aa0f48f]] How on earth did a big successful company make such a ridiculous interface?

See video.

Bottom line, it does put out pretty good heat. It tips very easily if you bump it have kids or pets. Remember, towers have the heating units / fan in the center, not at the bottom. So the center of gravity is at the center of the tower, and there’s nothing in the base so it easily tips over. And there’s no point in having a tower versus a short heater because heat rises people! Also, never believe the marketing pictures… No tower has heat that comes out of the whole height of the tower. That is a lie. Look closely, that dark box in the middle of the towers, is where the fan and heat are. Not in the rest of it at all. Try it out at home yourself. So there is NO REASON FOR TOWERS except it’s a little easier to bend and touch the controls versus bending further down. Plus many of them have remotes versus the little guys don’t. Now Dreo, a main competitor, finally added a remote to their small square unit which is cheaper and puts out more heat as a matter of fact. Will switch to that!

Anyway, I’d like to ask Lasko how on earth the design team thought it was a good idea to force people to press down on their control buttons 9-10 TIMES JUST TO GET IT TO A NORMAL TEMP AND USE!!!?!?! EVERY TIME YOU USE IT!!! No, it does not remember your last setting!

1 Power On (defaults to MAX HEAT - WHYYY!?!)
2 Temp button - press 7 times to reach 70° - the average indoor temp in America is 68°-73°. Lasko why make it SO HARD TO GET THERE!?!
3 Osc button to make it oscillate, because who wouldn’t want that?
4 Time - press to set shutoff time to 1-4 hours, because who remembers to come back and turn the same off so your electric bill isn’t huge?

Then there’s the low and high fan issue. Your temperature settings only work for the high fan. Fair enough, most people would want a high fan. But should you want a low fan, it forces the temperature to maximum. What? If it’s a low fan, doesn’t it make sense you probably also want lower heat? Anyway, press the temp button to adjust the temperature at a low fan, and boom, it forces you back into Max temp only. Hm..what on earth…

Returning.

No way I’m putting up with this charade every single time I want to use the dang machine!

title_review: Poo-Pourri Before You Go Toilet Spray
text:
I was on a trip and discussing white elephant gifts with a friend and she told me about the time that everyone was literally "fighting" over this as one of the gifts. I ordered to try. First let me say that I do NOT received free or discounted products to review.
This bottle is relatively small. But then, 4 oz, as it clearly states is NOT very big. Be sure to read and compare with something you have in hand to be sure you understand sizing. I included a pic to help with a realistic view of the size.
The fragrance is mentholy... with a hint of citrus to me - not flowery... but that's just my opinion. I like the smell. The bottle says "essential oils" are used in making it and it is "Made in USA." The bottle notes up to 200 uses. You can be "refill" bottles. But honestly this product is a bit overpriced for me.
The first time I tried it, I used only 4 sprays (the bottle recommends 3-5) AND I forgot to "shake the bottle well" before each use. I found it didn't "tame" much of anything. :(
The second time I tried it I shook the bottle vigorously for a couple of seconds and used 5 sprays. It worked to about 99% in my opinion. Much better than the first try...
I give them 3 stars for the product (mostly because the cost is soooo high) and added a star for a "made in the USA" product. If they dropped the price to about $5-7 per bottle I would be a regular customer and might bump up to 5 stars. A large canister of lysol is less than $5 and works about as well ... in my opinion. And lysol disinfects.. but it is not exactly the same product use set, I know.
The product arrived quickly (I have prime) and in good condition.
I never hesitate to update my reviews if new information could be helpful, including how many "uses" I actually can achieve.

After he left the bathroom I asked him if he could smell anything. He was like "No. Why?"
I didn't answer.
Then he smiled and asked "Did you like poop before I walked in or something?" and I nodded. He was like "Oh you!! That's so awesome! I didn't even smell it. Did you use that potpourri stuff or something?"

I told him yes and that it was poo-pourri but I digress. This stuff is expensive. I have tried VIPoo trying to save some money and it works but has a very chemical, slightly unpleasant odor and can't handle diarrhea smells.

I've actually seen him puke while changing my sister's diaper when she had a stomach virus one time. Anyway everytime I used to go he used to say the whole house smelled like poop very passive-aggressively (even before the stomach surgery). Now that I use this, he never says anything and nobody that walks in after me has to know

text:
About this item: Poo~Pourri Before-You-Go Toilet Spray 2 Fl Oz Black Pepper Leather. Swagger never smelled so good! An alluring blend of wood, citrus and herbal notes that liberates the senses. LIES. Swagger, I think they mean stagger. It did libereate my senses. They tried to run the hell away. I couldn't see, it was hard to breathe and for some God awful reason I could TASTE IT. It was not alluring unless you have deep, deep seated problems.

This smells like great, great great Aunt Ethels funeral that was laid in her parlor in the dog days of August pre ac. It is a cloying stench. I was expexting a nice smell of leather with a bit of a pepper kick. I got old perfum bottles that shattered and were baked in and the smell won't go away. This was just because I opened it to smell and a drop got on the package. It will gag you strong. If you have bowl movements that you need this scent to cover up you need a Dr asap.

I really don't know how they confused this as smelling anything other than flea market Avon bottle floral. It smells like the old rose scented bath crap we all gave grandma in the 80's.

I love the original scent. I give these away for baby showers to use in diaper pails etc. They help keep trash cans smelling great. However the only one I have ever actually enjoyed is the Original. The others I had tried were not this bad but this one broke me. Good luck to anyone who uses this, you will need it. Or maybe get your sinuses fixed. I will still by PooPourri but I hhink they need new sniffers over there, stick to the original scent its a light fresh and won't make you want to move. And as I said it is excellent shower gift!

title_review: Poo-Pourri Lavender Vanilla is Absolutely Amazing!!!
text:
Absolutely amazing!!!! I wish I started using this years ago!!!! I've had Crohn's Disease now for 18 years and have tried just about every spray out there. I got married in 2005 and was always worried about the "smell" and the only thing that really worked for me was the Bath and Body Works bathroom fragrance sprays because that was the only spray that would even come close to help cover the smell.... or so I thought anyway.

I am in quite a few support groups for Crohn's Disease and for years there were people that kept recommending Poo-pourri for the odor. The main reason I didn't try this sooner was because for number one I don't like change and number two of course was the price. Well, for the last 10 years, I've been having to listen to my husband gag over the smell (he has a very weak stomach) and I'm not going to lie but my bowel movements definitely don't smell pretty lol. Even spraying the bathroom before, during and after each bowel movement, he would still gag even on the other side of the house. Well finally one afternoon in May 2016, my husband kept gagging and ended up vomiting over the bathroom smell (it's a really good thing we don't have kids lol), I finally decided to look on Amazon and order a bottle. I ordered the Poo-Pourri Lavender Vanilla 8oz bottle for $19.99.

OMG....it ACTUALLY WORKS!!!! I spray the water in the toilet bowl 3-4 times before I do my business and miraculously there is no more odor!!! I promise you that I'm not getting paid for posting my review and that this is my honest review of Poo-Pourri Lavender Vanilla!! My husband no longer gags or vomits whenever I use the bathroom!!!! Thank you Poo-Pourri for inventing an AMAZING product and thank you Amazon Prime for offering this amazing product!!!! I highly recommend purchasing and using this product. It has been the best money I have ever spent!!!

title_review: I do have three larger area rugs that my dogs and cats love to roll around on
text:
I purchased this carpet cleaner because while I do not have carpet throughout my home, I do have three larger area rugs that my dogs and cats love to roll around on. I vacuum regularly to reduce dander and pick up pet hair that accumulates, but I know that that isn't enough! This carpet cleaner did a great job and I was surprised at just how much dirt was lingering in my rugs. It is a lot smaller capacity than I expected and found myself having to dump out dirty water and refill the clean solution tank a few times per rug. This was a bit annoying, but as this is not a task that I will be doing every day, I can live with it.

One complaint that I have is in regards to cleaning lighter colored rugs. I noticed that in some areas, no matter how many different directions I cleaned in, there are some streaks that I cannot seem to get out. I was hoping that once the rug was thoroughly dried, this would go away, but unfortunately it just lessened.

Overall, I am happy with this purchase and find it to be much more economical than renting a carpet cleaner.

text: Quick warning this does not come with an upholstery attachment to clean your couch or cars or spot clean. But I love it! I have an expensive Hoover and I've had to replace the belt TWICE in 4 years on the Hoover. The belt broke again and I decided I would not replace the belt a 3rd time. The hoover also used a lot of water but didn't suck it back up so the carpets would be wet even with fans blowing on it. This review is basically me comparing this to the Hoover and let me tell you this little Bissell machine is light weight, its easy to use and so so so good! I was skeptic it only had one brush row because the hoover as 2 but this cleans so well. This Bissell machine blew my mind, its has really strong suction and it definitely is conservative when it comes to water usage and it sucks up really well. I used the sample size solution that came in the box and it contains Oxy so thats probably why my carpets look extra clean. I tried a different Bissell Pet solution and it didn't get them as clean. If you are going to clean your carpets just stick with the red labeled bottle Extra Strength Oxy solution. I am so happy with this tiny machine, and its not quiet by any means but its MUCH more quiet than the Hoover I used to own.

After one year they held up so well, without going flat I wanted to buy them again for my sons new bed. When I saw there were 40% off I was excited. When I unboxed them I don’t recall the last time them arriving rolled up right, deflated wrapped in plastic. I’m certain they didn’t arrive like this.
I compared them to the other ones, and the difference is clear. They look identical. Same fabric on the outside. Same tags and stated contents, but they are not the same. The new ones are poofy, but sink in almost all the way with very little support.
I would have returned them, but with the low price I’ll keep them as guest pillows.

text:
Since I recently upgraded my bedspread (which came with two king-size shams), I wanted two new king-size pillows for my bed. I’m one of these people who has tons of pillows on her bed (because I keep trying for that perfect sleeping pillow), so why not add more?

I’m pretty picky about bed pillows, and I liked the idea of these being a down-alternative, since I have allergies.

When I opened the package, they fluffed up right away and had no noticeable odor.

I was happily surprised that (for me) these are very comfortable sleeping pillows. Not too firm and are cooling for those of us who sleep “hot.” I’m a side sleeper, but don’t find my face getting lost in the pillow and it still retains enough cushion and elevation.

I often sit on my bed to read or watch TV and like an extra-firm pillow to lean against. This is NOT that pillow (for me)…but for sleeping, it’s great. I just put these pillows behind my firmer “leaning” pillows.

I highly recommend and would purchase again.

text:
I get nightly migraines and have trouble finding a pillow that works well for me. I can't tolerate memory foam and anything too hard causes head and ear pain. I also need something cooling and all those type pillows always seem to be memory foam and absurdly expensive. This pillow was advertised as cooling and comfortable so I figured I'd give it a shot since it wasn't that expensive.

When the box arrived, I was shocked at how heavy it was. The pillows are vacuum packed and tightly rolled. You have to carefully cut the sealed plastic and let them plump up for about an hour. They are surprisingly heavy pillows. They don't shift around at night at all unless you purposely move them. Do not expect these to be firm pillows. They are what I call 'poofy'. You lay your head on them and immediately sink into it. Initially I thought these pillows would be okay. The first few nights were fine and I slept well.

Unfortunately after giving them ten days, they got worse. They lost all poof entirely and my head sank completely to the bed. My ear actually hurt during the night and I had to toss around and try to plump the pillow up several times during the night. In addition, they are very hot pillows. They have no cooling at all and are actually hotter to sleep on then the original ordinary pillows I was replacing. I ended up returning them.

text:
I was so looking forward to these after reading the reviews. I have a miserable time sleeping due to vertebrae issues in my neck.

Yes, these are rolled tight and expand when opened. No smell. However (see pic) they are rolled by first being folded in half, then rolled from the middle to edge. Well, this is dumb. The first pillow i opened has a clear, solid gap inside along that fold-line. No amount of fluffing or kneading or punching has fixed it. It's as if each side of the pillow had a ball of Fluffy Stuff put in and where they meet in the middle they arent at all blended. I can actually feel.an empty channel there and can see it on the cover.

Also these are really thin. I layed on one and it compressed so much my head immediately tilted down from my neck on an angle towards my shoulder. to try to show this i took a pic lightly pushing down on one side with my hand. It compressed to the width of half of my eyeglasses. 3-4" inches I'd say. No support at all. Very soft as if mushy and fluffy.

Maybe if you took 2 and put them on top of each other I'd be ok but I'll just be adjusting and rearranging all night as they slide around. Will pass along to family members who have small kids who won't care.

Really wish I got the miraculous pillows i read the reviews about here but i didnt.

text:
7.2.21 another quick update. Absolutely love these pillows. I received the king size set and am once again just very pleased with everything about these pillows. So, so comfy!
Great buy!

Quick update 6.23.21
Amazing! I am still loving these pillows! I actually came back to get two more! The pillows are holding up well & do seem to be in the same condition as they were when I first received them a few months ago.

My review April 25, 2021
I’ve had the Queen size pillows a month now and I am pretty happy with them! I am very picky about my pillows and I sure have tried A LOT of them. I feel like I’ve always been on a quest, searching for the perfect pillow. Usually I feel much like Goldilocks (too soft, too hard...)
These pillows are soft, fluffy and “squishy.”
For me, they do offer the perfect amount of support & comfort, I also like that they don’t get bunched up at night.
It does feel like sleeping on fluffy cotton balls.
One pillow wouldn’t be enough for me and I use both of them, sort of made into a “V.”
I haven’t noticed them keeping me any cooler at night and I do sleep very hot.
The claim about the pillows keeping you cool was actually one of the main reasons I made the purchase.
Overall though, I would say, these pillows, so far have been my favorite.
I will try to remember to update if my opinion changes.

title_review: Heat Resistant Terry Pot Holders Give Good Control
text:
These excellent DII EVERYDAY KITCHEN BASIC TERRY POT HOLDERS (7” x 7", Set of 3; 100% Cotton, Machine Washable, Heat Resistant) are the ones I reach for when I have to pick up a hot dish, crock pot liner, or hot-handled pot. They are thin enough to give good control, and have a heat-resistant fabric on one side that affords decent insulation.

These potholders are not ideal for handling really, really hot items (e.g., broiler pans). For those, a neoprene-backed hot pad (e.g., [[ASIN:B00N3R8YKA DII Cotton and Neoprene Pot Holder]]) is better. However, you can always use two of these Basic Terry pot holders, if you need to handle really hot items.

text:
Pot holders are one of those kitchen accessories that is usually out of sight and mind and comes out briefly when handling hot pans. As I cook with cast iron a lot, I need them frequently. I was curious to see if these pot holders would be any good, and they seem to be very acceptable, especially at the price.

These come three in a set, cloth on one side and a semi-reflective material on the other. These work just fin when I have used them to lift my cast iron skillet by the handle, and they also do a decent job of serving as hot pads for placing hot pots and pans on without damaging the counter top. These lack any fancy design or artwork but they are very functional.

As I write this, the set goes for $8 for a three-pack. That’s quite reasonable.

So far, no complaints with these. Time will tell how long they will hold up, but so far I’m satisfied.

title_review: Got A Week Out Of It
text:
With my family, we are always on the go and canned vegetables are a necessity. We have an electric can opener but a new manual handheld is always great to have as a backup. To say that I’m sorely disappointed is an understatement.

This can opener feels like something you would buy in a dollar store. I was apprehensive about using it after feeling how cheap it felt. I was amazed that a brand like KitchenAid would produce something so incredibly flimsy and poorly made. My suspicions were proven to be true when after only one week of daily use - it came apart at the opener and cannot be put back together. It seems this needs a redesign with better quality materials used. The color is great but is worthless if it doesn’t work.

I wouldn’t recommend this can opener.

title_review: The negative reviews: a fact check...
text:
I really like these rugs in the runner size and have one in the hall, and another in the bedroom, at the base of the bed. For what you pay, you get tremendous value. Both are the burgundy color, and add a lot of color and warmth to my home.

Some facts:

- They do off-gas, and that's what folks complaining about the smell are talking about. Almost any rug that you buy with a non-slip backing or a glue binder will do this for a while after they've been opened. Carpet will also do this after it has been installed. It's definitely noticable for a day or two, and I recommend you try to keep it outside for a bit, opened and unrolled, if possible before bringing it in. I'm sure it's not healthy, but I have asthma and haven't been triggered by the runners, that I'm aware of.

- The folks upset about washing this: why are you putting a rug like this in a washer? If you have a very large front-loading drum washer, MAYBE. But it's not the manufacturer's fault it falls apart of you're using a top-loading washer, it's your own. Vacuuming and spot cleaning seems like enough, even for a high traffic hallway. I use a Roomba on it daily and it's holding up. I also have a cat and the hairballs are easy to clean with a little water, soap, and a rag.

- OK, so, the big thing I keep seeing is the colors are faded or inconsistent: and they're supposed to be. Folks, this is supposed to have a weathered vibe, it's part of the aesthetic and trend with this style. So, neither rug I bought is precisely identical even though they were purchased on the same date, same size, same color. The color is the same, but the fading is what's a little different. It's not extreme, not like part of it was exposed to the sun, while the rest wasn't; it's a style choice, look it up.

Because of the off-gassing, I would be hesitant to buy a very large rug from this brand unless it was summer and I could safely let this rest outside for a bit before bringing it in. But the brand is solid, you get great bang for your buck, and it's a hard recommend-you-buy from me. Four stars overall because these aren't the fanciest rugs in the world; but they're pretty dang good.

text:
My purchase of this stainless steel french press was the best purchase that I have ever made on Amazon. Not only is the product amazing, but the customer service of the manufacturing company is beyond comparison.
Looking first at the product, it's super durable, easy to clean, and makes the best coffee that I've ever had. I think my favorite part is that it keeps my coffee nice and hot until I want to pour myself a cup or two.
As I mentioned, it's really easy to clean, and that's because the parts are easily unscrewed from each other. Unfortunately, because of this I lost a little piece of it that helps the filter stay positioned before plunging it down to filter the coffee. Since I live with a bunch of pig roommates, I knew that that piece was gone for good in the mess. After propping the plunger up with various items while I was waiting for my the coffee to sit, I knew I needed to contact the company about getting a replacement piece since I loved my french press so much.
As soon as I was thinking of this, the company seemingly read my mind and sent me an email asking how I liked the product and if I needed any replacement parts. After telling them about my missing piece, they told me that they didn't have a replacement right now, but were able to send me a whole new French Press for FREE!
I can't say enough about the quality of this item, and the amazing customer service of the company. BUY this product, and you will not be disappointed!

title_review: FIVE STARS and TIP to keep your NEW and EXPENSIVE Mattress protected
text:
FIRST, I DOUBLE ENCASE a mattress and THEN put a stretchy (like fitted sheet) Mattress Cover on top of that, but well worth it. Helps with allergies and protects your mattress well!

ANY zipper can break, but if you double encase your mattress from the beginning (I don't use a box spring, I have a platform bed) and then cover with a MATTRESS COVER, all you ever have to do is wash the cover.

I had a zippered mattress cover I literally paid twice as much for and like this one more! Now, I don't know about how it would be regarding liquid or bed bugs. I got just to help keep dust mites out as I have allergies, hence DOUBLE encasement (this one and a different brand on top).

I got it just to cover my mattress to keep it clean, free of dust mites and to cover with soft thick mattress cover , so if you are getting this to keep liquid out, I can't say.

But love the texture and the fact it zips all around. Mattress covers that are elastic and just cover the top don't feel like they are really protecting all the mattress. I DO have one on top of this one, but I probably wouldn't need to.

I WOULD DEFINITELY get this again!

title_review: Good percolator for an excellent price
text:
For years I pondered buying a percolator because I remember when my grandmother use to use a percolator such as this to make coffee. To me coffee brewing in a percolator smells just heavenly. Even though I rarely drink straight coffee, preferring my beverage to be more of a coffee drink than just brewed coffee with milk and sugar, I finally decided to purchase this one since it was reasonably priced at $19.99 and because my boyfriend is a regular coffee drinker.

PROS:
- The basket insert has very small horizontal openings for the water to drain through. This means not many grinds fall into the brewed coffee. With a round disc coffee filter such as [[ASIN:B001M8K5TU Melitta U S A Inc 628354 White Disc Coffee Filter]], almost zero grinds fall in.

- The outside of the pot has a cup indicator so it's easy to measure the water. Four (5 oz.) cups of water is the minimum level; eight (5 oz.) cups is max.

- The lid fits snugly.

- The pot pours easily.

CONS:
- The basket sits on a spring and that part is very easy to lose down the drain or in the garbage. I'm afraid that one day I'm going to forget to remove it from the post before dumping the coffee grinds from the basket.

- I would have preferred a glass top instead of the pastic one supplied. Apparently a [[ASIN:B0007Y8MDG Clear glass percolator top, fits Farberware, etc.]] can be purchased for an additional $6. It would have been nice if this product came with a glass top for an extra $3 in cost.

- The major con for me is that there's about a tablespoon of water left in the pot after I hand wash it. Hand washing is recommended. The lip on the pot prevented me from dumping this small amount of water out so every time I wash this pot my drying towels get soaked.

text:
Call me crazy, but I purchased this because no other maker could authentically brew my favorite chicory blend. I've tried moka pots and conventional filter makers and all fall short.

For me the capacity, construction and ability to evenly heat are why I awarded this percolator five stars. It's everything a good percolator should be, including basket size and the bottom that is definitely designed for stove tops. This will also work on a grill for camping. If you object to the plastic viewing top you can remedy that by ordering this glass replacement: [[ASIN:B000QOM6KC Fitz-All Replacement Percolator Top, Small]], which is a perfect fit. Frankly, I do not see the need because this percolator makes excellent coffee out of the box.

It works best with a fairly coarse grind. You are better off grinding beans yourself, but as long as you avoid espresso grinds (both European and Cuban) or grinds specifically for drip makers you will be fine.

This pot is fairly easy to use if you have used them in the past. I grew up using percolators, which were the only game in town for nearly the first three decades of my life. The electric ones compensated for the proper heat, but these stove top models do require that you turn down the heat slightly after the percolating begins. It's not completely necessary, but if you want a perfect brew it's highly recommend. Cleaning is fairly easy - about on par with a french press regarding time and complexity. A key advantage, aside from the brewed coffee, is there are no filters to purchase.

I'll end with a recommendation for my fellow coffee lovers from the South: if you love coffee with chicory give [[ASIN:B0002LDAHC Cafe Du Monde]] a try. It's as though this percolator and that particular blend were made for each other.

text:
Like many people, I formerly used a Keurig, but the weird subliminal taste that was in Keurig coffee compelled me try something else; so I tried the Faberware percolator.

First, I want to say that the material of the percolator was very durable for me. It cleaned easily, and I did not have the issues of the glass knob shattering like so many other reviewers did.

However, the coffee was weak compared to the Keurig, and by a significant amount. It did not give me that ‘buzz’ I usually get when drinking coffee, and I was very disappointed by this, as I followed all of the instructions correctly. Additionally, when the coffee was brewing, it smelled horrible, and not the warm and invigorating smell that my Keurig used to produce. (It became such a problem that my family asked me to make my coffee after they were asleep, as the smell was that bad.) I also noticed some coffee beans in my coffee. I personally don’t have an issue with this, but I know others might.

I may be an outlier with this, as other reviewers say that the percolator produced some of the best coffee they have ever tasted, but it just didn’t for me. However, I gave three stars because I did appreciate the durability and reliability of the materials being used.

title_review: Not for just a cup of coffee, it'll make VERY weak coffee
text:
I just received it today. I had a high hope for this product because of high review rating, then disappointed.
Issue is about brewing small amount of coffee and not mentioned in other reviews but I suspect many reviews complaining about weak coffee is caused by this.
The problem is, it perks very inefficiently when the amount of water is small, like 12 oz. in my case. There's barely a perk pumping but most of the water is boiled away before it extracts any coffee from the beans. I tried it with larger amount of water(without coffee), about a quart, and it pumps a lot more hot water. Just for the curiosity, I poured hot water over spent grind, and sure enough, it came out as very dark brown water(as known as coffee).
I have a (electric)Polyperk I bought back in 1980's but the inner parts rusted unusable. When it was working, it made good coffee regardless of amount every time. I was expecting the same but apparently not, and there's no mention of it anywhere in Amazon, nor the manual came with it, nor in any reviews posted here.
How could anyone not find out until now that there's a minimum amount of coffee you can make with this? If it was mentioned in the manual or product description in amazon, I would definitely have avoided buying this.
Since I may use it for large amount of coffee in some occasions, I decided to keep it. You know returning is a pain?
I suggest anybody to try this with small amount then tell me if I did something wrong. I'll be humble to listen to you.

By the way, I didn't have a problem with the plastic dome itself like so many people reported, but the stainless seat was bent badly that I couldn't screw it back once I removed it because it was crooked. After I did some metal bending work, it screws in and out much easier but it's still not straight. Functionally good enough though. I would have had the same problem even if it came with a glass dome. It's not the plastic but the metal that bends so easily.

Overall quality is much better than I expected specially for the price.

I would recommend this if you brew coffee more than a few cups every time and skillful at bending metal.
I would not recommend this if you like to brew a cup of fresh coffee each time.

*update* (5-28-11)
I tried 6 cups(by marking inside the percolator, which is 1cup = 8oz.) of coffee and it was a great success. It pumps up the water much more efficiently. It makes very strong coffee(color & taste) if I use the same water:coffee ratio as I do with hand dripping method, which already uses much less coffee grind than automatic drip coffee maker. When they say percolator makes bitter coffee, they probably used too much coffee. It is strong but not bitter. I perked for 6 minutes but I feel it was just a waste of time. The color didn't change darker after 2 or 3 minutes. I'll work on the time and the amount of grind in the future, it definitely has a potential for better and more economical coffee, though my main method will still be hand dripping because of easier clean up.
By the way, I used grind made for auto drip coffee maker then filter the silt with home made cloth filter instead of paper filter. It works perfectly.

update(4-18-20)
I have not used this percolator because it requires more preparation and cleaning than the pour over method with Hario.
Then I got a induction cook top, part of my plan to replace all cookware for the flameless cooking with automatic turn offs.
One of my neighbors had a fire hazard and it made me afraid to use gas stoves.

This one,
https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B07VL32SFC/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o00_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1

And also, this set to goes with.
https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B078998999/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o02_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1

Induction stove works wonderful so far specially with the percolator. With the gas stove, I always had hard time adjusting the flame without the hadle getting too hot but with the induction cook top, the handle doesn't get even warm. It's like a magic.
It's like they are made for each other.
I brew 24 oz of coffee at a time and the amount of water is enough for it to start perking.
I'm still experimenting the temperature and the time.

title_review: Absolutely gorgeous but definitely not induction-compatible
text:
I took the advice of another reviewer who said this stainless steel coffee percolator works on her induction stove and bought it specifically for that purpose. Maybe it's a difference in the way the cookware sensors work on my Max Burton and her burner, but mine gives me a decided "no" and won't turn on. I was mightily disappointed, but I can't fault the product for it. Farberware does not claim this pot to be induction-ready.

It's really too bad. It's a gorgeous coffee pot, high-quality stainless steel, easy to clean, and very well designed. It perfectly fits the smaller eye of an electric stove. The only thing I don't like about it, and I knocked off one star because it's a serious design issue, is that the spring that the percolator basket sits on is not attached to the brew spindle. This makes it very easy to drop it or lose it. Farberware should take direction from Presto in this regard.

So I'm back to the plug-in Presto for perking coffee and will use this pot just for heating water on the stove. I really really really wanted this to be induction-ready! :(

text: I was worried this would be small for the about 20 oz. of coffee we drink in the morning;  no problem there though, gave it three cups of water which only barely brought it up into the amount of water you NEED to use this.  Trouble, to me, is that I need 6-1/2 tbsp of coffee to make our two large-ish cups of coffee each morning.  Plus, it takes about twice as long to make as a Mr Coffee.  Water has to come to boil, at high heat, then at first perk, turn it down to lowish-medium heat, (so as not to boil your coffee, a no-no!).  Then perk for 8 to 10 minutes.  And at the end of it all, you have coffee about the same as from Mr. Coffee.  The nice thing is, we can use this during a power failure.  But for everyday use, wasteful of coffee, and sorry to say, wasteful of time.  The materials, size, shape, (bottom fits just a teensy bit bigger than small coil on electric stove), handle, etc., are all excellent.  Love that it's stainless steel both outside and inside and including the tube and basket.  UPDATE 1-20-2020  I just tried using a strong magnet to see if it was drawn to this "stainless steel" coffee pot;  THE MAGNET DID NOT RESPOND AT ALL.  but googling  ... is stainless steel magnetic ... it appears that stainless steel with high level of "austenite" may not be magnetic.  So ... now to read up on "austenite."  (sigh)  ... well, reading up on austenite in steel, it's not a bad thing.  I use this coffee pot just about every day just to boil water ... so far (about a year) it has worked perfectly and has had no problems, no rust, no deformation.

text: We use nothing but cast iron pans, so we know how to use them and how to take care of them.I thought it would be great to have a griddle/grill to use right on our gas stove; especially the grill side. After some careful reading, I selected this pan. I am not terribly impressed with it. I know griddles are pretty flat, as I have a super old round cast iron griddle that has been used for pancakes, etc. However, I am not real comfortable with the low sides when using it as a grill. It is much too easy to get splatter and splash back from anything that is cooking down fat. That, and the two cut outs are more apt to expose the area to flame. Again, we use cast iron every single time we cook, but this is just sitting in a drawer. I think I will look for a grill only item. Overall, I think it is an OK product as a griddle, and slightly less so as a grill.  And yes, everything stuck to it despite having plenty of oil. Further seasoning should enhance the performance, but this was annoying. I find that although using cast iron on a gas range is awesome, I will just use a large skillet, or even get out my electric skillet rather than use this item.

text:
This is one of the best purchases I ever made. This is an extremely high-quality piece of kitchen equipment. One side is a griddle, smooth and without ridges, and the other side is a grill, with the necessary ridges. My husband and I use this to cook vegetarian and non-vegetarian food. It is terrific for grilling onions, mushrooms or mixed vegetables. It works well for pancakes, eggs--just about anything you can imagine. We've gotten quite creative with it.

For cleaning, I let it cool down, then wipe it down well with a paper towel and olive oil. For a while we scrubbed it in the kitchen sink in a pan of soapy water, but we decided it wasn't worth all that trouble. The griddle made pot marks all over the sink; the water caused the cast iron to rust, and we just had to wipe it down with oil anyway to "season" it.

Note: Because this is iron, it will leach iron into whatever you cook on it. For men and for women past menopause, using it on a daily basis can cause you to ingest too much iron in your diet. For pre-menopausal women, however, it is a great source of dietary iron if you choose to use this daily. It's also a useful source of iron for vegetarians, who get less in their diet than meat-eaters.

This makes a terrific gift for anyone you know who likes to cook.

text:
When I received my Lodge grill/griddle a few days ago, I was stunned with how just plain beautiful it is. It is going to sit on my stove all the time, across the burners on one side, probably with the grilling side up to remind me that I can grill anything any time I want to.

I've never had a double-burner grill before, so I've experimented with turning on one or both burners; setting the burners on different settings; and cooking foods one normally would not cook on a grill on the grill side (eggs this morning, along with the bacon).

There is no better way to get the hang of cast iron cooking than to cook eggs. If you've got the seasoning right and the temperature right, you've got the best non-stick egg-cooking surface in the world. If you don't have it right and the eggs stick, just scour the pan with one of those dark green pot-scrubber pads (no soap!), rinse well, rub in some oil with your fingers or a napkin, and try again. If you don't cook something very acidic like tomato sauce in/on your cast iron, it will get so splendidly non-stick you will think you died and went to heaven.

I used my eggs-on-the-grill experiment to get a feel for the best temperature for the piece with only one burner on. The first time I did it, the eggs hardly stuck at all...so that's a great testament to the pre-seasoning.

What's nice is that, even when using only one burner, the entire piece heats up, so when you've finished cooking something on the side with the hot burner, you can move it over to the other side (the one with the burner off) and the food stays beautifully warm while you cook something else. I haven't tried pancakes on the griddle side yet (because I'm in the early stages of Atkins' diet), but I can tell this would be super for cooking up stacks of nice, warm, perfectly cooked pancakes.

When I first got it, it did smoke a good bit; I think this is because I had the heat too high...or maybe it just needed to smoke a little to settle it down. It's not smoking now.

I know this is a rambling review...I really just wanted to say this is a beautiful piece and I'm very happy to have it in my kitchen.

text:
At first I was skeptical about all the positive reviews about this product but was in need of a better way to cook certain foods. My kids love chicken teriyaki and it wasn't turning out so good on my regular saute pan. I've seen it in action at my relative's house and she seemed to really like using it. After reading some reviews on how to clean and care for the pan and using it a few times, I'm in love with it. The results are wonderful and the lack of sticking is what surprised me.
My first use was great because it came pre-seasoned. My second time, some sauce scorched and and food stuck on the pan. I was getting nervous because it looked like cleaning was going to be torture. I soaked it in water and used a plastic bristle brush to clean the burned sauce. The 3rd time I took my grill pan out and looked at the surface, some of the sheen was lost so I used a little cooking oil while it was heating up and took a paper towel to spread a very thin layer in the dulled area. That worked great to keep the surface working like I first bought it. After I finished cooking, I took a plastic pan scraper to clean up as much as possible. Then my sink cleaning time was so short! In about five minutes all the sauce washed off and my pan was back on top of the stove to dry.
I've been drying my pan by heating it up a bit on the stove as I read in other reviews. Today I took a look at it and the unseasoned area is smaller. Perhaps I scrapped off the seasoning from my first use but rubbing a little oil in and making adjustments here and there has made this a great cooking tool. It has a bit of a learning curve but reading some of the tips from other reviewers has made this process a little easier.

title_review: A tool that does a job and does it well. The expert design is very apparent.
text:
[[VIDEOID:e2bd4c31e0dd8a818a2cb431328e6d4]]This spiralizer is the best tool I have in the kitchen to aid in my low-carb, high fat, moderate protein diet. As you can see in the video I uploaded it is very easy to use and it only takes minutes to process 2 or 3 zucchini for enough noodles for a couple of people to have a healthy "pasta" dish. The different blades are useful. I tend to use the spaghetti noodle blade the most. The simple straight blade can be used to make spiraled wide thin pieces. Broken up a bit, these pieces are great for a lasagna dish.

This spiralizer will cut even the most fibrous of roots. I have it cutting ginger and daikon no problem.

Despite the complexity of getting one contraption to make these noodles everything is still pretty easy to clean. The machine was well designed with cleaning in mind. It was also developed with sanitation in mind. The lip where the noodles come out is built to overhang a small bowl or a plate/cutting board. It is perfect for catching all of the noodles after you have processed.

Dimensions of the product can be seen in the photos.

Included in this set:
*Spiralizer Body
*Spaghetti blade
*Fettuccine blade
*Wide thin spiral slice blade

Pros:
*Easy to use
*Easy to clean
*Designed to keep things sanitary

Cons:
*None

Additional Considerations:
Some quality kitchen shears are nice when using this product. After you process a whole zucchini for noodles you can gather up the noodles like rope and then once you have it all bunched up uniformly you can make cuts to get consistent noodle length.

Overall: 5/5 stars (>=.5 rounds up, <.5 rounds down) => 5 stars
